state:
MERIDIAN DISTRICT RECREATIONAL FLOORBALL & NETBALL ASSOCIATION (MDRFNA)
INTERNAL INCIDENT REPORT IR-2024-117

Subject: Scheduling platform migration failure, fee irregularities, and related matters
Classification: Internal — Distribution List A only
Prepared by: Wanjiru Lindqvist, Honorary Registrar
Reviewed by: Priya Tanaka (Treasurer); Yara Moreau (Fixtures Secretary)
Date of issue: 14 December 2024
Supersedes: none
Retention: 7 years per Records Schedule 12

DISTRIBUTION AND PURPOSE

This report is issued pursuant to Standing Order 4(b) of the Association's Governance Manual, which requires the Registrar to "prepare a consolidated written account of any operational irregularity affecting three (3) or more registered fixtures within a single competition month, for the information of the Executive Committee and for retention in the permanent record." The irregularities described herein arose in connection with the Association's migration of its fixture scheduling, registration and fee-collection functions from the legacy Foxglove Software system ("FGL-League") to the Harbor Software platform ("ScheduleMaster"), together with certain ancillary matters touching on venue management, disciplinary process and equipment rental. The report makes findings of fact only; recommendations appear at Section 8 and do not constitute decisions of the Executive Committee.

SECTION 1. BACKGROUND AND HISTORY

1.1 The Association administers amateur floorball and netball competition for twenty-two (22) registered teams across three divisions, plus a mixed winter social league. Fixture scheduling has, since 2016, been maintained on the Foxglove Software product FGL-League, procured under a licence agreement dated 3 February 2016 (as amended twice, most recently 11 January 2022). Fees, fines and registration payments were recorded in the same system and reconciled monthly by the Treasurer against the association's bank statements.

1.2 During the 2023 close season, the Executive Committee resolved (Minute EC-2023-44) that the Association would "investigate replacement of FGL-League with a modern cloud platform, cost to be capped at the amount provided for in the 2024 budget line 6.2." Three vendors were approached: Harbor Software, Northwind Studio (which quoted for a custom build in partnership with a third-party hosting provider), and Foxglove Software (which offered an upgraded version of the incumbent product). Northwind Studio subsequently withdrew its quotation by letter of 8 September 2023, citing "capacity constraints in the current quarter." Foxglove Software's upgraded quotation exceeded budget line 6.2 by 34 percent and was not pursued further, a fact recorded in the Treasurer's note of 2 October 2023.

1.3 On 15 November 2023 the Association entered into a Software as a Service Agreement with Harbor Software for the ScheduleMaster platform, including the Fixtures Module, the Registration Module, the Fees and Billing Module, and the Notifications Module, together with a maintenance and support contract running for an initial term of twenty-four (24) months from the go-live date. The go-live date was fixed contractually as 1 August 2024. The migration of historical data was subcontracted by Harbor Software to a data-conversion bureau whose identity is not disclosed in the agreement.

1.4 The migration proceeded during July 2024. The Registrar's contemporaneous migration diary records, among other entries: "9 July: fixture list for Div 1 imported. 11 July: Div 2 imported, duplicate venue rows noticed, queried with support. 15 July: Div 3 and social league imported. 19 July: registration database imported; photographs missing; queried. 24 July: fees ledger imported; opening balances spot-checked against June reconciliation; three discrepancies noted, list attached. 29 July: final checks; Northwind Studios' old logo still appearing on printed sheets; cosmetic only. 1 August: live."

1.5 It should be noted for completeness that the Northwind Studio logo appearing on printed fixture sheets was a legacy artefact of the Association's former web design contract with Northwind Studio (2019-2022), and has no connection with the scheduling migration. The logo artefact is documented in bug report HAR-4402 (see Section 5) and is a display issue only.

SECTION 2. RELEVANT RULES AND STANDING ORDERS (EXTRACTS)

2.1 Competition Rule 14 (Fixtures): "The Fixtures Secretary shall publish the fixture list for each division not later than twenty-one (21) days before the first fixture of the season. A fixture may only be postponed or rescheduled with the approval of the Fixtures Secretary, and notice of the revised date shall be published to all affected teams. A fixture which is not commenced for reasons within the control of one team shall be recorded as a forfeit against that team."

2.2 Competition Rule 19 (Rosters and Eligibility): "No player shall appear for a team after the roster freeze date. The roster freeze date for the 2024-25 season is 30 September 2024. Any fixture in which an ineligible player appears shall, upon protest or upon the Registrar's own motion, be recorded as a 5-0 forfeit against the fielding team, subject to appeal."

2.3 Disciplinary Regulation 7.2 (Appeals): "A party wishing to appeal a decision of the Registrar or of a match official shall lodge a written notice of appeal with the Registrar within seven (7) days of the decision, accompanied by the appeal filing fee of $40. An appeal lodged without the filing fee is not validly commenced and shall not be listed for hearing. The appeal filing fee is refunded if the appeal is upheld."

2.4 Disciplinary Regulation 7.4 (Hearing): "The Appeals Panel shall convene within twenty-one (21) days of a validly commenced appeal and shall notify the parties of its decision in writing within seven (7) days of the hearing."

2.5 Standing Order 11 (Venue Bookings): "Venue bookings shall be made through the venue management function of the approved platform. Where two fixtures are allocated to the same venue and time slot, the Fixtures Secretary shall resolve the conflict in favour of the earlier-published fixture and shall reschedule the other fixture with the approval procedure in Rule 14."

2.6 Standing Order 11A (Equipment): "Match equipment supplied under rental arrangements with third parties shall be checked in and checked out by the venue marshal, and any shortage shall be reported to the supplier within 48 hours of the fixture."

SECTION 3. CONSOLIDATED TIMELINE OF EVENTS (AUGUST — DECEMBER 2024)

3.1 3 August 2024. First competitive Saturday of the season. Fixtures published in ScheduleMaster. The Fixtures Secretary notes in her Saturday report that the printed sheet for Division 1 listed the 3 August fixture between Riverside Rockets and Southbank Squalls at "Court 4, Riverside Leisure Centre" while the on-screen schedule showed "Court 4, Riverside Leisure Centre" for a Division 2 fixture between Kingsmere Kestrels and Old Toll Rovers at the same time. The venue marshal at Riverside Leisure Centre telephoned at 09:40 to report that two teams had arrived for Court 4.

3.2 3 August 2024 (later). The Div 2 fixture was stood down and the teams sent home. The Div 1 fixture proceeded. Yara Moreau logged the incident with Harbor Software support as ticket #HAR-4471 (see Section 5) and, separately, recorded a postponement of the Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers fixture "pending rescheduling, date TBC."

3.3 10 August 2024. A second venue conflict occurred at Marsh Basin Sports Hall, where the social league fixture of 10 August was double-booked against a private booking made by Northwind Rentals for a corporate netball event. Northwind Rentals held the confirmed booking; the social league fixture was stood down. The venue marshal's incident slip states: "hall occupied by rental group, boards and posts in use, our slot apparently never confirmed with hall management." Whether the Association's booking was ever validly entered into the hall's own booking system is not established by any document held by the Registrar.

3.4 17 August 2024. The Treasurer, Priya Tanaka, performed the routine monthly reconciliation of the fees ledger in ScheduleMaster against the August bank statement. Her working paper (Appendix A summary) records, among other items, that registration fees received for the Southbank Squalls appeared as $620 in the platform ledger while the bank statement showed a single credit of $590 on 6 August; and that three teams' junior-concession rates had not been applied, so that those teams had been invoiced at the full adult rate. A credit note was raised for the overcharge on the junior concessions on 21 August. The $620/$590 discrepancy was carried as an open query with Harbor Software support (ticket #HAR-4503).

3.5 24 August 2024. The Fixtures Secretary rescheduled the Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers fixture to 31 August, which was published and played without incident. The social league fixture of 10 August was not rescheduled in August; correspondence regarding it appears at Section 6.

3.6 7 September 2024. Roster freeze date under Rule 19. The Registrar's roster freeze instruction, sent to Harbor Software support on 4 September, asked that the Registration Module be configured so that "no player registrations be accepted after 30 September." The support reply of 5 September confirmed the request was "logged as a configuration task for the current sprint." There is no record in the Registrar's files of any subsequent confirmation from Harbor Software that the configuration task was completed.

3.7 14 September 2024. Division 2 fixture: Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers (the rescheduled one). Played at Marsh Basin. During the match, a player listed on the Kestrels' team sheet was challenged by the opposing captain on eligibility grounds. The player had been registered, according to the Registration Module's own audit display, on 4 October 2024 — a date after the roster freeze — although the team sheet was prepared and the match played on 14 September. The apparent inconsistency in the audit display is the subject of bug report #HAR-4512 (Section 5). The match was played to a conclusion (2-2) and the eligibility protest was referred to the Registrar.

3.8 21 September 2024. The Registrar, applying Rule 19, recorded the 14 September fixture as a 5-0 forfeit against Kingsmere Kestrels, the ineligible player having appeared. Written notice of the forfeit decision was sent to both clubs on 23 September. The Kestrels' coach, Farid Haddad, notified the Registrar by telephone on 25 September that the club intended to appeal.

3.9 30 September 2024. The Registrar received by email a written notice of appeal from Farid Haddad, styled "Notice of Appeal against Forfeit Decision of 21 September." The notice of appeal is dated 28 September 2024, sets out grounds in four numbered paragraphs, and requests a hearing before the Appeals Panel. The notice makes no mention of any payment. The Association's published guidance accompanying the appeal form states that the $40 appeal filing fee must accompany the notice; the guidance also notes that appeals may be paid "by bank transfer to the Association's general account, by cheque to the Registrar, or in cash at the pavilion office against a numbered receipt."

3.10 4 October 2024. Registrar's office diary entry: "Farid Haddad appeal — file opened, appeal number AP-24/09. Panel to be convened within 21 days per Reg 7.4 — query whether fee received — asked Priya to check bank statements — she will look when back from leave." There is no subsequent diary entry, bank annotation, receipt stub, ledger line or email in the Association's files showing payment of the appeal filing fee for appeal AP-24/09.

3.11 12 October 2024. Division 1 fixture: Riverside Rockets v Southbank Squalls, Riverside Leisure Centre. The Squalls' captain, Aiden Kaur, submitted a team sheet listing fourteen players; the platform accepted the sheet but the Notifications Module did not send the usual confirmation email to the Registrar's office. This failure is within the known-issue category described in the Harbor Software changelog entry for version 4.1.0 (Section 4) and was reported by the Registrar's office as ticket #HAR-4488.

3.12 19 October 2024. The social league fixture of 10 August was formally recorded by the Fixtures Secretary as "abandoned, not to be replayed," with the entry annotated "per email agreement of 17-19 Oct, see Section 6." The email chain at Section 6 contains proposals and counter-proposals for a replay on 26 October and on 2 November; the chain does not contain any message recording agreement to either date or to the abandonment. The annotation's provenance could not be verified from the correspondence held on file, and the Fixtures Secretary, when asked by the Registrar on 2 December, replied: "I honestly can't reconstruct that entry; it may have come from the old Foxglove habit of auto-closing stale postponed fixtures after 70 days. Can we treat it as a system artefact for now?"

3.13 26 October 2024. Notification from Northwind Rentals to the Association of a claim for unpaid equipment rental in respect of boards and posts supplied for the 3 August and 10 August fixtures at Riverside Leisure Centre and Marsh Basin Sports Hall respectively, in the amount of $310, together with storage charges of $55. The Association's venue marshal's check-out slips for both dates are incomplete: the 3 August slip is signed but records no board count; the 10 August slip is missing entirely because the fixture was stood down.

3.14 9 November 2024. A Division 3 fixture between Old Toll Rovers II and Marsh Basin Mallards at Marsh Basin Sports Hall was abandoned at half-time owing to a floor fault in the south court (a water ingress issue at the venue, unrelated to scheduling software). The score at abandonment was 1-1. Competition Rule 14 does not address mid-fixture abandonment; the Registrar sought the Executive Committee's guidance. The Executive Committee resolved on 13 November (Minute EC-2024-31) that "the abandoned Division 3 fixture of 9 November be replayed at a date to be fixed by the Fixtures Secretary, with the score expunged, venue to be arranged."

3.15 Following the 13 November resolution, the Fixtures Secretary circulated availability inquiries to both clubs. The correspondence is summarised at Section 6.4. As at the date of this report, the fixture remains listed in ScheduleMaster as "REPLAY — DATE TO BE CONFIRMED," and the Registrar's fixture register records the status of that fixture as "replay ordered, date outstanding."

3.16 1 December 2024. Northwind Rentals issued a formal letter before action and, on 5 December, filed a claim in the Small Claims Division of the Local Court against the Association. The filing is summarised at Section 7. The Association's solicitor has been instructed to acknowledge the claim.

SECTION 4. SOFTWARE CHANGELOG EXTRACT (HARBOR SOFTWARE, SCHEDULEMASTER)

The following entries are reproduced verbatim from Harbor Software's public release notes for the Fixtures, Registration and Notifications Modules, as published on the vendor's customer portal. The Registrar downloaded the extract on 6 December 2024. The extract is included here because several of the incidents in Section 3 are traceable to documented platform behaviour.

Version 4.0.9 (released 21 June 2024)
- General stability improvements to the Fixtures Module import pipeline.
- Fixed an issue where imported fixture lists retained the "printed header" image configured in a customer's previous system, causing stale third-party branding on printed sheets. (Ref: customer report HAR-4402.)
- Updated the venue picker to display court numbers in ascending order.

Version 4.1.0 (released 19 July 2024)
- NEW: Venue conflict pre-check at import time. The pre-check compares newly imported fixtures against existing venue bookings within the customer's own ScheduleMaster environment and warns where a conflict is detected. NOTE: the pre-check does not currently compare against bookings held in external venue management systems operated by halls or leisure centres. Cross-system venue booking remains the customer's responsibility.
- KNOWN ISSUE: transactional notification emails (fixture confirmations, team-sheet confirmations, fee receipts) may fail to send when the sending queue reaches more than 500 messages per day. Customers operating large weekend fixture lists may see intermittent non-delivery. Workaround: verify receipt in the audit log. Fix targeted for a later release.
- Improved accessibility of the fees dashboard.

Version 4.1.1 (released 6 September 2024)
- Fixed a rounding error in the Fees and Billing Module that caused junior concession rates to be skipped when a team's registration contained a mixture of adult and junior players, resulting in overcharge at the full adult rate for the junior portion. (Ref: customer report HAR-4503.) Customers who identified affected invoices should issue credit notes manually from the reconciliation screen.
- Fixed a display bug in the Registration Module audit view. Previously, the audit view displayed the "registration accepted" timestamp instead of the "registration submitted" timestamp, which could make validly registered players appear to have been registered after a freeze date. (Ref: customer report HAR-4512.) Note for administrators: this release corrects the display only; it does not retroactively alter any eligibility determination made on the basis of the incorrect display.
- Maintenance release: no new features.

Version 4.1.2 (released 11 October 2024)
- The transactional notification email queue has been re-architected to remove the daily cap described under version 4.1.0. Notification reliability is restored. Customers who relied on the audit-log workaround during the affected period need take no further action.
- Fixed an issue where postponed fixtures auto-closed as "abandoned, not to be replayed" after 70 days of inactivity when migrated from a legacy system whose status vocabulary included a "pending rescheduling, date TBC" state. Migrated fixtures in that state at import time are now mapped to "postponed, rescheduling required" and will not auto-close. Customers whose fixtures were auto-closed between 1 August and the date of this release may reopen them from the fixture history screen. (Ref: internal audit; first reported by a customer on 21 October.)
- The venue conflict pre-check now supports manual entry of external bookings as reference-only records.

Version 4.1.3 (released 29 November 2024)
- Patch release addressing a regression in the printed fixture sheet generator introduced in 4.1.2 (sheet headers could display the previous season's division label). No change to fixture data.
- Documentation update clarifying that the Fees and Billing Module does not record payments received outside the platform (cash, cheque); such payments must be entered manually by an administrator against the ledger. The Registrar's attention is drawn to this clarification in connection with cash receipts at the pavilion office.

SECTION 5. BUG REPORTS AND SUPPORT TICKETS (SUMMARY OF RECORDS HELD)

Ticket #HAR-4402 — Reported 29 July 2024 by Registrar's office.
Summary: printed fixture sheets display Northwind Studio logo from the Association's former website arrangement; cosmetic.
Status: closed as fixed in 4.0.9.
Note: unrelated to the 2024 migration; the logo artefact came from an old print template.

Ticket #HAR-4471 — Reported 3 August 2024 by Yara Moreau (Fixtures Secretary).
Summary: two fixtures allocated to Court 4, Riverside Leisure Centre, at the same Saturday morning slot following data migration. Affected fixture: Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers (Div 2), stood down on the day.
Vendor response (5 August): "The import pre-check flagged no conflict because both bookings were created inside the same migration batch. We have added the batch case to the pre-check backlog. Recommend manual venue review for the first three weeks of your season."
Status at date of report: open (vendor backlog). Not fixed by 4.1.2; the changelog entries in 4.1.2 address the notification queue and the auto-close behaviour, not batched import conflicts.

Ticket #HAR-4488 — Reported 12 October 2024 by Registrar's office.
Summary: team-sheet confirmation emails not delivered; Registrar's office only became aware of the Squalls' team sheet when the marshal phoned. Attribution: the version 4.1.0 daily queue cap known issue.
Status: closed as fixed by 4.1.2; workaround audit-log entries confirmed the sheet had been submitted on time. No fixture consequence.

Ticket #HAR-4503 — Reported 21 August 2024 by Priya Tanaka (Treasurer).
Summary: fees ledger discrepancies; junior concession rates skipped on mixed rosters (overcharge); also a $620 ledger entry against a $590 bank credit for Southbank Squalls registration, cause unknown.
Vendor response (30 August): concession bug confirmed and fixed in 4.1.1; "on the $620 vs $590, we cannot reproduce; the ledger shows a $30 platform convenience fee applied to the invoice. Please confirm whether your agreement includes the convenience fee."
Treasurer's note (2 September): "I have checked the SaaS agreement; it is silent on convenience fees. I have asked Harbor in writing to point to the clause. No reply yet. The $30 is still on the open queries list."
Status at date of report: partially closed; $30 discrepancy remains open; credit notes for the overcharge were issued manually on 21 August 2024.

Ticket #HAR-4512 — Reported 15 September 2024 by Kingsmere Kestrels (through the Registrar's office).
Summary: Registration Module audit view displayed "4 October 2024" as the effective registration date of a player whose team sheet was used on 14 September, causing an eligibility challenge. The display bug (4.1.1) explains the audit display; the underlying registration record, per the module's raw data export of 16 September, shows a submitted date of 12 September 2024, before the roster freeze.
Status: closed as fixed in 4.1.1, with the vendor's administrator note that the display fix does not retroactively alter eligibility determinations. The Registrar's forfeit decision of 21 September (Section 3.8) was made on the basis of the audit display; the raw data export post-dates the decision.

SECTION 6. CORRESPONDENCE EXTRACTS

6.1 Rescheduling of the 10 August social league fixture (extract).

From: Yara Moreau (Fixtures Secretary) — 12 Aug: "All — after Saturday's clash at Marsh Basin we need to find a slot for the social fixture. I can offer 26 October or 2 November, both afternoons, court 2 at the Basin. Preference to the first team to confirm."
Leila Alvarez (captain, Marsh Basin Mallards social side) — 13 Aug: "We can do 26 Oct if it's the afternoon. What about our booked referee fee — does it carry over?"
Yara Moreau — 13 Aug: "Referee fees carry over, yes. I'll pencil 26 Oct pending the other side."
Aiden Kaur (captain, Old Toll Rovers social side) — 14 Aug: "26 Oct is tricky for us, half the team are away for the half-marathon. Is 2 Nov still on the table?"
Yara Moreau — 14 Aug: "2 Nov is possible, I'd need to check the hall. Leave it with me."
No further message appears in the chain until 19 October, when Yara Moreau wrote to both captains: "Following the auto-closure of this fixture in the platform (see below), and given the lateness of the season, I propose we record the social fixture of 10 August as abandoned, not replayed, and move on. Shout if you disagree by Friday." No reply from either captain is held on file. The platform's auto-closure event is described in changelog entry 4.1.2. The Registrar notes that the "per email agreement" annotation in Section 3.12 is not supported by the correspondence held.

6.2 Appeal correspondence (extract).

From: Farid Haddad — 30 Sep: "Please find attached our Notice of Appeal against the forfeit decision of 21 September. We ask that the Appeals Panel consider the raw registration export showing a 12 September submitted date. Happy to attend any hearing. Farid Haddad, coach, Kingsmere Kestrels."
From: Wanjiru Lindqvist (Registrar) — 1 Oct: "Received, thank you. Your appeal has been opened as AP-24/09. The Appeals Panel will convene in due course per Regulation 7.4. Please ensure the appeal filing fee of $40 is lodged if not already done, per Regulation 7.2; an appeal is not validly commenced without it. Please retain any receipt."
From: Farid Haddad — 1 Oct: "Understood. I'll sort the fee this week."
No receipt, bank credit, cheque record, ledger entry or cash-book entry referencing AP-24/09 or a $40 appeal fee from Kingsmere Kestrels is held on file as at 14 December 2024. The Appeals Panel has not convened; the Treasurer's search of the November bank statements (per her note of 2 December: "went through Nov line by line, nothing for $40 or KK") did not identify such a payment. For comparison, the Association's cash book shows that on 1 October 2024 the pavilion office issued receipt #P-1187 for a $40 appeal filing fee in respect of an unrelated umpire-appeal by the Southbank Squalls (appeal AP-24/10), and that appeal was duly listed.

6.3 Northwind Rentals correspondence (extract).

From: Northwind Rentals — 26 Oct: "Our records show boards and posts supplied on 3 August (Riverside) and 10 August (Marsh Basin). Rental per our rate card is $155 per event plus storage where equipment is not checked out the same day. Your 3 August slip is signed but shows no board count; the 10 August slip was never received. Invoice attached: $310 rental plus $55 storage, total $365, payable within 14 days. Please also note our crews were double-committed on 10 August because of your late clash with our corporate booking."
From: Priya Tanaka — 28 Oct: "The 10 August fixture did not proceed; the Association's position is that equipment supplied for a fixture that was stood down should be charged to the party whose booking displaced ours. We are reviewing."
From: Northwind Rentals — 1 Nov: "We hold a confirmed hall booking for 10 August. We have seen no evidence of the Association's booking with the hall. Our invoice stands."
The Association's file does not include any hall booking confirmation for Marsh Basin Sports Hall on 10 August 2024, whether from the venue's own system, from ScheduleMaster, or otherwise.

6.4 Replay of the abandoned Division 3 fixture of 9 November (extract).

From: Wanjiru Lindqvist — 14 Nov: "Both clubs — following EC-2024-31, the 9 November fixture is to be replayed. Please send weekend availability for December and January to Yara by 24 November."
Old Toll Rovers II (team manager, unsigned) — 18 Nov: "We can offer 14 Dec, 15 Dec, or any Saturday in January except 11 Jan."
Marsh Basin Mallards (Leila Alvarez) — 22 Nov: "Our availability is 21 Dec or 4 Jan; we cannot do 14-15 Dec because of the club dinner, and January Saturdays other than 4 Jan look unlikely given holidays."
From: Yara Moreau — 23 Nov: "Noted, thanks. 21 Dec might work — I need to check whether Marsh Basin is free that afternoon given the hall's floor repair. I'll come back to you both once I've spoken to the venue manager."
No further message appears in the chain. Marsh Basin Sports Hall's availability for 21 December is not recorded anywhere in the Association's files. The venue manager was on leave from 25 November to 9 December; whether the Fixtures Secretary spoke to the venue manager upon her return is not documented. The fixture remains shown in ScheduleMaster as "REPLAY — DATE TO BE CONFIRMED."

SECTION 7. COURT FILING EXCERPT (SMALL CLAIMS DIVISION, LOCAL COURT)

Claim no. SC-2024-2819, filed 5 December 2024 by Northwind Rentals Pty Ltd ("the Plaintiff") against Meridian District Recreational Floorball & Netball Association Incorporated ("the Defendant"). Nature of claim: unpaid account for hire of sporting equipment. Amount claimed: $365 plus filing costs of $45.

The Plaintiff's particulars, so far as relevant, state: (a) the Plaintiff supplied boards and posts at Riverside Leisure Centre on 3 August 2024 and at Marsh Basin Sports Hall on 10 August 2024 pursuant to a hire arrangement conducted with the Defendant's venue marshal; (b) the agreed rate was $155 per event; (c) equipment from the 10 August event was not checked out on the day and accrued storage at $5 per day for eleven days, $55 in total; (d) the Defendant has failed to pay the invoiced sum of $365 within the stipulated 14 days.

The Defendant's draft defence, prepared by the Association's solicitor and circulated to the Executive Committee on 11 December (not yet filed), pleads: (a) that the 10 August fixture was displaced by the Plaintiff's own corporate booking, and any equipment supplied for a fixture that did not proceed was supplied to the Plaintiff's event; (b) that the check-out slip regime under Standing Order 11A was not observed by the Plaintiff's crew; (c) set-off in the sum of $30 representing the platform convenience fee under dispute with a third party, which the solicitor's memorandum of 12 December describes as "arguably misconceived, since the $30 is owed to the Association by Harbor Software, not by the Plaintiff." The solicitor's memorandum recommends settling the claim at $365 plus costs. No decision on settlement has been made by the Executive Committee; the matter is listed for directions on 19 January 2025.

SECTION 8. FINDINGS AND RECOMMENDATIONS

8.1 Findings of fact (summary): (a) the 3 August venue conflict arose from a batched-import defect documented in ticket #HAR-4471; (b) the overcharge of junior concession rates arose from a billing defect documented in ticket #HAR-4503 and changelog 4.1.1, for which credit notes were issued on 21 August 2024; (c) the apparent post-freeze registration display was a display defect documented in ticket #HAR-4512; (d) the auto-closure of the 10 August social fixture arose from the legacy-vocabulary mapping defect documented in changelog 4.1.2; (e) notification non-delivery on 12 October arose from the queue-cap known issue documented at changelog 4.1.0 and fixed at 4.1.2; (f) the $30 discrepancy remains an open query with Harbor Software.

8.2 The Registrar notes the interaction between ticket #HAR-4512 and appeal AP-24/09: the forfeit decision of 21 September rests on a display that the vendor has since corrected, and the raw export suggests the player was validly registered before the freeze. The Registrar expresses no view on the merits; the appeal, if validly commenced, is for the Appeals Panel.

8.3 Recommendations: (i) that the Executive Committee consider terminating the maintenance and support contract with Harbor Software under clause 14.3 of the SaaS Agreement (persistent defects); (ii) that a draft termination notice be prepared for the Committee's consideration; (iii) that the September fixture result stand pending the appeal; (iv) that the 9 November replay be scheduled by 31 January 2025; (v) that cash and cheque receipts at the pavilion office be entered against the ledger on the day of receipt, per the vendor's documentation note at 4.1.3; (vi) that the $30 convenience-fee query be pursued in writing.

8.4 Status of recommendations: Recommendation (i) was tabled at the Executive Committee meeting of 12 December 2024. Minute EC-2024-40 records: "Termination of the Harbor Software maintenance contract: DISCUSSION. The Committee noted the draft termination notice circulated by the Registrar. On the proposal of the Treasurer, seconded by the Fixtures Secretary, consideration of termination was DEFERRED to the January 2025 meeting to allow the small claims matter to conclude first. No decision was taken." A draft termination notice, addressed to Harbor Software and dated 10 December 2024, is held in the Registrar's drafts folder marked "HOLD — not sent." No termination notice, notice of intent, or other communication ending or suspending the maintenance contract has been sent to Harbor Software as at the date of this report, and no vendor contract of any kind has been terminated by the Association during 2024. The contracts with Foxglove Software (legacy licence) and Northwind Studio (web design, 2019-2022) ended by expiry in 2022 and 2023 respectively, before the migration, and no current contract exists with either.

APPENDIX A. FEES LEDGER — SELECTED ENTRIES (AUGUST-OCTOBER 2024)

Registration fees received: Riverside Rockets $590 (3 Aug); Southbank Squalls $590 bank / $620 ledger (6 Aug); Kingsmere Kestrels $445 incl. 3 juniors at concession (9 Aug); Old Toll Rovers $590 (10 Aug); Marsh Basin Mallards social $180 (12 Aug).
Credit note CN-2024-05, 21 Aug, Kingsmere Kestrels, junior concession overcharge correction, $75.
Forfeit fine, Competition Rule 14, Kingsmere Kestrels (unrelated Aug forfeit, since reversed), $50 — reversed 30 Aug.
Appeal filing fees: receipt #P-1187, 1 Oct, Southbank Squalls, appeal AP-24/10, $40 (cash, pavilion office). No other appeal fee entries appear in the cash book, ledger or bank statements for the period.
Umpire fees, honoraria, hall hire, insurance levy and equipment lines are omitted as not relevant.

APPENDIX B. FIXTURE REGISTER — STATUS AS AT 14 DECEMBER 2024 (EXTRACT)

3 Aug, D1, Riverside Rockets v Southbank Squalls — played (won by Squalls 4-2).
3 Aug, D2, Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers — stood down (venue conflict); replayed 31 Aug — played (1-3).
10 Aug, Social, Old Toll Rovers social v Marsh Basin Mallards social — auto-closed 19 Oct as "abandoned, not to be replayed" (closure mechanism per changelog 4.1.2; annotation provenance unverifiable).
14 Sep, D2, Kingsmere Kestrels v Old Toll Rovers — played 2-2; recorded 21 Sep as forfeit 0-5 against Kestrels (Rule 19), pending appeal AP-24/09.
12 Oct, D1, Riverside Rockets v Southbank Squalls — played; team sheet notification non-delivery (ticket #HAR-4488), no consequence.
9 Nov, D3, Old Toll Rovers II v Marsh Basin Mallards — abandoned at half-time 1-1 (floor fault); replay ordered EC-2024-31; replay listed as "REPLAY — DATE TO BE CONFIRMED"; status: replay ordered, date outstanding.

APPENDIX C. ROSTER FREEZE CONFIGURATION NOTE

The Registrar's instruction of 4 September requested configuration of the registration freeze. Harbor's reply of 5 September logged it "as a configuration task for the current sprint." The sprints of September and October concluded (per the vendor's portal) without any release note referencing a registration-freeze feature or configuration, and no confirmation of completion appears in the correspondence held. Whether the freeze is currently operative in the platform is unknown to the Registrar. The version 4.1.1 and 4.1.2 release notes contain no entry concerning registration freezes.

APPENDIX D. DOCUMENTS RELIED UPON

SaaS Agreement with Harbor Software (15 Nov 2023); Governance Manual Standing Orders 4(b), 11, 11A; Competition Rules 14 and 19; Disciplinary Regulations 7.2 and 7.4; migration diary (July 2024); Treasurer's working papers (Aug, Nov, Dec 2024); tickets HAR-4402, 4471, 4488, 4503, 4512; Harbor Software release notes 4.0.9-4.1.3 (portal extract, 6 Dec 2024); correspondence at Section 6; Small Claims filing SC-2024-2819; Executive Committee Minutes EC-2023-44, EC-2024-31, EC-2024-40; fixture register; cash book; receipt book stubs (P-series).

Wanjiru Lindqvist, Honorary Registrar. Ends.

CM: Noted, action on IT. Item three, the Saturday double-booking. Rosa, walk us through it.

And Chiara, I want to say, brilliant job on the catering numbers for that Saturday, truly, you ordering sandwiches for the exam-prep headcount while I'd booked the workshop headcount with Copperleaf has created the single most confusing invoice I have ever seen.

CM: Was that sarcasm, Rosa?

(2) The Kestrel Dental workshop on Saturday is CANCELLED, I phoned their practice manager this morning and confirmed, we'll reschedule for June -- approved, done. (3) Rosa's proposal to hire Callum Sorensen as a paid weekend tutor to cover the reschedule -- I'm shelving that one, Callum's got a conflict of interest since he negotiated the Granite storage contract, we'll use agency staff instead, sorry Rosa. CM: Minuted. Meeting closed 3:40pm. These minutes to be circulated, and Rosa, don't paraphrase me again please.

--- END MEETING NOTES ---

Please direct all further Delgado queries to me and only me, I am begging. Also the soup was cold by the time I got to eat it, in case anyone was wondering how my day is going.

CM: Agreed, and let's kill the other rumour right now. I never told Rosa that Uma dropped Dmitri. I told Rosa that Uma had 'processed a withdrawal for one of the Delgados' and Rosa, with respect, you filled in the rest yourself.

RP: That... is unfortunately accurate. Moving on before I die of embarrassment.

CM: Item two, the hardship refund. Dmitri wants a partial lab-fee refund under the hardship clause. The handbook says hardship refunds apply when a student withdraws for documented work-schedule changes within the first 8 weeks. We're in week 6, he attached his Kestrel Dental rota, so handbooks says yes. HOWEVER -- and I checked with Callum by phone, he agreed -- the autumn Python pre-enrolment discount Dmitri received includes a signed waiver saying he accepts no lab-fee refunds on any withdrawal. So the waiver beats the hardship clause. Decision: no refund. We WILL waive his 25-pound late-withdrawal admin fee as a goodwill gesture, that's approved, effective today.

UK: Minuted. Also flag: Antonia Delgado got a 'sorry to see you go' email meant for Dmitri, because the roster system matched on surname. She's fine, she thought it was funny, but let's fix the template.

CM: Noted, action on IT. Item three, the Saturday double-booking. Rosa, walk us through it.

RP: So, the mix-up. I double-booked the entire Saturday cohort -- Kestrel Dental's oral-health workshop AND the exam prep session in the same room at the same time, 11am Saturday. My fault, the calendar migrated badly, whatever, it's on me. And Chiara, I want to say, brilliant job on the catering numbers for that Saturday, truly, you ordering sandwiches for the exam-prep headcount while I'd booked the workshop headcount with Copperleaf has created the single most confusing invoice I have ever seen.

CM: Was that sarcasm, Rosa?

RP: Yes. Obviously. I'm drowning here.

CM: Decision time on item three, people, actual decisions: (1) We EXTEND Dmitri's autumn Python payment deadline by two weeks, he asked in his form and it costs us nothing -- approved. (2) The Kestrel Dental workshop on Saturday is CANCELLED, I phoned their practice manager this morning and confirmed, we'll reschedule for June -- approved, done. (3) Rosa's proposal to hire Callum Sorensen as a paid weekend tutor to cover the reschedule -- I'm shelving that one, Callum's got a conflict of interest since he negotiated the Granite storage contract, we'll use agency staff instead, sorry Rosa. (4) Rosa's other proposal to cancel the exam prep session as well and just give everyone the morning off -- rejected, we are NOT doing that, exam prep proceeds. So: extended deadline, yes; cancelled workshop, yes; hire Callum, no; cancel exam prep, no; lab-fee refund, no; late-fee waiver, yes. That's the whole slate. Anyone got anything else?

UK: One last thing for completeness: the Copperleaf deposit. I know the old clause said we paid it, but per Amendment 2 it's their problem now. Just so the minutes are complete.

CM: Minuted. Meeting closed 3:40pm. These minutes to be circulated, and Rosa, don't paraphrase me again please.

P.S. from Uma, written 5pm: also, in case anyone asks, I did NOT initiate Dmitri's withdrawal, and I did not process one for Antonia either -- she's still enrolled, she's fine, she's actually thriving. Please direct all further Delgado queries to me and only me, I am begging. Also the soup was cold by the time I got to eat it, in case anyone was wondering how my day is going.

state: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE — Northwind Labs Announces Completion of the Corrigan Rooftop Array. Northwind Labs today confirmed that the 240-panel rooftop installation commissioned for the Corrigan distribution centre was energised on 14 March and has, per the attached monitoring dashboard, produced 41.2 MWh in its first quarter of operation. The company's standard 25-year limited warranty applies to all modules supplied under this contract. Purchasers are directed to Section 4(c) of the Warranty Schedule, which provides that microcracks detected in any module are covered only where an accredited inspector attributes the cracking to hail impact exceeding 25 mm in diameter; microcracks arising from any other cause, including thermal cycling, handling, or transit, are expressly excluded from coverage. A hailstorm did strike the Corrigan district on 2 September of last year, and Northwind Labs at that time issued a public advisory noting that some older installations in the district warranted inspection. However, the post-storm inspection report for this array, filed by accredited inspector Greta Fischer and dated 20 September, concluded that no hail impact marks were present on the modules and that observed microcracks on four panels originated from thermal cycling across the summer temperature range. Separately, the contract grants a 5-year workmanship guarantee on racking and wiring, and a 10-year inverter replacement guarantee, neither of which extends to the glass or cells of the modules themselves. Installer Kwame Mensah has scheduled replacement of the four affected panels at the purchaser's expense, and a purchase order for replacement modules at $1,840 has been raised. Northwind Labs reminds all press contacts that the warranty document, not this release, is the sole authoritative statement of coverage, and that inquiries concerning Section 4(c) should be directed to the warranty office rather than to the press desk.

question.instruction: Using the coverage rules stated in the release — a 25-year module warranty that contains an exception clause for microcracks, where microcracks are covered only if an accredited inspector attributes them to hail impact exceeding 25 mm — determine whether the four cracked panels on the Corrigan array are covered by the module warranty, answering yes if covered and no if not.

notes: Inspector Fischer attributed cracks to thermal cycling; hail exclusion exception requires hail attribution; storm distractor does not apply to this array.

state: GRANITE SOFTWARE OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH — INSTALLER INJURY INTAKE FORM. Form 7-B must be completed within 24 hours of any incident on a solar installation site. Employee name: Callum Mensah. Site: rooftop photovoltaic retrofit, Harbourview block. Date of incident: 11 June. Section A — Nature of injury: employee reports a laceration to the left forearm sustained while torqueing a rail clamp, plus subsequent dizziness. Section B — Height and fall record: employee did not fall from the roof; no fall-arrest equipment was deployed; no rescue from height occurred. Section C — Medical attention: wound closed with four sutures at the Riverside clinic on the day of the incident. Section D — Heat and conditions: ambient temperature at 14:00 local reading was 33 degrees C with full sun exposure on an unshaded metal roof; employee had taken one water break in the preceding four hours. Section E — Prior conditions: employee disclosed at onboarding, and again on this form, a pre-existing cardiac arrhythmia under regular medication. Occupational health officer note: per Directive 12, a heat-related illness is recordable only where the affected worker had no pre-existing condition that could independently account for the symptoms, and where the worker was denied a rest break, not where the worker declined one. notes: Arrhythmia could account for dizziness, and Mensah declined (was not denied) the 13:15 break; both Directive 12 conditions fail.

state: SECTION 3 OF 9 — COMMUNITY SOLAR GRANT APPLICATION, submitted by Tidewater Software Community Energy Initiative. Applicant: Tidewater Software, acting as fiscal sponsor for the Marsh Flats residents' cooperative. Project summary: installation of 96 photovoltaic panels on the Marsh Flats community hall, with associated battery storage, serving an estimated 140 low-income households. Grant conditions under the Bright Neighbourhoods Fund, as reproduced in the applicant's own compliance annex: (a) at least 60 percent of benefiting households must fall below the regional median income; (b) the applicant or sponsor must not have an outstanding environmental violation within the previous 5 years; (c) the project must commence within 12 months of award; (d) matching funds of at least 20 percent of total cost must be secured by application date. Applicant's stated figures: regional median income $52,000; of the 140 households, 92 are documented below the median, and a further 34 households receive housing benefit which, per the fund's guidance notes, may be treated as evidence of low income. Commencement: residents have voted to begin works in March of next year, which the applicant states is within the 12-month window from a September award. Matching funds: the cooperative holds $18,000 in a designated account and has a verbal pledge of $9,000 from Bluefin Rentals; total project cost is quoted as $96,000. Compliance note filed by Priya Bergstrom, grant officer: verbal pledges do not count as secured funds under condition (d), and the September award date is contingent, as the fund has not yet confirmed its decision calendar; historical environmental violations are counted only against the applicant or sponsor, not against subcontractors — the proposed installer, Granite Software, has two open violations, but this is irrelevant to condition (b). Tidewater Software itself has none.

question.instruction: Condition (d) of the fund requires matching funds of at least 20 percent of total cost, secured as of the application date, with verbal pledges not counting as secured. Using the figures in the application, does this project currently satisfy the matching-funds condition?

notes: 20% of $96,000 = $19,200; secured funds $18,000; $9,000 pledge excluded; 92+34=126 households distractor is condition (a).

state: PRESS STATEMENT — Bluefin Rentals Property Group. Bluefin Rentals is pleased to announce the second phase of its rooftop solar programme across the Halden self-storage portfolio. Under phase two, panels will be fitted to eleven additional storage facilities, following the successful phase one fit-out of three sites completed in the previous financial year. The company's published procurement policy applies to this phase: solar contracts exceeding $250,000 in value must be tendered openly, except where the works are awarded to a supplier already under a master framework agreement, in which case a direct award is permitted provided the framework was itself tendered within the preceding four years. The phase two contract, valued at $312,000, was awarded directly to Northwind Labs under the master framework agreement signed six years ago, following a competitive tender. A separate $190,000 battery storage contract was awarded to Tidewater Software without tender; the policy's tendering threshold applies to each contract individually, not to their combined value. Rosa Bergstrom, estates director, is quoted: "We are proud to demonstrate that renewable investment and sound procurement can proceed together." The statement further notes that the phase one installer, whose contract was fully tendered at the time, achieved an average payback period of 6.1 years, and that phase two sites were selected for roof condition, grid connection availability, and local planning considerations. A residents' liaison meeting is scheduled for next month, and it was not confirmed at the time of writing whether phase three sites have been identified. End of statement.

notes: Direct award allowed only if framework tendered within 4 preceding years; framework was tendered 6 years ago, outside window.

state: GRANT APPLICATION SECTION 5 — HOUSEHOLD ELIGIBILITY AUDIT, submitted by Greta Fischer on behalf of the Dunmore Lane Community Solar Cooperative. This section documents the cooperative's 47 participating households for the Regional Energy Resilience Grant. Programme rules as restated by the applicant: households qualify as vulnerable where they are (i) home to a resident aged over 70, (ii) dependent on electrically powered medical equipment, (iii) in fuel poverty as defined by spending more than 10 percent of net income on energy, or (iv) without any alternative heating source. Documentation provided: household 12, the Okonkwo residence, includes a 74-year-old resident and spends 8 percent of income on energy; household 19, the Ilic residence, spends 14 percent of income on energy but has gas central heating and no elderly or medically dependent residents; household 26, the Priya residence — unrelated to any person of the same first name in other applications — spends 9 percent on energy, has a heat pump as primary heating with electric backup, and cares for a resident on a home dialysis machine; household 33, the Adeyemi residence, spends 11 percent of income on energy and is headed by a resident aged 69; the cooperative's chair, Kwame Mensah, notes that several other households previously flagged have since withdrawn. Grant officer remark appended in the margin by Yara Bergstrom: the fuel-poverty test is applied strictly against the 10 percent figure, and the age test is applied strictly against the over-70 requirement, with no discretion for near-miss cases; equipment dependency qualifies regardless of any other household circumstances; a household need meet only one of the four criteria to be classed as vulnerable. Applications containing material misstatements are void, but arithmetic near-misses corrected at audit, as occurred here, are not treated as misstatements.

notes: Spends 11% (meets fuel poverty) but head is 69, not over 70 — wait, 11% > 10% satisfies criterion (iii). Correction: qualifies TRUE via fuel poverty; see notes.

A.5 Internet.

A.6 Timezones.
Core hours are 9:30–3:00 Pacific. If you live in a timezone more than 3 hours off, you and your lead set written core overlap hours. Written means in the HRIS notes field, not a handshake.

Employees hired before 2022 who had written remote arrangements keep them until role change. Currently 4 people are grandfathered: (names on file with HR, not in this doc for privacy, which defeats the purpose of a policy doc, noted for rev 8).

SECTION B. TIME OFF: PTO, PARENTAL LEAVE, SABBATICAL

B.1 PTO.
Full time employees accrue PTO at 15 days/year for years 0–2, 20 days for years 3–7, 25 days for 8+. Accrual per paycheck, you can borrow up to 5 unaccrued days with lead approval. PTO requests over 5 consecutive business days need 30 days advance notice in the HRIS. Under 5 days, one week notice is polite but the rule is 3 business days.

B.2 PTO carryover.
Max carryover 5 days into the new calendar year. Rest forfeits. Yes forfeits, we warned you in October, we put it in the November newsletter, Ines made a meme about it.

B.3 Blackout windows.
Fulfillment: Nov 15–Dec 20. Support: none, support takes turns. Sales: first week of each quarter unless quota already hit.

B.4 Parental leave.
All new parents (birth, adoption, foster placement, surrogacy) get 8 weeks paid parental leave at 100% of base pay. Runs within 12 months of the birth/placement date. Can be split into 2 chunks minimum 2 weeks each. Both parents eligible if both work here. Request via HRIS at least 21 days before intended start if foreseeable. HR confirmation required — leave is not considered approved until the HR status shows APPROVED. Approvals are signed by the People Ops Director. Start date can be moved once by the employee without a new request, moved twice = new request.

B.5 Sabbatical.
After 7 continuous years of service, employees are eligible to apply for a 4-week paid sabbatical, one per lifetime at this company. Apply in Q1 for same-year sabbaticals; the company approves up to 2 per year. Applications reviewed by People Ops Director. If denied, you can reapply next year, no hard feelings, capacity reasons.

B.6 Sick days.
10 sick days/year, separate from PTO. Sick days dont carry over, dont pay out. If you are sick more than 3 consecutive days, HR may ask for a doctors note. We hate asking, blame the auditors.

B.7 Bereavement.
5 days for immediate family (spouse/domestic partner, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, plus spouse's parents and siblings). 2 days for aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, close friends, step relations. 1 day if you need to travel 500+ miles for any of the above, added on top. Definitions under review, see meeting notes attached.

B.8 Jury duty & voting.
Jury duty: paid difference between jury pay and normal pay, unlimited. Voting: early voting exists, use PTO if you want a whole day, otherwise polls are open after work.

B.9 Unpaid leave.
Up to 90 days unpaid leave with Director approval, benefits continue. Beyond 90 days benefits stop unless COBRA.

B.10 Returning from leave.
Same or equivalent role guaranteed for parental leave and sick leave. For sabbatical, same role guaranteed. For unpaid leave, equivalent role guaranteed. Schedule a return-to-work chat with HR the week before you come back, bring snacks, optional.


SECTION C. TUITION & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT REIMBURSEMENT

C.1 What counts.
Job-related courses, certifications, workshops, one conference per year, books yes if job related, podcast subscriptions no, a standing desk treadmill no.

C.2 Caps.
Undergraduate or certification programs: $2,000 per employee per calendar year. Graduate programs: $3,500 per year. One conference per year: registration + travel up to $1,800 combined. Books/materials: $300 per year, inside or outside the tuition cap? Outside, its a separate line, dont get clever.

C.3 Grades.
For graded courses, need B or better for full reimbursement, C gets 50%, below C gets zero. Pass/fail courses need the pass. Certifications need the actual cert copy, not a screenshot of the score page, we been burned.

C.4 How to request.
Submit BEFORE enrolling using HR-311. Pre-approval is required. Retroactive requests considered case by case but default is no. HR has 10 business days to respond, silence is not approval, silence is silence.

C.5 Repayment clawback.
If you leave the company within 12 months of a reimbursement over $1,000, you repay 50% of it. Prorated by month. Payroll deducts it from final checks if needed.

C.6 What never counts.
Anything unrelated to your role or a plausible next role at Foxglove. Someone tried to expense a scuba certification because we sell rain jackets. Denied. HR laughed, then felt bad, then denied again.

SECTION A. REMOTE & HYBRID WORK

A.1 Who can work remote.
Everyone full time can work remote up to 3 days per week (Mon–Fri). Part time folks get 1 day. Interns get none, sorry, come enjoy the office popcorn machine.

A.2 Which days.
Team leads pick anchor days. Anchor day = day everybody must be in office. Most teams anchor is Tuesday. Sales anchors Tuesday AND Thursday because customers like a full house. If you dont know your anchor day, ask your lead, do not guess, guessing caused problems before.

A.3 Hotelling.
We got rid of assigned desks in the Portland office in 2023. You book a desk thru the FoxDesk app. Book by 5pm the day before. If you book and no-show 3 times in one month, app locks you out for 2 weeks and you sit in the lunch room which honestly has better chairs anyway.

A.4 Remote outside Oregon.
Working remote from another state for more than 14 days total in a calendar year requires a form. Form is HR-402. Nobody ever fills this out, please start. Tax people are getting nervous. Working from another COUNTRY requires HR-402 plus legal sign off and minimum 30 days notice. Working from the moon is not addressable under current policy.

A.5 Internet.
You need internet that works. If your internet drops during a client call twice in a week, lead can pull your remote days for that month. This is not a punishment, its a coverage thing. The company does NOT pay your home internet bill. The company DOES pay for a headset, see Section D.

A.6 Timezones.
Core hours are 9:30–3:00 Pacific. If you live in a timezone more than 3 hours off, you and your lead set written core overlap hours. Written means in the HRIS notes field, not a handshake.

A.7 Dress code (current).
Business casual in office. On camera for client calls: top half business casual, whatever below. Hoodies fine on non-client days. Sandals fine year round. This section is under review, see meeting notes attached.

A.8 Remote day tracking.
Remote days are tracked automatically by badge absence. If you badge in and leave after lunch, that still counts as office day, the system is not smart. If you work from home while sick, log it as sick day not remote day, its not a vacation.

A.9 Grandfathered exceptions.
Employees hired before 2022 who had written remote arrangements keep them until role change. Currently 4 people are grandfathered: (names on file with HR, not in this doc for privacy, which defeats the purpose of a policy doc, noted for rev 8).

A.10 Contractors.
Not covered by this section. Contractors follow their own contracts. Stop emailing HR about contractors, please.


SECTION B. TIME OFF: PTO, PARENTAL LEAVE, SABBATICAL

B.1 PTO.
Full time employees accrue PTO at 15 days/year for years 0–2, 20 days for years 3–7, 25 days for 8+. Accrual per paycheck, you can borrow up to 5 unaccrued days with lead approval. PTO requests over 5 consecutive business days need 30 days advance notice in the HRIS. Under 5 days, one week notice is polite but the rule is 3 business days.

B.2 PTO carryover.
Max carryover 5 days into the new calendar year. Rest forfeits. Yes forfeits, we warned you in October, we put it in the November newsletter, Ines made a meme about it.

B.3 Blackout windows.
Fulfillment: Nov 15–Dec 20. Support: none, support takes turns. Sales: first week of each quarter unless quota already hit.

B.4 Parental leave.
All new parents (birth, adoption, foster placement, surrogacy) get 8 weeks paid parental leave at 100% of base pay. Runs within 12 months of the birth/placement date. Can be split into 2 chunks minimum 2 weeks each. Both parents eligible if both work here. Request via HRIS at least 21 days before intended start if foreseeable. HR confirmation required — leave is not considered approved until the HR status shows APPROVED. Approvals are signed by the People Ops Director. Start date can be moved once by the employee without a new request, moved twice = new request.

B.5 Sabbatical.
After 7 continuous years of service, employees are eligible to apply for a 4-week paid sabbatical, one per lifetime at this company. Apply in Q1 for same-year sabbaticals; the company approves up to 2 per year. Applications reviewed by People Ops Director. If denied, you can reapply next year, no hard feelings, capacity reasons.

B.6 Sick days.
10 sick days/year, separate from PTO. Sick days dont carry over, dont pay out. If you are sick more than 3 consecutive days, HR may ask for a doctors note. We hate asking, blame the auditors.

B.7 Bereavement.
5 days for immediate family (spouse/domestic partner, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, plus spouse's parents and siblings). 2 days for aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, close friends, step relations. 1 day if you need to travel 500+ miles for any of the above, added on top. Definitions under review, see meeting notes attached.

B.8 Jury duty & voting.
Jury duty: paid difference between jury pay and normal pay, unlimited. Voting: early voting exists, use PTO if you want a whole day, otherwise polls are open after work.

B.9 Unpaid leave.
Up to 90 days unpaid leave with Director approval, benefits continue. Beyond 90 days benefits stop unless COBRA.

B.10 Returning from leave.
Same or equivalent role guaranteed for parental leave and sick leave. For sabbatical, same role guaranteed. For unpaid leave, equivalent role guaranteed. Schedule a return-to-work chat with HR the week before you come back, bring snacks, optional.


SECTION C. TUITION & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT REIMBURSEMENT

C.1 What counts.
Job-related courses, certifications, workshops, one conference per year, books yes if job related, podcast subscriptions no, a standing desk treadmill no.

C.2 Caps.
Undergraduate or certification programs: $2,000 per employee per calendar year. Graduate programs: $3,500 per year. One conference per year: registration + travel up to $1,800 combined. Books/materials: $300 per year, inside or outside the tuition cap? Outside, its a separate line, dont get clever.

C.3 Grades.
For graded courses, need B or better for full reimbursement, C gets 50%, below C gets zero. Pass/fail courses need the pass. Certifications need the actual cert copy, not a screenshot of the score page, we been burned.

C.4 How to request.
Submit BEFORE enrolling using HR-311. Pre-approval is required. Retroactive requests considered case by case but default is no. HR has 10 business days to respond, silence is not approval, silence is silence.

C.5 Repayment clawback.
If you leave the company within 12 months of a reimbursement over $1,000, you repay 50% of it. Prorated by month. Payroll deducts it from final checks if needed.

C.6 What never counts.
Anything unrelated to your role or a plausible next role at Foxglove. Someone tried to expense a scuba certification because we sell rain jackets. Denied. HR laughed, then felt bad, then denied again.


SECTION D. EQUIPMENT & EXPENSES

D.1 New hire kit: laptop, monitor if requested, headset, mouse. All company property.
D.2 Replacement: broken equipment swapped free, lost equipment is $150 deductible per item unless police report.
D.3 Expense reports: submit within 30 days of purchase, itemized, receipts over $25. Mileage at IRS rate.
D.4 Office snacks: free. Coffee: free but the good beans only on Fridays, dont fight about it.


SECTION E. COMPLAINTS & DISPUTES

E.1 Disagreements about any of the above go first to your lead, then People Ops, then the skip-level. E.2 Everything above is policy and binding. Compiled by: Uma Kowalski, People Ops Director
Rev 7 — May 2024. Rev 6 is void. Rev 5 is very void.

INDEX
A. Remote & Hybrid Work
B. Time Off: PTO, Parental Leave, Sabbatical
C. Tuition & Professional Development Reimbursement
D. Equipment, Expenses & Desk Stuff
E. Bereavement & Sick Days
Appendix 1: Leave Tables
Appendix 2: Reimbursement Caps Quick Card
Then attached: EMAIL THREAD re Viktor leave, MEETING NOTES re handbook review, CHAT LOG re coverage july


SECTION A. REMOTE & HYBRID WORK

A.1 Who can work remote.
Everyone full time can work remote up to 3 days per week (Mon–Fri). Part time folks get 1 day. Interns get none, sorry, come enjoy the office popcorn machine.

A.2 Which days.
Team leads pick anchor days. Anchor day = day everybody must be in office. Most teams anchor is Tuesday. Sales anchors Tuesday AND Thursday because customers like a full house. If you dont know your anchor day, ask your lead, do not guess, guessing caused problems before.

A.3 Hotelling.
We got rid of assigned desks in the Portland office in 2023. You book a desk thru the FoxDesk app. Book by 5pm the day before. If you book and no-show 3 times in one month, app locks you out for 2 weeks and you sit in the lunch room which honestly has better chairs anyway.

A.4 Remote outside Oregon.
Working remote from another state for more than 14 days total in a calendar year requires a form. Form is HR-402. Nobody ever fills this out, please start. Tax people are getting nervous. Working from another COUNTRY requires HR-402 plus legal sign off and minimum 30 days notice. Working from the moon is not addressable under current policy.

A.5 Internet.
You need internet that works. If your internet drops during a client call twice in a week, lead can pull your remote days for that month. This is not a punishment, its a coverage thing. The company does NOT pay your home internet bill. The company DOES pay for a headset, see Section D.

A.6 Timezones.
Core hours are 9:30–3:00 Pacific. If you live in a timezone more than 3 hours off, you and your lead set written core overlap hours. Written means in the HRIS notes field, not a handshake.

A.7 Dress code (current).
Business casual in office. On camera for client calls: top half business casual, whatever below. Hoodies fine on non-client days. Sandals fine year round. This section is under review, see meeting notes attached.

A.8 Remote day tracking.
Remote days are tracked automatically by badge absence. If you badge in and leave after lunch, that still counts as office day, the system is not smart. If you work from home while sick, log it as sick day not remote day, its not a vacation.

A.9 Grandfathered exceptions.
Employees hired before 2022 who had written remote arrangements keep them until role change. Currently 4 people are grandfathered: (names on file with HR, not in this doc for privacy, which defeats the purpose of a policy doc, noted for rev 8).

A.10 Contractors.
Not covered by this section. Contractors follow their own contracts. Stop emailing HR about contractors, please.


SECTION B. TIME OFF: PTO, PARENTAL LEAVE, SABBATICAL

B.1 PTO.
Full time employees accrue PTO at 15 days/year for years 0–2, 20 days for years 3–7, 25 days for 8+. Accrual per paycheck, you can borrow up to 5 unaccrued days with lead approval. PTO requests over 5 consecutive business days need 30 days advance notice in the HRIS. Under 5 days, one week notice is polite but the rule is 3 business days.

B.2 PTO carryover.
Max carryover 5 days into the new calendar year. Rest forfeits. Yes forfeits, we warned you in October, we put it in the November newsletter, Ines made a meme about it.

B.3 Blackout windows.
Fulfillment: Nov 15–Dec 20. Support: none, support takes turns. Sales: first week of each quarter unless quota already hit.

B.4 Parental leave.
All new parents (birth, adoption, foster placement, surrogacy) get 8 weeks paid parental leave at 100% of base pay. Runs within 12 months of the birth/placement date. Can be split into 2 chunks minimum 2 weeks each. Both parents eligible if both work here. Request via HRIS at least 21 days before intended start if foreseeable. HR confirmation required — leave is not considered approved until the HR status shows APPROVED. Approvals are signed by the People Ops Director. Start date can be moved once by the employee without a new request, moved twice = new request.

B.5 Sabbatical.
After 7 continuous years of service, employees are eligible to apply for a 4-week paid sabbatical, one per lifetime at this company. Apply in Q1 for same-year sabbaticals; the company approves up to 2 per year. Applications reviewed by People Ops Director. If denied, you can reapply next year, no hard feelings, capacity reasons.

B.6 Sick days.
10 sick days/year, separate from PTO. Sick days dont carry over, dont pay out. If you are sick more than 3 consecutive days, HR may ask for a doctors note. We hate asking, blame the auditors.

B.7 Bereavement.
5 days for immediate family (spouse/domestic partner, child, parent, sibling, grandparent, grandchild, plus spouse's parents and siblings). 2 days for aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, close friends, step relations. 1 day if you need to travel 500+ miles for any of the above, added on top. Definitions under review, see meeting notes attached.

B.8 Jury duty & voting.
Jury duty: paid difference between jury pay and normal pay, unlimited. Voting: early voting exists, use PTO if you want a whole day, otherwise polls are open after work.

B.9 Unpaid leave.
Up to 90 days unpaid leave with Director approval, benefits continue. Beyond 90 days benefits stop unless COBRA.

B.10 Returning from leave.
Same or equivalent role guaranteed for parental leave and sick leave. For sabbatical, same role guaranteed. For unpaid leave, equivalent role guaranteed. Schedule a return-to-work chat with HR the week before you come back, bring snacks, optional.


SECTION C. TUITION & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT REIMBURSEMENT

C.1 What counts.
Job-related courses, certifications, workshops, one conference per year, books yes if job related, podcast subscriptions no, a standing desk treadmill no.

C.2 Caps.
Undergraduate or certification programs: $2,000 per employee per calendar year. Graduate programs: $3,500 per year. One conference per year: registration + travel up to $1,800 combined. Books/materials: $300 per year, inside or outside the tuition cap? Outside, its a separate line, dont get clever.

C.3 Grades.
For graded courses, need B or better for full reimbursement, C gets 50%, below C gets zero. Pass/fail courses need the pass. Certifications need the actual cert copy, not a screenshot of the score page, we been burned.

C.4 How to request.
Submit BEFORE enrolling using HR-311. Pre-approval is required. Retroactive requests considered case by case but default is no. HR has 10 business days to respond, silence is not approval, silence is silence.

C.5 Repayment clawback.
If you leave the company within 12 months of a reimbursement over $1,000, you repay 50% of it. Prorated by month. Payroll deducts it from final checks if needed.

C.6 What never counts.
Anything unrelated to your role or a plausible next role at Foxglove. Someone tried to expense a scuba certification because we sell rain jackets. Denied. HR laughed, then felt bad, then denied again.


SECTION D. EQUIPMENT & EXPENSES

D.1 New hire kit: laptop, monitor if requested, headset, mouse. All company property.
D.2 Replacement: broken equipment swapped free, lost equipment is $150 deductible per item unless police report.
D.3 Expense reports: submit within 30 days of purchase, itemized, receipts over $25. Mileage at IRS rate.
D.4 Office snacks: free. Coffee: free but the good beans only on Fridays, dont fight about it.


SECTION E. COMPLAINTS & DISPUTES

E.1 Disagreements about any of the above go first to your lead, then People Ops, then the skip-level. E.2 Everything above is policy and binding. E.3 This pack supersedes the handbook v4 where they conflict, except the payroll sections, the handbook still owns payroll. E.4 If you find a typo that changes a meaning, tell Uma, there are typos, there are always typos.

Table 1-C: Sabbatical
Eligibility: 7 continuous years. Length: 4 weeks paid. Max approvals per year: 2. Apply in Q1, decision within 30 days of application.

Table 1-D: Bereavement
5 days immediate family | 2 days extended | +1 day if travel over 500 miles.

FOXGLOVE HEALTH — DEVELOPER PORTAL FAQ (excerpt, last reviewed 3 March 2025)
Maintained by the Developer Experience group. Entries below are reproduced verbatim from the patient-data integration FAQ. This page covers questions we receive about the Foxglove Health data API, the reporting CLI, and webhook configuration. It does not cover billing; see the separate billing FAQ.

────────────────────────────────
Q1. How do I get access to the patient-data API?
A1. Access to the patient-data API requires a server-side API key issued per environment. Client-side keys (browser keys) are never valid for patient-data endpoints, even read-only ones. To obtain a server-side key, your organization's Foxglove contact person submits the key request form on the portal; individual developers cannot self-issue keys. Keys rotate every 90 days and the old key remains valid for 24 hours after rotation as a grace overlap.

────────────────────────────────
Q2. Can I use the same key in staging and production?
A2. No. Keys are environment-bound. A staging key used against production endpoints receives HTTP 403 with error code FOX-ENV-MISMATCH. This is the single most common support ticket we receive, so we mention it here at the top of the page.

────────────────────────────────
Q3. What happens if my key expires during a batch job?
A3. Batch jobs should implement the renewal handshake: 15 minutes before expiry the API returns an X-Renew-Soon header on every response, and your job should request a refreshed key via the /key/renew endpoint using the current key. Jobs that ignore the header will receive HTTP 401 once expiry passes, and HTTP 401 responses are not retried automatically by the gateway.

────────────────────────────────
Q4. How are webhooks secured?
A4. Every webhook payload is signed with an HMAC-SHA256 signature placed in the X-Fox-Signature header. Your receiver must verify the signature using the shared secret shown in the portal under Integrations > Webhooks. Payloads without a valid signature must be rejected by your side. Note that the signature covers the raw request body, not the parsed JSON, so verification must happen before any re-serialization. We recommend verifying before parsing, because re-serializing the JSON and signing that will produce a different byte sequence and the check will fail.

────────────────────────────────
Q5. What is the webhook delivery timeout, and what happens when a delivery times out?
A5. The gateway waits up to 10 seconds for your endpoint to acknowledge with a 2xx status. On timeout the connection is closed and the delivery attempt is recorded with status 'timeout'. You can see attempt logs under Integrations > Webhooks > Delivery log. The delivery log shows the timestamp of each attempt and the response code, when one was received.

────────────────────────────────
Q6. Which HTTP status codes should my webhook endpoint return?
A6. Any 2xx code marks the delivery as acknowledged. Codes 3xx are treated as failures because the gateway does not follow redirects. Codes 4xx and 5xx are treated as failures and logged with the code received.

────────────────────────────────
Q7. How do I export nightly ward reports with the CLI?
A7. The reporting CLI (fh-report) supports the command 'fh-report ward nightly' with flags --date and --format (csv|json). By default it writes to the current directory. Authentication for the CLI uses the same server-side key as the API, supplied via the FOX_KEY environment variable. The CLI does not support browser keys.

────────────────────────────────
Q8. Is the old legacy CLI still supported?
A8. The legacy CLI (fh-legacy) is in maintenance mode: it still runs and will keep running for the foreseeable future, but new features land only in fh-report. Removal of fh-legacy is scheduled in principle, however no removal date has been announced yet, and we will give at least 90 days notice on this page before it stops working. Do not migrate based on rumors in community channels.

────────────────────────────────
Q9. Are there rate limits on the patient-data API?
A9. Yes: 600 requests per minute per key, and 60 requests per second per key, both enforced. Exceeding either limit returns HTTP 429 with the limit that was hit named in the response body. The response also carries a Retry-After header expressed in whole seconds. Bursts up to 50 requests are allowed to arrive simultaneously without tripping the per-second limit, provided the rolling average stays under the per-second value.

────────────────────────────────
Q10. Where can I ask a question that is not on this page?
A10. Write to devex@foxglovehealth.example. Please include the environment, the endpoint, and the correlation ID from the response header X-Fox-Correlation. Questions about pricing or invoices sent to this address are forwarded to the billing team, which maintains a separate FAQ; we cannot answer billing questions ourselves.

────────────────────────────────

THISTLE ANALYTICS — INTERNAL ENGINEERING REPORT
Report TR-2025-07: Migration of build infrastructure from Jenkins to the hosted CI platform
Author: Wanjiru Delgado, Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Peer reviewer: Farid Bergstrom, Staff Engineer
Date of report: 30 June 2025
Status: FINAL (with appended post-mortem addendum added 15 July 2025)
Distribution: Platform Engineering leadership, Finance Business Partner

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The migration of Thistle Analytics' build infrastructure from the self-hosted Jenkins estate to the hosted CI platform was proposed in January 2025 with an original completion target of 31 May 2025. This report summarizes the outcome. In the executive view presented to leadership on 2 June, the migration was described as on track; the fuller picture, including schedule performance, cost performance and the incidents in Appendix C, is set out below. Readers who only need the headline numbers should read Section 2 and the Addendum.

2. SCOPE AND DELIVERABLES
The scope covered 43 build pipelines across four teams: data-ingest, model-training, reporting and mobile.
