SECTION 3 — APPLICANT BACKGROUND & COMMUNITY BENEFIT
Applicant: Ferngully Grain Growers Cooperative
Contact: Viktor Lindqvist, Secretary / Treasurer
Program: Rural Solar Uptake Fund, 2nd call
Project: 120 kW solar PV on shared grain storage + drying shed, Lot 7 Harrow Rd

3.1 About the applicant

Ferngully Grain Growers Coop was formed in 2009 by 11 local farming families. we now have 23 member farms, mostly wheat + barley, some canola. the coop owns the central storage + drying shed on Harrow Rd which all members use during harvest. shed runs grain dryers, aeration fans, augers, and a small office. power bill last yr was approx $41,000, most of it during oct-jan harvest + drying period which happens to be peak sun.

we are a not for profit coop, registered, audited accounts attached (appendix 2). no paid staff, all run by volunteer committee. i have been secretary/treasurer since 2017.

3.2 Previous funding

the coop has not previously received any government or private grant funding. the shed was built in 2011 fully from member contributions + a commercial loan from Harrow Valley Credit Union which was paid off in 2020. this is our first grant application of any kind. we did look at a regional drought support grant in 2019 but decided not to apply as we didnt meet the criteria (it was for individual farms, not coops).

3.3 Community benefit

we believe this project benefits the wider community in several ways, not just coop members:

(a) lower costs for members means grain drying fees can be reduced. committee has agreed to cut the per tonne drying levy by approx 15% once system is running. this matters a lot for the smaller member farms who cant afford their own dryers.

(b) the shed will act as a demonstration site. we will host an annual open day for local farmers (members + non members) to see the system, the monitoring data, and talk to our installer about costs. Granite Analytics (a local ag data firm, one of our members kids works there lol) has offered to set up a public dashboard showing live generation for free.

(c) local jobs: installer we chose (Brackenridge Solar, based in town, 9 staff) will use local electricians + labourers. est 6 local people employed for approx 4 weeks.

(d) school program: Ferngully Primary asked if they can visit for science classes. we said yes, 2 visits per yr, committee member will supervise.

(e) grid support: during off season the shed uses very little power so most generation exports, which helps the local feeder which has voltage issues on hot days according to the network (letter from network attached, appendix 5).

things that are NOT part of this project, so no one gets confused: we are not installing battery storage in this stage, we are not offering power to members homes (not legal for us to sell power anyway), and we are not building any new buildings.

3.4 Why now

shed roof was re-sheeted last yr after storm damage, insurance covered it, so the roof is new and suitable for 25+ yr panel life. installer did structural check, all good (appendix 4). power prices went up approx 22% in last 2 yrs and members are feeling it. harvest dryers are the biggest single cost after fuel.

3.5 Capacity to deliver

we know we are volunteers not a big organisation. committee has 5 members, meets monthly. we have appointed an independent project manager from Brackenridge who has done 30+ commercial installs. i will handle reporting + finances, i have done the coops books for 7 yrs with clean audits every yr. the coop has $52,000 in reserves, of which $38,000 is committed to this project as our co contribution.

3.6 Support letters

attached: shire council (appendix 6), Ferngully Primary (appendix 7), network operator (appendix 5), 2 non member farms who want to attend open days (appendix 8).

sorry this section is a bit long, wanted to cover everything. happy to answer q's by phone, number on cover page. best time is evenings, im on the header most days.

Viktor Lindqvist
Secretary / Treasurer
Ferngully Grain Growers Cooperative

2. INCIDENT POSTMORTEM PM-2024-04
Water ingress, Brightwater Court, units 5B -> 4B
Version 2.1 (final), author: Dalia Tanaka, reviewed by: operations lead
Date of this version: 12 April 2024
=====================================================================

2.1 Summary

On Tuesday 12 March 2024, in the evening, water escaped from the kitchen of flat 5B and entered flat 4B below through the kitchen ceiling. The tenant of 4B reported at 21:14. The water was isolated at 01:20 on 13 March by our contractor. The source was a cracked compression isolation valve that was installed by Okafor Plumbing & Heating on 19 February 2024 under work order WO-2024-0219-3 (replacement of dripping old valve). The damage in 4B is ceiling plaster, paint, part of the laminate floor, and some personal items of the tenant (laptop, rug). There was no damage in the common parts. The water reported by the ground floor shop Copperleaf Outfitters on the same night was a different problem (blocked gutter on awning), handled in ticket HL-2024-0312-09 and not part of this postmortem.

2.2 Impact

- Flat 4B: kitchen unusable for part of 12 and 13 March, ceiling wet, laminate swelled in approx 3 m2. Tenant personal items damaged (tenant claims through own contents insurer).
- Flat 5B: no water supply from 01:20 to 12:30 on 13 March (approx 11 hours). Tenant was away and did not experience it directly.
- Owner: potential cost of repairs, but see 2.6.
- Harbourline: some service level misses, see 2.5.

2.3 Timeline (all times local)

19 Feb 2024 (Mon) 10:00-12:15: Okafor replaced isolation valve in 5B under WO-2024-0219-3. Completion signed by tenant of 5B at 12:15. Contractor invoice INV-OK-1177 for 185.00 paid by Harbourline on behalf of owner on 26 Feb.
12 Mar 2024 (Tue) approx 20:30-21:00: valve body cracks (estimated, from amount of water).
12 Mar 21:14: ticket created by tenant 4B.
12 Mar 21:47: first reply to tenant 4B by property manager.
12 Mar 22:10: tenant 5B reached by phone, gives permission to enter.
13 Mar 01:05: contractor on site.
13 Mar 01:20: water isolated.
13 Mar 09:40: written update to tenant 5B.
13 Mar 10:02: phone call with tenant 4B.
13 Mar 12:30: new valve fitted, water restored to 5B.
14 Mar: tenant 4B opens claim with own contents insurer.
15 Mar 10:00: written update to tenant 4B.
18 Mar 09:30: notification to building insurer Stonebridge Mutual.
19 Mar 16:10: written warranty notice to Okafor.
20 Mar 08:50: Okafor accepts responsibility in writing.
4 Apr: ceiling and floor repair in 4B by Castleford Decorators.

2.4 Root cause

The new valve (brand "TorrentFix TF-15") had a manufacturing defect: hairline crack in the brass body near the compression nut. Hiro Okafor reported that another valve of the same batch failed in a different property one week before. The fitting itself (tightening) was checked by an independent plumber from Rapidflow on 26 March at our request, who said the installation was "acceptable, not overtightened", and the failure is "most likely material defect". Our initial assumption that the tenant of 5B had left a tap or appliance open was wrong. The tenant of 5B was away since Sunday 10 March.

Why we first blamed the 5B tenant: in our building history, 3 of the last 4 leaks were caused by tenants (bath overflow twice, washing machine hose once). Pattern thinking. Lesson in 2.7.

2.5 Service level review (against HS-7)

The incident started on Tuesday 12 March. For HS-7 (c) and (d) we count business days after that day.

(a) Acknowledge reporter within 1 hour: ticket 21:14, reply 21:47 = 33 minutes. MET.
(b) Contractor on site within 4 hours: 21:14 to 01:05 = 3 hours 51 minutes. MET. Note: backup plumber Rapidflow offered 02:30, which would have been 5 h 16 min and missed; correct decision to wait for Okafor.
(c) Written update to every affected tenant within 2 business days after the day of ticket: the two business days after Tue 12 March are Wed 13 and Thu 14 March. Tenant 5B got written update on 13 March. Tenant 4B got a phone call on 13 March and written email only on Fri 15 March 10:00. The phone call does not count. For tenant 4B: see our assessment below.
(d) Building insurer notified in writing within 5 business days after day of incident: 13, 14, 15, 18, 19 March, so the last day is Tue 19 March. Notified Mon 18 March. MET.
(e) Warranty notice before warranty expiry: see 2.6.

Our assessment for (c): I was first writing in draft version 1.0 that (c) was met because the 5B update was on time and there was a phone call to 4B. The operations lead corrected this in review: HS-7 says every affected tenant, and in writing. So for (c) the result is: met for 5B, not met for 4B. The overall (c) is NOT MET.

2.6 Responsibility and cost

Work order WO-2024-0219-3 is under the Okafor framework agreement (appendix B). Clause 9.1 of that agreement: "The Contractor guarantees all parts supplied and all workmanship for a period of 30 (thirty) calendar days from the date of completion of the job. Defects appearing within this period, and damage directly caused by such defects, shall be rectified and paid by the Contractor, provided written notice is given to the Contractor within the guarantee period." Clause 9.2: "After the guarantee period the Contractor is liable only if negligence is proven."

Completion: 19 February 2024. Year 2024 is leap year, so February has 29 days. 30 calendar days from 19 Feb: 10 days to 29 Feb, then 20 days in March = 20 March 2024 is the last day of guarantee. Failure on 12 March is inside the period (22 days after completion). Written notice was sent on 19 March, also inside the period, one day before the end.

The owner Beatriz Petrov first thought she must pay the contractor again for the second valve, and Okafor also first sent invoice INV-OK-1213 for 240.00 for the emergency call-out and the second valve, addressed to Harbourline for the owner. After the warranty notice Okafor cancelled this invoice (credit note CN-OK-0031, appendix D). The ceiling and floor repair (2,440.00 excl. VAT) is being paid by Okafor through their liability insurer. The owner pays nothing for this incident, apart from her normal management fee. The tenant of 4B pays nothing. The tenant of 5B pays nothing and is not at fault.

Note about the 4B tenant's personal items: her contents insurer Northgate may later try to recover the money from Okafor (subrogation). That is between Northgate and Okafor.

Note about the rent reduction requested by the tenant of 5B: owner declined on 2 April, because the water interruption was 11 hours and the tenant was not at home. The owner offered a reduction of 150.00 to tenant 4B for kitchen being unusable, accepted by tenant 4B on 5 April.

2.7 Lessons and actions

L1. Do not assume tenant fault before inspection. Action: remove the "likely tenant cause" default text in our leak template.
L2. Written updates to all affected tenants, not only the one we speak to first. Action: HS-7 checklist on P1 tickets to list each unit.
L3. Track warranty dates for every contractor job. Action: add "guarantee end date" field to work orders. In this incident we were only one day before the end; luck.
L4. Batch problem with TorrentFix TF-15. Action: Okafor will replace all TF-15 installed in our buildings in the last 3 months (4 installations), at their cost.

2.8 Open points at date of this version

- Final settlement from Okafor's insurer expected in May.
- Owner has mentioned she may want a bigger renovation of 4B kitchen. Not part of this postmortem.

2. INCIDENT POSTMORTEM PM-2024-04
Water ingress, Brightwater Court, units 5B -> 4B
Version 2.1 (final), author: Dalia Tanaka, reviewed by: operations lead
Date of this version: 12 April 2024
=====================================================================

2.1 Summary

On Tuesday 12 March 2024, in the evening, water escaped from the kitchen of flat 5B and entered flat 4B below through the kitchen ceiling. The tenant of 4B reported at 21:14. The water was isolated at 01:20 on 13 March by our contractor. The source was a cracked compression isolation valve that was installed by Okafor Plumbing & Heating on 19 February 2024 under work order WO-2024-0219-3 (replacement of dripping old valve). The damage in 4B is ceiling plaster, paint, part of the laminate floor, and some personal items of the tenant (laptop, rug). There was no damage in the common parts. The water reported by the ground floor shop Copperleaf Outfitters on the same night was a different problem (blocked gutter on awning), handled in ticket HL-2024-0312-09 and not part of this postmortem.

2.2 Impact

- Flat 4B: kitchen unusable for part of 12 and 13 March, ceiling wet, laminate swelled in approx 3 m2. Tenant personal items damaged (tenant claims through own contents insurer).
- Flat 5B: no water supply from 01:20 to 12:30 on 13 March (approx 11 hours). Tenant was away and did not experience it directly.
- Owner: potential cost of repairs, but see 2.6.
- Harbourline: some service level misses, see 2.5.

2.3 Timeline (all times local)

19 Feb 2024 (Mon) 10:00-12:15: Okafor replaced isolation valve in 5B under WO-2024-0219-3. Completion signed by tenant of 5B at 12:15. Contractor invoice INV-OK-1177 for 185.00 paid by Harbourline on behalf of owner on 26 Feb.
12 Mar 2024 (Tue) approx 20:30-21:00: valve body cracks (estimated, from amount of water).
12 Mar 21:14: ticket created by tenant 4B.
12 Mar 21:47: first reply to tenant 4B by property manager.
12 Mar 22:10: tenant 5B reached by phone, gives permission to enter.
13 Mar 01:05: contractor on site.
13 Mar 01:20: water isolated.
13 Mar 09:40: written update to tenant 5B.
13 Mar 10:02: phone call with tenant 4B.
13 Mar 12:30: new valve fitted, water restored to 5B.
14 Mar: tenant 4B opens claim with own contents insurer.
15 Mar 10:00: written update to tenant 4B.
18 Mar 09:30: notification to building insurer Stonebridge Mutual.
19 Mar 16:10: written warranty notice to Okafor.
20 Mar 08:50: Okafor accepts responsibility in writing.
4 Apr: ceiling and floor repair in 4B by Castleford Decorators.

2.4 Root cause

The new valve (brand "TorrentFix TF-15") had a manufacturing defect: hairline crack in the brass body near the compression nut. Hiro Okafor reported that another valve of the same batch failed in a different property one week before. The fitting itself (tightening) was checked by an independent plumber from Rapidflow on 26 March at our request, who said the installation was "acceptable, not overtightened", and the failure is "most likely material defect". Our initial assumption that the tenant of 5B had left a tap or appliance open was wrong. The tenant of 5B was away since Sunday 10 March.

Why we first blamed the 5B tenant: in our building history, 3 of the last 4 leaks were caused by tenants (bath overflow twice, washing machine hose once). Pattern thinking. Lesson in 2.7.

2.5 Service level review (against HS-7)

The incident started on Tuesday 12 March. For HS-7 (c) and (d) we count business days after that day.

(a) Acknowledge reporter within 1 hour: ticket 21:14, reply 21:47 = 33 minutes. MET.
(b) Contractor on site within 4 hours: 21:14 to 01:05 = 3 hours 51 minutes. MET. Note: backup plumber Rapidflow offered 02:30, which would have been 5 h 16 min and missed; correct decision to wait for Okafor.
(c) Written update to every affected tenant within 2 business days after the day of ticket: the two business days after Tue 12 March are Wed 13 and Thu 14 March. Tenant 5B got written update on 13 March. Tenant 4B got a phone call on 13 March and written email only on Fri 15 March 10:00. The phone call does not count. For tenant 4B: see our assessment below.
(d) Building insurer notified in writing within 5 business days after day of incident: 13, 14, 15, 18, 19 March, so the last day is Tue 19 March. Notified Mon 18 March. MET.
(e) Warranty notice before warranty expiry: see 2.6.

Our assessment for (c): I was first writing in draft version 1.0 that (c) was met because the 5B update was on time and there was a phone call to 4B. The operations lead corrected this in review: HS-7 says every affected tenant, and in writing. So for (c) the result is: met for 5B, not met for 4B. The overall (c) is NOT MET.

2.6 Responsibility and cost

Work order WO-2024-0219-3 is under the Okafor framework agreement (appendix B). Clause 9.1 of that agreement: "The Contractor guarantees all parts supplied and all workmanship for a period of 30 (thirty) calendar days from the date of completion of the job. Defects appearing within this period, and damage directly caused by such defects, shall be rectified and paid by the Contractor, provided written notice is given to the Contractor within the guarantee period." Clause 9.2: "After the guarantee period the Contractor is liable only if negligence is proven."

Completion: 19 February 2024. Year 2024 is leap year, so February has 29 days. 30 calendar days from 19 Feb: 10 days to 29 Feb, then 20 days in March = 20 March 2024 is the last day of guarantee. Failure on 12 March is inside the period (22 days after completion). Written notice was sent on 19 March, also inside the period, one day before the end.

The owner Beatriz Petrov first thought she must pay the contractor again for the second valve, and Okafor also first sent invoice INV-OK-1213 for 240.00 for the emergency call-out and the second valve, addressed to Harbourline for the owner. After the warranty notice Okafor cancelled this invoice (credit note CN-OK-0031, appendix D). The ceiling and floor repair (2,440.00 excl. VAT) is being paid by Okafor through their liability insurer. The owner pays nothing for this incident, apart from her normal management fee. The tenant of 4B pays nothing. The tenant of 5B pays nothing and is not at fault.

Note about the 4B tenant's personal items: her contents insurer Northgate may later try to recover the money from Okafor (subrogation). That is between Northgate and Okafor.

Note about the rent reduction requested by the tenant of 5B: owner declined on 2 April, because the water interruption was 11 hours and the tenant was not at home. The owner offered a reduction of 150.00 to tenant 4B for kitchen being unusable, accepted by tenant 4B on 5 April.

2.7 Lessons and actions

L1. Do not assume tenant fault before inspection. Action: remove the "likely tenant cause" default text in our leak template.
L2. Written updates to all affected tenants, not only the one we speak to first. Action: HS-7 checklist on P1 tickets to list each unit.
L3. Track warranty dates for every contractor job. Action: add "guarantee end date" field to work orders. In this incident we were only one day before the end; luck.
L4. Batch problem with TorrentFix TF-15. Action: Okafor will replace all TF-15 installed in our buildings in the last 3 months (4 installations), at their cost.

2.8 Open points at date of this version

- Final settlement from Okafor's insurer expected in May.
- Owner has mentioned she may want a bigger renovation of 4B kitchen. Not part of this postmortem.

2. INCIDENT POSTMORTEM PM-2024-04
Water ingress, Brightwater Court, units 5B -> 4B
Version 2.1 (final), author: Dalia Tanaka, reviewed by: operations lead
Date of this version: 12 April 2024
=====================================================================

2.1 Summary

On Tuesday 12 March 2024, in the evening, water escaped from the kitchen of flat 5B and entered flat 4B below through the kitchen ceiling. The tenant of 4B reported at 21:14. The water was isolated at 01:20 on 13 March by our contractor. The source was a cracked compression isolation valve that was installed by Okafor Plumbing & Heating on 19 February 2024 under work order WO-2024-0219-3 (replacement of dripping old valve). The damage in 4B is ceiling plaster, paint, part of the laminate floor, and some personal items of the tenant (laptop, rug). There was no damage in the common parts. The water reported by the ground floor shop Copperleaf Outfitters on the same night was a different problem (blocked gutter on awning), handled in ticket HL-2024-0312-09 and not part of this postmortem.

2.2 Impact

- Flat 4B: kitchen unusable for part of 12 and 13 March, ceiling wet, laminate swelled in approx 3 m2. Tenant personal items damaged (tenant claims through own contents insurer).
- Flat 5B: no water supply from 01:20 to 12:30 on 13 March (approx 11 hours). Tenant was away and did not experience it directly.
- Owner: potential cost of repairs, but see 2.6.
- Harbourline: some service level misses, see 2.5.

2.3 Timeline (all times local)

19 Feb 2024 (Mon) 10:00-12:15: Okafor replaced isolation valve in 5B under WO-2024-0219-3. Completion signed by tenant of 5B at 12:15. Contractor invoice INV-OK-1177 for 185.00 paid by Harbourline on behalf of owner on 26 Feb.
12 Mar 2024 (Tue) approx 20:30-21:00: valve body cracks (estimated, from amount of water).
12 Mar 21:14: ticket created by tenant 4B.
12 Mar 21:47: first reply to tenant 4B by property manager.
12 Mar 22:10: tenant 5B reached by phone, gives permission to enter.
13 Mar 01:05: contractor on site.
13 Mar 01:20: water isolated.
13 Mar 09:40: written update to tenant 5B.
13 Mar 10:02: phone call with tenant 4B.
13 Mar 12:30: new valve fitted, water restored to 5B.
14 Mar: tenant 4B opens claim with own contents insurer.
15 Mar 10:00: written update to tenant 4B.
18 Mar 09:30: notification to building insurer Stonebridge Mutual.
19 Mar 16:10: written warranty notice to Okafor.
20 Mar 08:50: Okafor accepts responsibility in writing.
4 Apr: ceiling and floor repair in 4B by Castleford Decorators.

2.4 Root cause

The new valve (brand "TorrentFix TF-15") had a manufacturing defect: hairline crack in the brass body near the compression nut. Hiro Okafor reported that another valve of the same batch failed in a different property one week before. The fitting itself (tightening) was checked by an independent plumber from Rapidflow on 26 March at our request, who said the installation was "acceptable, not overtightened", and the failure is "most likely material defect". Our initial assumption that the tenant of 5B had left a tap or appliance open was wrong. The tenant of 5B was away since Sunday 10 March.

Why we first blamed the 5B tenant: in our building history, 3 of the last 4 leaks were caused by tenants (bath overflow twice, washing machine hose once). Pattern thinking. Lesson in 2.7.

2.5 Service level review (against HS-7)

The incident started on Tuesday 12 March. For HS-7 (c) and (d) we count business days after that day.

(a) Acknowledge reporter within 1 hour: ticket 21:14, reply 21:47 = 33 minutes. MET.
(b) Contractor on site within 4 hours: 21:14 to 01:05 = 3 hours 51 minutes. MET. Note: backup plumber Rapidflow offered 02:30, which would have been 5 h 16 min and missed; correct decision to wait for Okafor.
(c) Written update to every affected tenant within 2 business days after the day of ticket: the two business days after Tue 12 March are Wed 13 and Thu 14 March. Tenant 5B got written update on 13 March. Tenant 4B got a phone call on 13 March and written email only on Fri 15 March 10:00. The phone call does not count. For tenant 4B: see our assessment below.
(d) Building insurer notified in writing within 5 business days after day of incident: 13, 14, 15, 18, 19 March, so the last day is Tue 19 March. Notified Mon 18 March. MET.
(e) Warranty notice before warranty expiry: see 2.6.

Our assessment for (c): I was first writing in draft version 1.0 that (c) was met because the 5B update was on time and there was a phone call to 4B. The operations lead corrected this in review: HS-7 says every affected tenant, and in writing. So for (c) the result is: met for 5B, not met for 4B. The overall (c) is NOT MET.

2.6 Responsibility and cost

Work order WO-2024-0219-3 is under the Okafor framework agreement (appendix B). Clause 9.1 of that agreement: "The Contractor guarantees all parts supplied and all workmanship for a period of 30 (thirty) calendar days from the date of completion of the job. Defects appearing within this period, and damage directly caused by such defects, shall be rectified and paid by the Contractor, provided written notice is given to the Contractor within the guarantee period." Clause 9.2: "After the guarantee period the Contractor is liable only if negligence is proven."

Completion: 19 February 2024. Year 2024 is leap year, so February has 29 days. 30 calendar days from 19 Feb: 10 days to 29 Feb, then 20 days in March = 20 March 2024 is the last day of guarantee. Failure on 12 March is inside the period (22 days after completion). Written notice was sent on 19 March, also inside the period, one day before the end.

The owner Beatriz Petrov first thought she must pay the contractor again for the second valve, and Okafor also first sent invoice INV-OK-1213 for 240.00 for the emergency call-out and the second valve, addressed to Harbourline for the owner. After the warranty notice Okafor cancelled this invoice (credit note CN-OK-0031, appendix D). The ceiling and floor repair (2,440.00 excl. VAT) is being paid by Okafor through their liability insurer. The owner pays nothing for this incident, apart from her normal management fee. The tenant of 4B pays nothing. The tenant of 5B pays nothing and is not at fault.

Note about the 4B tenant's personal items: her contents insurer Northgate may later try to recover the money from Okafor (subrogation). That is between Northgate and Okafor.

Note about the rent reduction requested by the tenant of 5B: owner declined on 2 April, because the water interruption was 11 hours and the tenant was not at home. The owner offered a reduction of 150.00 to tenant 4B for kitchen being unusable, accepted by tenant 4B on 5 April.

2.7 Lessons and actions

L1. Do not assume tenant fault before inspection. Action: remove the "likely tenant cause" default text in our leak template.
L2. Written updates to all affected tenants, not only the one we speak to first. Action: HS-7 checklist on P1 tickets to list each unit.
L3. Track warranty dates for every contractor job. Action: add "guarantee end date" field to work orders. In this incident we were only one day before the end; luck.
L4. Batch problem with TorrentFix TF-15. Action: Okafor will replace all TF-15 installed in our buildings in the last 3 months (4 installations), at their cost.

2.8 Open points at date of this version

- Final settlement from Okafor's insurer expected in May.
- Owner has mentioned she may want a bigger renovation of 4B kitchen. Not part of this postmortem.

2. INCIDENT POSTMORTEM PM-2024-04
Water ingress, Brightwater Court, units 5B -> 4B
Version 2.1 (final), author: Dalia Tanaka, reviewed by: operations lead
Date of this version: 12 April 2024
=====================================================================

2.1 Summary

On Tuesday 12 March 2024, in the evening, water escaped from the kitchen of flat 5B and entered flat 4B below through the kitchen ceiling. The tenant of 4B reported at 21:14. The water was isolated at 01:20 on 13 March by our contractor. The source was a cracked compression isolation valve that was installed by Okafor Plumbing & Heating on 19 February 2024 under work order WO-2024-0219-3 (replacement of dripping old valve). The damage in 4B is ceiling plaster, paint, part of the laminate floor, and some personal items of the tenant (laptop, rug). There was no damage in the common parts. The water reported by the ground floor shop Copperleaf Outfitters on the same night was a different problem (blocked gutter on awning), handled in ticket HL-2024-0312-09 and not part of this postmortem.

2.2 Impact

- Flat 4B: kitchen unusable for part of 12 and 13 March, ceiling wet, laminate swelled in approx 3 m2. Tenant personal items damaged (tenant claims through own contents insurer).
- Flat 5B: no water supply from 01:20 to 12:30 on 13 March (approx 11 hours). Tenant was away and did not experience it directly.
- Owner: potential cost of repairs, but see 2.6.
- Harbourline: some service level misses, see 2.5.

2.3 Timeline (all times local)

19 Feb 2024 (Mon) 10:00-12:15: Okafor replaced isolation valve in 5B under WO-2024-0219-3. Completion signed by tenant of 5B at 12:15. Contractor invoice INV-OK-1177 for 185.00 paid by Harbourline on behalf of owner on 26 Feb.
12 Mar 2024 (Tue) approx 20:30-21:00: valve body cracks (estimated, from amount of water).
12 Mar 21:14: ticket created by tenant 4B.
12 Mar 21:47: first reply to tenant 4B by property manager.
12 Mar 22:10: tenant 5B reached by phone, gives permission to enter.
13 Mar 01:05: contractor on site.
13 Mar 01:20: water isolated.
13 Mar 09:40: written update to tenant 5B.
13 Mar 10:02: phone call with tenant 4B.
13 Mar 12:30: new valve fitted, water restored to 5B.
14 Mar: tenant 4B opens claim with own contents insurer.
15 Mar 10:00: written update to tenant 4B.
18 Mar 09:30: notification to building insurer Stonebridge Mutual.
19 Mar 16:10: written warranty notice to Okafor.
20 Mar 08:50: Okafor accepts responsibility in writing.
4 Apr: ceiling and floor repair in 4B by Castleford Decorators.

2.4 Root cause

The new valve (brand "TorrentFix TF-15") had a manufacturing defect: hairline crack in the brass body near the compression nut. Hiro Okafor reported that another valve of the same batch failed in a different property one week before. The fitting itself (tightening) was checked by an independent plumber from Rapidflow on 26 March at our request, who said the installation was "acceptable, not overtightened", and the failure is "most likely material defect". Our initial assumption that the tenant of 5B had left a tap or appliance open was wrong. The tenant of 5B was away since Sunday 10 March.

Why we first blamed the 5B tenant: in our building history, 3 of the last 4 leaks were caused by tenants (bath overflow twice, washing machine hose once). Pattern thinking. Lesson in 2.7.

2.5 Service level review (against HS-7)

The incident started on Tuesday 12 March. For HS-7 (c) and (d) we count business days after that day.

(a) Acknowledge reporter within 1 hour: ticket 21:14, reply 21:47 = 33 minutes. MET.
(b) Contractor on site within 4 hours: 21:14 to 01:05 = 3 hours 51 minutes. MET. Note: backup plumber Rapidflow offered 02:30, which would have been 5 h 16 min and missed; correct decision to wait for Okafor.
(c) Written update to every affected tenant within 2 business days after the day of ticket: the two business days after Tue 12 March are Wed 13 and Thu 14 March. Tenant 5B got written update on 13 March. Tenant 4B got a phone call on 13 March and written email only on Fri 15 March 10:00. The phone call does not count. For tenant 4B: see our assessment below.
(d) Building insurer notified in writing within 5 business days after day of incident: 13, 14, 15, 18, 19 March, so the last day is Tue 19 March. Notified Mon 18 March. MET.
(e) Warranty notice before warranty expiry: see 2.6.

Our assessment for (c): I was first writing in draft version 1.0 that (c) was met because the 5B update was on time and there was a phone call to 4B. The operations lead corrected this in review: HS-7 says every affected tenant, and in writing. So for (c) the result is: met for 5B, not met for 4B. The overall (c) is NOT MET.

2.6 Responsibility and cost

Work order WO-2024-0219-3 is under the Okafor framework agreement (appendix B). Clause 9.1 of that agreement: "The Contractor guarantees all parts supplied and all workmanship for a period of 30 (thirty) calendar days from the date of completion of the job. Defects appearing within this period, and damage directly caused by such defects, shall be rectified and paid by the Contractor, provided written notice is given to the Contractor within the guarantee period." Clause 9.2: "After the guarantee period the Contractor is liable only if negligence is proven."

Completion: 19 February 2024. Year 2024 is leap year, so February has 29 days. 30 calendar days from 19 Feb: 10 days to 29 Feb, then 20 days in March = 20 March 2024 is the last day of guarantee. Failure on 12 March is inside the period (22 days after completion). Written notice was sent on 19 March, also inside the period, one day before the end.

The owner Beatriz Petrov first thought she must pay the contractor again for the second valve, and Okafor also first sent invoice INV-OK-1213 for 240.00 for the emergency call-out and the second valve, addressed to Harbourline for the owner. After the warranty notice Okafor cancelled this invoice (credit note CN-OK-0031, appendix D). The ceiling and floor repair (2,440.00 excl. VAT) is being paid by Okafor through their liability insurer. The owner pays nothing for this incident, apart from her normal management fee. The tenant of 4B pays nothing. The tenant of 5B pays nothing and is not at fault.

Note about the 4B tenant's personal items: her contents insurer Northgate may later try to recover the money from Okafor (subrogation). That is between Northgate and Okafor.

Note about the rent reduction requested by the tenant of 5B: owner declined on 2 April, because the water interruption was 11 hours and the tenant was not at home. The owner offered a reduction of 150.00 to tenant 4B for kitchen being unusable, accepted by tenant 4B on 5 April.

2.7 Lessons and actions

L1. Do not assume tenant fault before inspection. Action: remove the "likely tenant cause" default text in our leak template.
L2. Written updates to all affected tenants, not only the one we speak to first. Action: HS-7 checklist on P1 tickets to list each unit.
L3. Track warranty dates for every contractor job. Action: add "guarantee end date" field to work orders. In this incident we were only one day before the end; luck.
L4. Batch problem with TorrentFix TF-15. Action: Okafor will replace all TF-15 installed in our buildings in the last 3 months (4 installations), at their cost.

2.8 Open points at date of this version

- Final settlement from Okafor's insurer expected in May.
- Owner has mentioned she may want a bigger renovation of 4B kitchen. Not part of this postmortem.

Dear Sir or Madam, and dear colleagues at Millbrook Estates Holdings,

I do hope this message finds you all very well, and please allow me first to thank you most sincerely for the many years of kind and attentive support you have shown to Foxglove Foods since we first took occupation of Unit 7 in the spring of 2019. It has genuinely been a pleasure to be your tenant, and I would be most grateful if you would accept this submission in the spirit of warmth and respect in which it is offered.

With that said, and with no small amount of regret, I am writing on behalf of Foxglove Foods Ltd to formally give notice that we wish to exercise the tenant's break option contained in Clause 9.2 of our lease, and to bring the tenancy to an end on 28 February 2025, which I understand to be the sixth anniversary date contemplated by that clause. I would be very much obliged if you would treat this form, together with the signed letter attached to it, as our written notice for the purposes of the lease.

I feel it is only courteous to explain our reasons, even though I appreciate the lease does not require us to give any. Over the past two years our ready-meal and chilled sauce lines have grown far more quickly than any of us anticipated, and our board has concluded, after a great deal of careful thought, that we need to consolidate all of our production under a single roof. We have therefore agreed to take a much larger purpose-built facility at Kestrel Park in Stockport, which offers the cold-chain capacity, loading bays and floor area that Unit 7, for all its many merits, simply cannot accommodate. Our move is entirely about relocating our manufacturing to that bigger site; it has nothing whatsoever to do with any dissatisfaction with you or with the estate.

Indeed, I would like to place on record that the estate management team has always been exceptionally helpful. When our roller shutter failed in the winter of 2021 your contractor attended the very same afternoon, and the resurfacing of the service yard last year was handled with great consideration for our delivery schedule. We have never had cause to complain about maintenance, communication or the service charge, and we remain very grateful for all of it. Our finances are also in good order, and I would not wish there to be any impression that we are leaving because of difficulty in meeting our obligations; we intend to pay rent and service charge in full up to the termination date.

I understand from Clause 9.3 that the break is conditional upon the tenant having paid all rent due up to the break date and giving vacant possession. I am pleased to confirm that our account is fully up to date, and we fully intend to hand back the unit with vacant possession, having removed our production equipment, racking and signage. We would, of course, be delighted to arrange a joint inspection at a time that suits your surveyor, so that any dilapidations matters can be discussed in good time and in a cooperative manner. Please do let me know which dates in January might be convenient, and I shall make sure our facilities manager is available.

For your records, our forwarding address from 1 March 2025 will be: Foxglove Foods Ltd, Unit 2, Kestrel Park, Brinnington Road, Stockport. Until that date, all correspondence may continue to be sent to Unit 7 or to my email address above, whichever you find most convenient.

I would be most thankful if you could kindly confirm receipt of this notice in writing at your earliest convenience, and let me know if there is any further document or signature you require from us. I should hate for any technicality to cause a difficulty, so please do not hesitate to point out anything at all that you feel is missing.

With renewed thanks and very best wishes to the whole team,

Chiara Iyer

Section 4: Terms and Conditions of Carriage (Customer Edition)
Document reference: QF-FAQ-TC-04, Revision 12, effective 1 January 2024

A warm welcome from Quill Freight
Thank you most sincerely for choosing Quill Freight for your shipping needs. We are truly honoured by your trust, and we have prepared these frequently asked questions in the hope that they will make our Terms and Conditions of Carriage a little easier to understand. We would respectfully remind you that this FAQ is a summary only; in the unlikely event of any difference between this document and the full Terms and Conditions of Carriage (reference QF-TC-2024), the full Terms will prevail. We are always delighted to answer any further questions, so please do not hesitate to contact our Customer Contracts team at contracts@quillfreight.example.

4.1 Who is the contract between?
We are grateful for the opportunity to clarify this point. When you book a consignment with us, a contract of carriage is formed between Quill Freight Ltd (the "Carrier") and the person or organisation named as the shipper on the booking (the "Customer"). Where a booking is made by an agent or freight forwarder on a customer's behalf, the agent is treated as having authority to accept these Terms on the customer's behalf. We kindly ask agents to ensure their principals are aware of these Terms.

4.2 When does your responsibility for my goods begin and end?
Thank you for asking. Our responsibility begins when our driver or depot staff sign for the goods on collection or on drop-off at one of our depots, and ends when the goods are delivered to the consignee's address shown on the booking and a signature or electronic proof of delivery is obtained. If the consignee has authorised us in writing to leave goods in a safe place, our responsibility ends once the goods are left at that place.

4.3 Which items are you unable to carry?
We are so sorry that there are some items we cannot accept for carriage under any circumstances. For the safety of our staff, the public and other customers' goods, the following items are strictly prohibited on all Quill Freight services:
- Explosives of any kind, including fireworks, flares and ammunition
- Live animals, including insects, fish and livestock
- Cash, banknotes, coins and other forms of legal tender, as well as bearer bonds
- Firearms, replica firearms and weapon components
- Human remains, including ashes
- Controlled drugs and substances
If a prohibited item is found in a consignment, we will, with our apologies, hold the consignment and contact you. Any costs of return or disposal will be charged to the Customer.

4.4 Are there items you can carry only under special conditions?
Yes, and thank you for checking before you ship. The following items are accepted only where the stated conditions are met:
- Lithium batteries: accepted when packed in accordance with our Dangerous Goods Guide and accompanied by a completed battery declaration form.
- Chilled and frozen foodstuffs: accepted only on our Temperature-Controlled service, booked at least 48 hours in advance.
- Fine art and antiques: accepted when a declared value is provided and our Enhanced Cover option is purchased.
- Alcohol: accepted for business-to-business shipments only, with the Customer holding any necessary licences.
- Aerosols and flammable liquids: accepted in limited quantities as set out in the Dangerous Goods Guide.
We very much appreciate your help in following these conditions, which keep everyone safe.

4.5 How much will you pay if my goods are lost or damaged?
We are deeply sorry if this ever happens to you. Under our standard terms, our liability for loss or damage is limited to £20 per kilogram of the gross weight of the goods lost or damaged, subject to a maximum of £10,000 per consignment. Where you have purchased our Enhanced Cover option and declared a value on the booking, our liability is limited to the declared value, up to a maximum of £50,000 per consignment. We are not liable for indirect or consequential loss, such as loss of profit or business, save where the law does not allow us to exclude it.

4.6 How long do I have to make a claim?
Thank you for asking this very important question. Please notify us of any visible damage or shortage on the delivery note at the time of delivery, and in any event in writing within 7 days of delivery. Concealed damage must be notified in writing within 14 days of delivery. A full written claim, with supporting documents such as invoices and photographs, must be submitted within nine months of the date of delivery, or, in the case of non-delivery, within nine months of the date on which the goods were collected. We are very sorry, but claims received after these periods cannot be accepted.

4.7 What documents should I include with a claim?
We would be most grateful if you could provide: the booking reference; a description of the goods and their packaging; a copy of the commercial invoice or other evidence of value; photographs of the damaged goods and packaging; and details of any salvage value. Our Claims team will do their utmost to review your claim within 30 days of receiving all documents.

4.8 Can I change or cancel a booking?
Of course, and we are always happy to help. Bookings may be amended or cancelled free of charge until 17:00 on the working day before collection. Cancellations made after that time, or when our driver attends and the goods are not ready, may incur a failed collection fee of £35 plus VAT. We hope you understand that this fee helps us cover the cost of the wasted journey.

4.9 When must I pay?
Thank you for your prompt attention to this. Account customers must pay invoices within 30 days of the invoice date. Non-account customers must pay at the time of booking. Where invoices remain unpaid after the due date, we may, with regret, charge interest at 4% per annum above the Bank of England base rate, and we may exercise a lien over goods in our possession until all sums owed are paid.

4.10 How are disagreements between us resolved?
We very much hope that you will never have cause for disagreement with us, but should any dispute arise, we would first warmly invite you to raise it with our Customer Contracts team, who will make every effort to resolve it informally within 28 days. If the matter cannot be resolved in that way, the Terms provide that the dispute shall be referred to and finally resolved by binding arbitration under the rules of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators, with a single arbitrator appointed by agreement or, failing agreement, by the President of that Institute. The seat of the arbitration shall be Manchester, and the language of the arbitration shall be English. By agreeing to the Terms, both parties waive the right to bring the dispute before the ordinary courts, except for applications for urgent interim relief or to enforce an arbitral award. We hope this provides reassurance that any disagreement will be dealt with fairly and efficiently.

4.11 Which law governs the contract?
Thank you for asking. The contract of carriage is governed by the law of England and Wales. Where the carriage is international and an international convention (such as the CMR Convention for road carriage) applies compulsorily, the provisions of that convention will prevail to the extent required.

4.12 Do you use subcontractors?
We are most grateful for your understanding that, to provide the best possible network coverage, we may subcontract all or part of the carriage to other carefully selected carriers. Where we do so, these Terms continue to apply, and Quill Freight remains responsible to you as though we had performed the carriage ourselves.

4.13 What happens if the goods cannot be delivered?
We are very sorry if this occurs. Our driver will leave a card and we will attempt delivery on the next working day. After two failed attempts, the goods will be returned to our nearest depot and held for up to 14 days while we contact you for instructions. Storage charges of £5 per pallet per day may apply after the first three days. If we do not receive instructions within 14 days, we may, with regret, return the goods to you at your cost.

4.14 Do you accept responsibility for delays?
Thank you for raising this. We make every effort to deliver on the date and within any time window booked, and we are genuinely sorry when things do not go to plan. However, unless you have purchased our Guaranteed Timed service, delivery dates are estimates only and we do not accept liability for delay. Where a Guaranteed Timed service fails, we will refund the premium paid for that service.

4.15 What is a "force majeure" event?
We are grateful for the chance to explain. A force majeure event is an event beyond our reasonable control, such as severe weather, road closures, industrial action affecting third parties, fire, flood or government action. We will not be liable for any failure or delay caused by such an event, but we will always do our best to keep you informed and to minimise disruption.

4.16 How do you handle my personal data?
We take your privacy very seriously indeed. We process personal data only for the purposes of performing the contract, meeting our legal obligations and, where you have agreed, sending you service updates. Full details are in our Privacy Notice, available on our website.

4.17 Where can I find the full Terms?
The full Terms and Conditions of Carriage are available on our website under "Legal", and a printed copy can be posted to you free of charge on request. We would be delighted to send one.

A closing word of thanks
Once again, thank you so very much for choosing Quill Freight. We hope these answers have been helpful, and we look forward to serving you. If there is anything at all we can do to make your experience better, we would be truly grateful to hear from you.

Quill Freight Ltd, Customer Contracts Team

The full Terms and Conditions of Carriage are available on our website under "Legal", and a printed copy can be posted to you free of charge on request. We would be delighted to send one.

A closing word of thanks
Once again, thank you so very much for choosing Quill Freight. We hope these answers have been helpful, and we look forward to serving you. If there is anything at all we can do to make your experience better, we would be truly grateful to hear from you.

Quill Freight Ltd, Customer Contracts Team

=== PART 4: DETAILS OF NOTICE ===
Dear colleagues at Copperleaf Freight,

I very much hope you are all keeping well, and I would like to begin by thanking you most warmly for the partnership our two companies have enjoyed since September 2022. Your drivers have always been courteous and your customer service team has been unfailingly kind in answering our many questions. It is therefore with genuine reluctance, and with the greatest respect, that I find myself writing to you in a more formal capacity today.

Please accept this submission as formal notice, given under clause 14.2 of the Master Services Agreement referenced above, that Brightwater Ceramics considers Copperleaf Freight to be in breach of the collection window service level set out in paragraph 3.1 of Schedule 2.

As you will be aware, paragraph 3.1 of Schedule 2 obliges Copperleaf Freight to collect our outbound consignments from our Leeds dispatch centre within the two-hour window agreed for each scheduled collection, and requires that no more than one scheduled collection in any calendar quarter be missed or collected outside its agreed window. I am very sorry to report that during the quarter from 1 April to 30 June 2024, five scheduled collections were not made within their windows. I have set these out below for your convenience, and I would be most grateful if your team would check them against your own records:

1. Tuesday 9 April 2024: window 08:00–10:00; vehicle arrived 13:25.
2. Thursday 25 April 2024: window 14:00–16:00; no vehicle attended; collection made the following morning.
3. Wednesday 15 May 2024: window 08:00–10:00; vehicle arrived 11:40.
4. Monday 3 June 2024: window 08:00–10:00; no vehicle attended; collection made 4 June.
5. Friday 21 June 2024: window 14:00–16:00; vehicle arrived 17:50, after our loading dock had closed.

On each occasion our dispatch staff telephoned your control room, and I would like to acknowledge that your controllers were always apologetic and did their very best to help. I would also like to make clear, so that there is no misunderstanding, that on none of these occasions were any of our goods damaged, lost or short-delivered; our concern relates entirely to the timing of collections. We have been very happy with the care your drivers take in handling our products, and we have no complaints about invoicing, which has always been accurate and timely.

The late and missed collections have, I am afraid, caused us real difficulties. Two of our major retail customers imposed penalties on us for late delivery of seasonal stock, and our warehouse team has had to work additional overtime to reschedule loading. I mention this not to be critical but simply so that you understand why we feel it necessary to put the matter on a formal footing.

In accordance with clause 14.2, we respectfully request that Copperleaf Freight remedy the breach within 30 days of the date of this notice, that is, by 21 August 2024. For the avoidance of any doubt, and with sincere apologies for the formality, we would be most grateful if you would kindly:

(a) provide us, within 14 days, with a written corrective action plan explaining the causes of the missed collections and the steps you will take to ensure that the collection window service level is met going forward;
(b) apply the service credits due under paragraph 2 of Schedule 3 for the quarter ending 30 June 2024, which, by our calculation of four collections in excess of the permitted one at 5% of the monthly charge each, amount to 20% of the monthly charge, to be credited against our next invoice; and
(c) arrange a governance review meeting under Schedule 5 between our operations team and your account management team at a mutually convenient date before 21 August 2024.

I would like to stress that we are not, at this stage, giving notice of termination, and we very much hope that it will never come to that. We value the relationship and would far prefer to work together to put things right. We are also not seeking any refund of the charges we have paid for the services, nor are we making any claim for the penalties imposed on us by our retail customers at this time, though we would respectfully reserve our rights in that respect. However, I am obliged to note, with regret, that under clause 14.3, if a material breach is not remedied within the cure period, the non-breaching party may terminate the Agreement by giving written notice, and we must reserve that right.

Thank you so very much for your time and attention to this matter. I would be delighted to discuss any aspect of it by telephone, and I look forward to hearing from you.

With kind regards and sincere thanks,

Hiro Rahman
Head of Supply Chain, Brightwater Ceramics Ltd

Please note that this automated confirmation acknowledges receipt only. It does not constitute an admission of breach or acceptance of any claim, and all of Copperleaf Freight's rights under the Agreement are reserved. Where the Agreement requires notices to be served in a particular manner, please ensure you have complied with those requirements in addition to using this portal.

Guidance for customers using this form:
- Notices of breach should identify the clause or schedule said to be breached and the facts relied upon.
- Where you request a remedy, please state clearly what you are asking us to do and by when.

- Our Contracts team is always very happy to discuss any notice by telephone before or after submission, and we warmly encourage you to get in touch.

LARKSPUR FOODS - CARRIER DAMAGE & TEMPERATURE CLAIMS POLICY (outbound + inbound LTL/FTL)
rev 4.2 / owner: Transport Ops / last edit by S. Tanaka-Holm

1. PURPOSE
this page explains how we handle claims agianst carriers and how customers claim agianst us when product arrives damaged, short, or out of temp. applies to all chilled + frozen lanes run by Larkspur Foods or our contracted carriers. does NOT apply to parcel (see parcel page), does not apply to export ocean containers (see intl page). if u are unsure which page applies ask transport ops before filing anything, dont guess.

2. WHO CAN FILE
- consignee (the customer receiving the goods) can file a customer claim against Larkspur.
- Larkspur transport ops files carrier claims against the carrier. customers never file directly against our carriers, even if the carrier name is on the BOL.
- sales reps can NOT file claims on behalf of customers. they can open a ticket and pass it to claims desk. a sales rep promising a refund on the phone is not a claim decision.
- 3rd party brokers acting for consignee need a signed letter of authority on file first.

3. FILING WINDOW
- claim must be filed within 7 calendar days of the delivery date shown on the signed POD. not the ship date, not the invoice date, the delivery date.
- day 1 = the day after delivery. so delivered on a monday, day 7 is the next monday.
- concealed damage (found after unwrapping) same 7 day rule, no extension. we used to allow 15 days for concealed damage in rev 3.x, that was removed in rev 4.0. old emails that mention 15 days are out of date.
- the only extension is if our claims portal was down, and ops posts a notice with new deadline. no portal outage notice was issued in the current period.

4. WHAT COUNTS AS A TEMPERATURE EXCURSION
- chilled lanes: set point 0 to 4 C. an excursion = reefer download or data logger shows product air above 4.0 C for MORE THAN 45 continuous minutes.
- frozen lanes: set point -18 C or colder. excursion = above -15.0 C for more than 30 continuous minutes.
- door-open spikes during unloading are excluded if under 20 min total.
- a single reading above threshold is not an excursion. a bunch of short spikes that each reset below threshold do not add up, the rule is continuous minutes.
- if the reefer unit log and our independent data logger disagree, the independent logger wins.

5. PAYABLE COMPONENTS (only when claim is APPROVED)
when a claim is approved the following can be reimbursed, each separately:
 a) product value at invoice price (not retail, not replacement cost)
 b) freight charge refund for the affected pallets, pro rata by pallet count
 c) disposal / destruction fee, only if destruction was ordered or approved by Larkspur QA in writing
 d) re-delivery cost if a replacement load is sent at customer request
none of these are payable on a denied claim. a denied claim pays zero, including disposal. customers sometimes destroy stock first and then ask for disposal fee, if the claim is denied the disposal cost stays with the customer.

6. EXCLUSIONS (claim is denied if any applies)
- E1 late filing (outside 7 days per s.3)
- E2 clean POD: consignee signed POD with no exception notation for visible damage. visible damage means stuff a person could see at the dock, crushed corners, leaking cases, broken wrap. concealed damage is not hit by E2.
- E3 shipper-packed pallet with no independent data logger, temperature claims only. (if Larkspur packed it we always put a logger, so E3 is mostly for co-packer and customer-return loads)
- E4 no excursion per s.4 (temperature claims)
- E5 product accepted at dock after its best-before date
- E6 short-ship claims where seal number on arrival matches seal on BOL AND piece count was signed as correct

7. DECISIONS + CODES
claims desk records one of: APPROVED / PARTIAL / DENIED / PENDING. PENDING must be resolved within 10 business days. codes on denial reference exclusion (E1..E6). goodwill credits issued by sales are tracked separately under GW- numbers and are NOT claims, they dont change a claim status. if a GW credit exists on the same order the claim can still be denied.

8. CARRIER RECOVERY
when a customer claim is approved, transport ops tries to recover from the carrier within 30 days. recovery success doesnt change what the customer gets. if customer claim is denied we usually dont chase the carrier, except where we think the carrier caused a loss we ate ourselves.

9. ESCALATION
customer can appeal a denial once, within 14 days of the denial notice, with NEW evidence. repeating the same argument isnt an appeal. appeals go to Head of Transport Ops. appeal outcomes are logged in Appendix B (not reproduced here, see sharepoint).

--------------------------
APPENDIX A - CLAIMS LOG EXTRACT, WEEK 11-12 (for training new claims desk staff; real cases, customer names shortened)

LF-2288
customer: Brenholt Grocers DC2
lane: chilled, FTL
delivered: Mar 2 (POD signed 06:40, notation 'ok')
claim filed: Mar 11
issue: customer says 3 pallets yogurt swollen lids found on Mar 9 during putaway
notes: concealed damage type issue. customer rep cited old 15-day window from a 2022 email. rev 4 is 7 days. Mar 2 + 7 = Mar 9 last day. filed Mar 11.
status: DENIED - E1
sales note: rep Harlan offered 'we'll sort it' on call, not a decision per s.2.

LF-2291
customer: Quayside Deli Supply
lane: chilled, LTL, Larkspur packed (logger S/N 55-0192 present)
delivered: Mar 5, POD notation 'warm to touch??'
claim filed: Mar 6
issue: temp. customer states product warm, requests product value + freight refund + disposal fee (they binned 2 pallets same day, no QA approval asked)
logger download: peak 5.1 C, above 4.0 C from 14:12 to 14:42 (30 min), then back to 3.6 C. second rise 4.3 C from 15:05 to 15:20 (15 min).
reefer unit log shows 'alarm 47 min' but independent logger wins per s.4.
assessment: longest continuous period above 4.0 = 30 min, below 45 min threshold. spikes dont add up.
status: DENIED - E4
finance: product value 0, freight refund 0, disposal 0 (also no written QA approval for destruction so disposal would fail anyway), re-delivery not requested.
GW-0417 goodwill credit 5% issued by sales to Quayside on same order. tracked separately, claim status unchanged.

LF-2294
customer: Mornbrook Catering
lane: frozen, FTL
delivered: Mar 8, POD signed clean, no notation
claim filed: Mar 9
issue: 6 cases of fish fillet crushed, cartons caved in on top layer, photos show visible crush from outside of wrap
assessment: visible damage, clean POD. E2 applies. customer argues driver rushed them, not an exception to E2.
status: DENIED - E2
appeal: customer said will appeal 'if they dont reconsider', no appeal received at time of extract.

LF-2297
customer: Tillery Farm Shop (customer return load)
lane: chilled, LTL, shipper packed by customer, no independent logger
received at our DC: Mar 10
claim filed: Mar 12 (this one is Larkspur claiming against carrier, internal)
issue: temp, reefer log shows 6 C for 70 min
assessment: E3 applies to temp claims on shipper-packed pallets without independent logger. reefer log alone not enough per our own rule, we apply it to ourselves too.
status: initially PENDING, then DENIED - E3 on Mar 14
carrier recovery: none attempted.

LF-2299 - NOT in this extract, opened Mar 15 (week 13), see next log.

summary line wk 11-12: claims opened 4, approved 0, partial 0, denied 4, pending 0. GW credits 1 (GW-0417).

training tips for new desk staff:
- read the POD notation first. 'warm to touch??' is a notation but it doesnt create an excursion, the logger decides.
- check the delivery date before anything else, E1 kills a lot of claims and saves time.
- never tell a customer disposal will be paid until the claim is approved AND QA ok'd destruction in writing.
- if the customer mentions a sales promise, log it but it changes nothing.
- goodwill credits = sales budget, not claims budget. dont mix them in reports.
- when in doubt, PENDING is fine, but close it within 10 business days.

questions on this page -> transport ops channel, not the claims inbox pls. claims inbox is for customer claims only.

candidates.description: Reimbursement of goods at invoice price. Example: 20 cases at $30 invoice = $600 paid back.
Pro-rata refund of freight charged for affected pallets. Example: 2 of 10 pallets affected, 20% of freight refunded.
Cost of destroying spoiled goods, paid back to the customer. Example: $150 landfill fee reimbursed.
Cost of sending a replacement load at customer request. Example: second truck billed to Larkspur.

notes: Longest continuous run above 4.0C = 14:12-14:42 = 30 min < 45 -> DENIED E4; denied claim pays nothing; GW-0417 credit is not a claim payment.

version 9 / effective jan 1 / sections 4-11 + Schedule R shown. sections 1-3 (definitions, account opening) omitted from this excerpt.

4. RENTAL PERIOD
4.1 rental period starts at gate-out time printed on the equipment interchange receipt (EIR) and ends at gate-in time on the return EIR.
4.2 daily rate is charged per started 24h block. so gate-out 09:00 mon and gate-in 10:00 wed = 3 blocks (not 2).
4.3 grace period: a return up to 2 hours after the end of the last full block that was pre-booked is not charged an extra block. grace applies only to the final block, and only if the renter pre-booked a fixed return date in the booking.
4.4 open-ended rentals (no fixed return date) get no grace period at all.

5. LATE RETURN
5.1 if equipment is returned after the booked return time plus any grace in 4.3, a late fee of 1.5x daily rate applies for each started 24h block of lateness.
5.2 late fee replaces, and is not in addition to, the normal daily rate for those blocks.
5.3 late fee is waived where Saltmarsh closed the return depot on the booked return day (public holiday or depot notice).

6. CONDITION ON RETURN
6.1 renter returns equipment in same condition as gate-out, fair wear and tear excepted.
6.2 fair wear and tear includes: scuffs under 10 cm, normal tire wear, dust, minor floor marks.
6.3 damage fee: assessed by depot inspector on the return EIR. no damage fee can be charged unless damage is recorded on the return EIR with photo reference. damage found later than gate-in is not chargable.
6.4 cleaning fee: flat 85 per unit where the inspector records 'residue', 'odour' or 'debris' on the return EIR.
6.5 reefer units: fuel fee charged at cost + 20% if genset fuel below 3/4 tank on return. fuel level recorded on EIR as fraction.

7. USE RESTRICTIONS
7.1 no sublease or loan of equipment to any third party. no exceptions, written consent from a depot manager doesnt override this, only the Saltmarsh legal team can approve and they dont.
7.2 no hazmat classes 1, 6.2 or 7 in any unit.
7.3 max gross weight as per plate on unit. overweight = fee 250 per incident if a weighbridge ticket shows it.
7.4 units may not leave the country of gate-out without a cross-border addendum.

8. PAYMENT
8.1 invoices due 30 days from invoice date.
8.2 overdue invoices accrue 1.5% per month.
8.3 a deposit may be held on the renter card, released within 10 business days of gate-in if no fees assessed.

9. TERMINATION BY SALTMARSH
Saltmarsh may terminate a rental and recall equipment on 24h notice if ANY of the following:
 9.1 an invoice is more than 45 days overdue
 9.2 renter breaches s.7 (sublease, prohibited hazmat, cross-border without addendum)
 9.3 renter provides false information in the booking (e.g. false company registration)
 9.4 equipment is reported stolen or involved in an insurance event and renter fails to report within 48h
termination for convenience is not available to Saltmarsh during a fixed-term booking.

10. TERMINATION BY RENTER
renter can end early by returning the unit. minimum charge = 1 block. no refund for prepaid blocks unused, unless unused blocks exceed 7, then 50% refund of those.

11. NOTICES / DISPUTES
fee disputes within 14 days of invoice to disputes@ (fictional adress on file). depot staff comments are not binding. an email from a depot clerk saying 'we will waive it' is not a waiver unless confirmed by billing in writing.

version 9 / effective jan 1 / sections 4-11 + Schedule R shown. sections 1-3 (definitions, account opening) omitted from this excerpt.

4. RENTAL PERIOD
4.1 rental period starts at gate-out time printed on the equipment interchange receipt (EIR) and ends at gate-in time on the return EIR.
4.2 daily rate is charged per started 24h block. so gate-out 09:00 mon and gate-in 10:00 wed = 3 blocks (not 2).
4.3 grace period: a return up to 2 hours after the end of the last full block that was pre-booked is not charged an extra block. grace applies only to the final block, and only if the renter pre-booked a fixed return date in the booking.
4.4 open-ended rentals (no fixed return date) get no grace period at all.

5. LATE RETURN
5.1 if equipment is returned after the booked return time plus any grace in 4.3, a late fee of 1.5x daily rate applies for each started 24h block of lateness.
5.2 late fee replaces, and is not in addition to, the normal daily rate for those blocks.
5.3 late fee is waived where Saltmarsh closed the return depot on the booked return day (public holiday or depot notice).

6. CONDITION ON RETURN
6.1 renter returns equipment in same condition as gate-out, fair wear and tear excepted.
6.2 fair wear and tear includes: scuffs under 10 cm, normal tire wear, dust, minor floor marks.
6.3 damage fee: assessed by depot inspector on the return EIR. no damage fee can be charged unless damage is recorded on the return EIR with photo reference. damage found later than gate-in is not chargable.
6.4 cleaning fee: flat 85 per unit where the inspector records 'residue', 'odour' or 'debris' on the return EIR.
6.5 reefer units: fuel fee charged at cost + 20% if genset fuel below 3/4 tank on return. fuel level recorded on EIR as fraction.

7. USE RESTRICTIONS
7.1 no sublease or loan of equipment to any third party. no exceptions, written consent from a depot manager doesnt override this, only the Saltmarsh legal team can approve and they dont.
7.2 no hazmat classes 1, 6.2 or 7 in any unit.
7.3 max gross weight as per plate on unit. overweight = fee 250 per incident if a weighbridge ticket shows it.
7.4 units may not leave the country of gate-out without a cross-border addendum.

8. PAYMENT
8.1 invoices due 30 days from invoice date.
8.2 overdue invoices accrue 1.5% per month.
8.3 a deposit may be held on the renter card, released within 10 business days of gate-in if no fees assessed.

9. TERMINATION BY SALTMARSH
Saltmarsh may terminate a rental and recall equipment on 24h notice if ANY of the following:
 9.1 an invoice is more than 45 days overdue
 9.2 renter breaches s.7 (sublease, prohibited hazmat, cross-border without addendum)
 9.3 renter provides false information in the booking (e.g. false company registration)
 9.4 equipment is reported stolen or involved in an insurance event and renter fails to report within 48h
termination for convenience is not available to Saltmarsh during a fixed-term booking.

10. TERMINATION BY RENTER
renter can end early by returning the unit. minimum charge = 1 block. no refund for prepaid blocks unused, unless unused blocks exceed 7, then 50% refund of those.

11. NOTICES / DISPUTES
fee disputes within 14 days of invoice to disputes@ (fictional adress on file). depot staff comments are not binding. an email from a depot clerk saying 'we will waive it' is not a waiver unless confirmed by billing in writing.

----------------------------------------

EIR gate-in: fri 09:31, fuel 3/4, inspector J. Okafor. notes: 'scuff LHS rear 6cm (pre-existing), floor clean, no residue, genset ok'. photos ref: PH-88121..88126 (condition record, no damage noted)
weighbridge: loaded out at 26.4 t, plate max 30.48 t

billing QA comments:
- gate-in 09:31 vs booked return 08:00 = 1h31m after. within the 2h grace for final block, fixed return booking, so no extra block and no late fee. first draft invoice wrongly added a late fee 1.5x, billing removed it.
- fuel 3/4 on return. 6.5 says fee if BELOW 3/4. exactly 3/4 is not below. no fuel fee.
- cleaning: EIR 'floor clean, no residue'. no cleaning fee.
- damage: scuff pre-existing, recorded at gate-out, and 6cm is fair wear anyway. no damage fee.

Esi replied 'ok understood, we wont'. GPS track shows unit stayed on Fischer Haulage routes tue-fri, only drops at customer sites on the booking.
- thu: Esi asked about hauling a class 3 flammable load (paint). 7.2 bans only 1, 6.2 and 7. depot said class 3 ok. load not actually carried per GPS/customer list, she moved food only.

BRIGHTWATER FREIGHT HUB - DANGEROUS GOODS ACCEPTANCE & SURCHARGE POLICY
doc DG-POL-07 / rev 11 / approved by Uma Castillo (DG safety lead) / questions to dg-desk
read the whole thing b4 quoting a customer. sales keeps quoting DG fees on stuff thats exempt, costs us deals.

1. SCOPE
applies to all road consolidations departing Brightwater hub (LTL groupage, dedicated FTL are covered under DG-POL-09 instead). covers acceptance, segregation, paperwork and surcharges. air and sea DG not covered, we dont do those.

2. DEFINITIONS (short)
- DG = dangerous goods as per the road DG regs, identified by UN number + class.
- LQ = limited quantity. inner packs under the LQ limit for that UN number, marked with LQ diamond. max 30 kg gross per package.
- EQ = excepted quantity. tiny amounts, EQ mark, max 1 kg / 1 L per package typically.
- 1.1.3.6 threshold = 'small load exemption'. total 'points' per vehicle under 1000 = no orange plates, no ADR driver cert needed. points = qty x multiplier for transport category (cat 1 x50, cat 2 x3, cat 3 x1, cat 4 x0).
- Section II lithium = lithium batteries packed in or with equipment, meeting sec II of packing instruction, lithium mark only, no class 9 label.

3. WHAT WE DONT ACCEPT AT ALL
- class 1 explosives (any division except 1.4S, see 3a)
- class 6.2 infectious substances
- class 7 radioactive
- any damaged or leaking DG package
- DG without a DG note / transport doc
3a. 1.4S (e.g. small arms cartridges, some airbag inflators) is accepted, but gets DG handling surcharge and must be booked 48h ahead.

4. SURCHARGES
4.1 DG handling surcharge: 45 per consignment for fully regulated DG (not LQ, not EQ, not sec II lithium).
4.2 ADR vehicle surcharge: 120 per consignment when the vehicle load of the shipment on its own takes points to 1000 or more, requiring plated vehicle + ADR driver. (we calculate per consignment for billing even though its really a vehicle thing, see 4.2a)
4.2a if a single consignment is under 1000 points but the hub combines it with others and the vehicle goes over, the customer is NOT charged 4.2. thats our planning cost.
4.3 segregation surcharge: 60 when the consignment itself contains 2 or more classes that must be segregated from each other per table 7 (e.g. class 3 flammable liquids with class 5.1 oxidisers). segregation from OTHER customers goods is our problem, no charge.
4.4 temp controlled DG (organic peroxides, self-reactive w/ control temp): 200. we rarely take these.
4.5 LQ and EQ: no DG surcharges of any kind under 4.1-4.4. LQ over 8 t gross per vehicle needs LQ vehicle marks, still no charge to customer.
4.6 Section II lithium: no surcharge. section I lithium (class 9 labelled) = fully regulated, 4.1 applies.

5. PAPERWORK
- DG note with UN number, proper shipping name, class, packing group, qty, tunnel code.
- LQ: no DG note needed for road, but we ask for a declaration on the CMR 'LQ' line so we can count tonnage.
- sec II lithium: no DG note, but lithium mark on package.
- missing docs = booking rejected at gate, no fee, customer rebooks.

6. BOOKING LEAD TIMES
- fully regulated DG: 24h
- 1.4S: 48h
- LQ / EQ / sec II: same as general cargo

7. SEGREGATION TABLE 7 (extract, for 4.3)
class 3 vs 5.1: segregate
class 8 vs 4.3: segregate
class 2.1 vs 5.1: segregate
class 3 vs 8: compatible (no segregation) in most cases
class 3 vs 9: compatible
class 8 vs 9: compatible

8. WORKED EXAMPLES (sales training)
ex A: customer ships 20 x 5L paint (UN1263, class 3, PG III, cat 3) as fully regulated, 100 L total. points 100 x 1 = 100. under 1000. charges: 4.1 = 45. no 4.2. no 4.3 (single class).
ex B: customer ships 1,200 L of UN1203 petrol (class 3, cat 2). points 1200 x 3 = 3600. charges: 4.1 = 45 + 4.2 = 120 = 165.
ex C: pool chemicals mixed load, class 5.1 oxidiser + class 3 solvent in same consignment: 4.1 + 4.3, + 4.2 if points >= 1000.
ex D: LQ aerosols, 600 kg: nothing. 0 surcharge.

9. CURRENT BOOKING FOR REVIEW (dg-desk queue, pasted by Zoltan Kowalski, ops planner)
booking BRW-44871, customer: Hollowmere Cleaning Supplies
collection mon, delivery tue, LTL groupage
lines:
 L1 - 40 cartons hand sanitiser gel, UN1170 ethanol solution, class 3, PG II, packed as LQ (500 ml bottles x 12 per carton, LQ diamond marked, 7.2 kg gross per carton). total 288 kg
 L2 - 16 cartons toilet descaler, UN1789 hydrochloric acid solution, class 8, PG III, packed LQ (1 L bottles x 12, LQ marked, 13.5 kg gross per carton). total 216 kg
 L3 - 6 cordless floor scrubbers with lithium ion battery installed, marked lithium mark, sec II per shipper declaration, no class 9 label
 L4 - 30 cartons microfibre cloths, not DG
total DG gross (LQ) 504 kg
shipper note on CMR: 'LQ 504 kg'. no DG note attached.

Zoltan comments: sales quoted 45 + 60 because 'two DG classes, acid and alcohol, gotta segregate'. customer disputing. also sales thinks the scrubbers need class 9 fee. I think the whole quote is wrong, pls confirm. hub will combine this with a Kovanda Chemicals fully regulated load of UN1203 petrol 1,100 L on the same trailer tue, which puts the trailer over 1000 pts. planning aware.

10. DG DESK RESPONSE (Uma Castillo, tue 08:10)
Zoltan - agree, quote wrong. L1 and L2 both LQ per s.2 (packs marked, cartons under 30 kg). per 4.5 LQ gets no surcharge under 4.1-4.4, that includes segregation, and anyway class 3 vs 8 is compatible per table 7. L3 is sec II lithium, 4.6 no surcharge, no class 9. L4 not DG. trailer going over 1000 is from the Kovanda petrol, 4.2a says Hollowmere not charged. no DG note needed for LQ on road, CMR LQ line fine. booking lead time normal. pls reissue quote with DG surcharges = 0. accept booking.

fyi for sales - common mistakes:
 1) seeing two class numbers and adding 4.3. check table 7 AND check whether its LQ.
 2) charging 4.2 because the truck went over 1000. only if THIS consignment does it by itself.
 3) treating any lithium as class 9. sec II isnt.
 4) quoting 45 on LQ. never.
rev history: rev 10 charged a flat 25 LQ admin fee, removed in rev 11 (this rev). old quotes with 25 LQ fee are wrong now.

11. RECORD KEEPING
DG desk keeps the booking, the DG note or LQ declaration, and the surcharge decision for 2 years. disputes on DG surcharges go to Uma, not sales mgmt. sales mgmt can give commercial discounts but cannot declare something non-DG or change a classification. any change to classification needs a new shipper declaration.

12. TRAINING
all sales staff do DG awareness module yearly. ops planners do full DG module every 2 yrs. hub gate staff check LQ markings on arrival, if an LQ diamond is missing the carton is held and treated as undeclared DG until the shipper confirms. a held carton gets no surcharge but may miss the trailer.
