OK. As promised, here's the spec sheet for the new match balls from Meridian Supply. They asked me to post it in full so people 'understand the product'. I've copied it word for word. Any typos are theirs. Any sarcasm afterward is mine.

=== BEGIN SPEC SHEET ===

MERIDIAN SUPPLY
Product Specification Sheet
Product: Meridian Strata 5 Match Ball
Document: MS-SPEC-0417 | Revision C
Category: Outdoor football, recreational and club level

1. OVERVIEW
The Meridian Strata 5 is a size 5 outdoor match ball designed for adult recreational leagues, club training and small-sided games on natural grass and third-generation artificial turf. It is engineered for consistent flight, durable surface wear and a soft first touch.

2. DIMENSIONS AND WEIGHT
- Size: 5
- Circumference: 68.5 to 69.5 cm
- Weight (dry, inflated to recommended pressure): 420 to 445 g
- Note: weight may vary slightly with humidity and panel stitching tolerances.

3. CONSTRUCTION
- Outer casing: thermally bonded polyurethane, 12-panel layout
- Backing: three-layer polyester/cotton laminate
- Bladder: butyl, with reinforced valve seat
- Seam type: thermally bonded (no external stitching)

4. INFLATION
- Recommended pressure: 0.7 to 0.9 bar (approximately 10 to 13 psi)
- Do not exceed 1.1 bar.
- Use a lubricated needle. Do not use a dry needle. A dry needle damages the valve, and the valve does not forgive.

5. PERFORMANCE
- Rebound tested at 20 degrees C onto steel plate from 2 m drop: within manufacturer's internal target range.
- Designed for reduced water uptake compared with the previous Meridian Strata 4 model.
- Note: This product has not been submitted for third-party certification and does not carry any governing-body quality mark. It is intended for recreational use.

6. SURFACES
- Natural grass: suitable
- Third-generation artificial turf: suitable
- Indoor hard court: not recommended
- Gravel/asphalt: not recommended; will void warranty

7. WARRANTY
- 12 months from date of purchase against manufacturing defects (seam separation, bladder failure not caused by puncture or over-inflation).
- Warranty does not cover cosmetic wear, punctures, dog bites, or use as a garden decoration.

8. CARE
- Clean with a damp cloth and mild soap.
- Store partially deflated in a cool, dry place.
- Do not leave in a car in direct sunlight.
- Do not use on surfaces listed as 'not recommended' in Section 6.

9. PACKAGING
- Supplied deflated in retail box.
- Case quantity: 10 balls per case.
- Needle not included.

10. ORDERING
- Product code: MS-STR5-WHT (white/teal colourway), MS-STR5-ORG (high-visibility orange)
- Contact your Meridian Supply account representative for pricing and availability.

=== END SPEC SHEET ===

So there you go. It's round. It's size 5. It has a warranty. It may not be left in a car. The needle is not included, which I found out when I tried to inflate one and ended up blowing into the valve like a lunatic.

IN THE COUNTY COURT OF MARLOW COUNTY, CIVIL DIVISION

SVEN RAHMAN,
Plaintiff,
v.
BRIGHTWATER MOTORS LLC, d/b/a Brightwater Kestrel of Marlow,
Defendant.

Case No. 24-CV-03817

DEFENDANT BRIGHTWATER MOTORS LLC'S RESPONSE TO PLAINTIFF'S MOTION FOR PARTIAL SUMMARY JUDGMENT, WITH INCORPORATED STATEMENT OF POSITION ON REQUESTED RELIEF

(Excerpt: Sections I through VII, Exhibit C, and Certificate of Service)

May it please the Court:

Defendant Brightwater Motors LLC ('Brightwater' or 'Defendant'), by and through its undersigned counsel, most respectfully submits this Response to the Motion for Partial Summary Judgment filed by Plaintiff Sven Rahman ('Plaintiff' or 'Mr. Rahman'). Defendant wishes at the outset to extend its sincere gratitude to the Court for its patience in granting the brief extension requested on March 29, and to thank Plaintiff and his counsel for their unfailing courtesy throughout discovery. Defendant is keenly aware that Mr. Rahman has been a loyal customer of the dealership, having purchased two prior vehicles from it, and Defendant would like the Court to know that nothing in this Response is intended to diminish the genuine regret the dealership feels about the difficulties Mr. Rahman experienced. Defendant simply and humbly asks that the Court consider the record as a whole.

I. INTRODUCTION

This matter arises from Plaintiff's purchase, on September 14 of last year, of a new Kestrel TR-400 pickup truck in the Trailhand trim, equipped with the 3.2-liter engine (the 'Vehicle'). Plaintiff alleges that he was told the Vehicle could tow up to 7,500 pounds, that he relied on that representation in purchasing a travel trailer, and that the Vehicle's transmission overheated and failed on October 22 while he was towing that trailer on the Hollis Pass grade. Plaintiff seeks rescission of the purchase, refund of certain fees and add-on charges, reimbursement of diagnostic costs, punitive damages, and attorney fees.

Defendant would most respectfully note that the parties' disagreements are narrower than the pleadings might suggest. As set out in Section VI below, Defendant has, in the spirit of good faith and with the greatest respect for Mr. Rahman, elected not to contest several items of relief. Defendant does, however, continue to oppose certain other items, and it very politely asks the Court to deny summary judgment as to those.

II. STATEMENT OF UNDISPUTED FACTS (AS RESPONDED TO BY DEFENDANT)

Defendant responds to Plaintiff's numbered statement of facts as follows, and apologizes in advance for the length of certain responses, which it has tried to keep as brief as candor allows.

1. Plaintiff's Paragraph 1 (date of purchase). Admitted. The purchase agreement was executed on September 14.

2. Plaintiff's Paragraph 2 (identity of Vehicle). Admitted. The Vehicle is a Kestrel TR-400, Trailhand trim, 3.2-liter engine, four-wheel drive, with a 6.5-foot bed. Defendant would gently add that it is not disputed by either party that the Vehicle was not equipped with the optional Max Tow Package at the time of sale, and that no such package was installed at any time afterward.

3. Plaintiff's Paragraph 3 (salesperson). Admitted that the transaction was handled by sales consultant Mr. Oren Pellwood, who has been with Brightwater for eleven years and who, Defendant would respectfully mention, has asked counsel to convey his personal apologies to Mr. Rahman for any confusion.

4. Plaintiff's Paragraph 4 (window sticker). Denied. Defendant denies that its salesperson failed to provide the Monroney window sticker. The sticker was affixed to the Vehicle on the lot and a copy was placed in the deal jacket; Plaintiff's own initials appear on the delivery checklist line reading 'Window sticker reviewed with customer.' Defendant most humbly submits that this fact is not reasonably in dispute.

5. Plaintiff's Paragraph 5 (the brochure). Admitted in part. Defendant admits that the 2024 TR-400 general sales brochure displayed in the showroom states that the TR-400 line 'tows up to 7,500 lbs.' Defendant respectfully notes that the same page of the brochure carries a footnote reading 'When properly equipped. See dealer for trim-specific ratings.' Defendant does not ask the Court to decide at this stage whether that footnote was adequate, and it is grateful for the opportunity to address the point at trial if the Court should wish.

6. Plaintiff's Paragraph 6 (the revised specification sheet). Defendant would very respectfully respond as follows. In August of last year, the manufacturer, Kestrel Truck Company, issued a revised trim-specific specification sheet for the TR-400 (the 'Revised Sheet,' attached as Exhibit C). Defendant does not dispute that it did not furnish the Revised Sheet to Plaintiff prior to the execution of the purchase agreement on September 14. Defendant's records reflect that the Revised Sheet was received by the dealership's sales office on August 30 but had not yet been distributed to the sales floor binders at the time of Plaintiff's purchase. Defendant regrets this lapse most sincerely.

7. Plaintiff's Paragraph 7 (the trailer). Admitted that Plaintiff purchased, from an unrelated seller, a travel trailer with a manufacturer's dry weight of 5,400 pounds. Defendant would kindly note that Plaintiff's own weigh-station ticket of October 22, produced in discovery, reflects a loaded trailer weight of 6,200 pounds.

8. Plaintiff's Paragraph 8 (transmission failure). Admitted that the Vehicle's transmission overheated on October 22 and that the Vehicle was towed to Brightwater's service department on October 23.

9. Plaintiff's Paragraph 9 (diagnostic charge). Admitted that Plaintiff was charged a diagnostic fee of $310.00 on October 24, and that Plaintiff paid it.

10. Plaintiff's Paragraph 10 (warranty denial). Admitted that the manufacturer's warranty administrator declined coverage on the ground that the Vehicle had been operated above its rated towing capacity. Defendant takes no position on the correctness of the manufacturer's decision and would not wish to be understood as endorsing it.

11. Plaintiff's Paragraph 11 (dealer add-ons). Admitted that the purchase agreement included a 'Brightwater Protection Bundle' (paint sealant, interior fabric guard, nitrogen-filled tires and wheel locks) priced at $1,450.00.

12. Plaintiff's Paragraph 12 (late fee). Admitted that a late fee of $75.00 was assessed on Plaintiff's November payment through Brightwater's in-house finance arm, during the period when the Vehicle was out of service.

III. THE MANUFACTURER'S RATINGS

Defendant would most respectfully direct the Court's attention to Exhibit C, the Revised Sheet. Defendant appreciates that specification sheets are not the most engaging reading, and it thanks the Court in advance for its forbearance.

The Revised Sheet lists four configurations of the TR-400. Defendant has reproduced the relevant table below. Only one of these configurations corresponds to the Vehicle. Defendant would note, with respect, that the 7,500-pound figure appearing in the brochure corresponds to the Trailhand trim only when the Max Tow Package is installed, and that the 8,900-pound figure sometimes discussed in online forums corresponds to the Summit trim with the 3.8-liter engine, which the Vehicle is not.

IV. ARGUMENT: GENUINE DISPUTES OF MATERIAL FACT REMAIN AS TO RELIANCE

Defendant would most humbly submit that summary judgment on Plaintiff's misrepresentation count is not appropriate because the record contains conflicting evidence regarding what Mr. Pellwood said to Plaintiff. Mr. Pellwood's deposition testimony is that, when Plaintiff asked about towing, Mr. Pellwood said 'the TR-400 can do up to seventy-five hundred, but I'd want to check the exact number for this one.' Plaintiff's testimony is that Mr. Pellwood said 'this truck does seventy-five hundred, no problem.' Defendant does not suggest that either witness is being anything other than honest; memories of conversations fade, and Defendant has the greatest respect for Mr. Rahman's recollection. But the difference is material, and Defendant respectfully submits that a fact-finder should be permitted to weigh it.

Defendant would further note, with apologies for belaboring the point, that the question of reliance is complicated by the fact that the loaded trailer weight of 6,200 pounds would have exceeded the Vehicle's rating whether or not Plaintiff had been told 7,500 pounds; it is the rating itself, not the conversation, that governs the warranty question. Defendant raises this not to shift blame to Plaintiff, which it would never wish to do, but because the causal chain is a matter for trial.

V. ARGUMENT: PLAINTIFF'S RESCISSION CLAIM IS NOT RIPE FOR SUMMARY DISPOSITION

Defendant most respectfully opposes Plaintiff's request for full rescission of the purchase agreement at this stage. The purchase price of $48,960.00 was financed in part through a third-party lender, Coastline Auto Credit, which is not a party to this action. (D) Goodwill transmission replacement. Although Plaintiff has not requested this as relief, Defendant wishes the Court to be aware that it replaced the transmission at no charge on January 9, and that it does not now seek, and will not in the future seek, any payment for that work.

(E) Full rescission of the purchase agreement. Defendant opposes this request for the reasons set out in Section V. Defendant would not be unwilling to discuss a negotiated trade-in arrangement, but it cannot, with respect, consent to rescission at this stage.

(F) Punitive damages. Defendant opposes this request. Defendant most respectfully submits that nothing in the record would permit a finding of malice or reckless indifference; the failure to distribute the Revised Sheet was an administrative oversight, which Defendant has candidly acknowledged.

(G) Attorney fees. Defendant opposes Plaintiff's request for attorney fees in the amount claimed ($22,800.00). Defendant does not suggest that Plaintiff's counsel's hours were anything other than genuinely incurred, but it respectfully submits that fees are not recoverable under the counts on which summary judgment is sought.

VII. CONCLUSION

For the foregoing reasons, Defendant Brightwater Motors LLC most respectfully requests that the Court (1) enter judgment in Plaintiff's favor as to items (A), (B) and (C) of Section VI, to which Defendant consents; (2) deny Plaintiff's Motion as to items (E), (F) and (G); and (3) set the remaining issues for trial at the Court's earliest convenience. Defendant once more thanks the Court for its time and consideration.

Respectfully submitted,

Dalia Kaur
Kaur & Whitfield, Attorneys at Law
Counsel for Defendant Brightwater Motors LLC

Dear Valued Kestrel Retail Partner,

Thank you so very much for your continued partnership. Worksite trim: 2.7-liter inline-four turbo, 270 hp, 8-speed automatic, rear-wheel drive standard, four-wheel drive optional.

Summit trim: 3.8-liter V6 twin-turbo, 400 hp, 10-speed automatic, four-wheel drive standard.

Configuration | Max Trailer Weight | Max Tongue Weight | Payload | GCWR
Worksite 2.7L | 4,200 lbs | 420 lbs | 1,640 lbs | 9,300 lbs

We would be most grateful if retail partners would assist customers in confirming whether a given vehicle carries the Max Tow Package. #1 chiara_mensah_boxoffice (Box Office Manager, Harbourline Museum of Maritime History)

Hi all. Long-time lurker, occasional poster, currently sitting in the back office with a cold coffee and a stack of printouts that is genuinely taller than my stapler, so forgive me if this rambles. It's going to ramble. I'm making one big thread instead of six little ones because honestly everything is tangled together and every time I try to explain one problem to someone I end up explaining three others, so here's everything in one place and people can reply to whichever bit they know about.

Context for the newer folks: we're a mid-sized maritime museum, about 180k visitors a year on a good year, a main hall plus the dry-dock gallery plus the lightship you can walk through (the lightship is timed entry because it's tiny and the fire marshal has opinions). We've been on Copperleaf Gate, the hosted version, for about two and a half years. Card payments go through Granite Labs as the processor. We have a membership program, a schools program, a corporate partner program, and the timed-entry lightship tickets. It all mostly works. Mostly. This autumn it did not mostly work.

The list, roughly in the order they exploded:

1. Member upgrade refunds going out twice. Like, somebody upgrades from Individual to Family, we refund the unused portion of the Individual membership, and the refund goes out two times. Our finance person noticed because the reconciliation was off by a weird amount.

2. The Brookfield school group thing in October, where the teacher got an email saying the booking was cancelled and then called us in an absolute state. I'll explain below.

3. Tidewater Health, our biggest corporate partner, whose employee passes started getting rejected at the gate in March and who have now, and I'm not joking, filed an actual court complaint. I have the excerpt. I'll paste the relevant bits.

4. When the clocks changed in the autumn, the lightship timed-entry slots for the Sunday shifted by an hour in the confirmation emails. People showed up at the wrong time. Chaos on the gangway.

5. Granite Labs payouts being slow in November.

6. Companion tickets for access-needs visitors (the free carer ticket) suddenly charging the full adult price for about a week.

And on top of all this our development director Yara is writing a grant application to the Coastal Heritage Foundation for new ticketing hardware and she wants numbers from me, and I keep sending her numbers, and then the numbers change because of all the refund reversals. So I'll paste the draft section she sent me too because people on here have asked before about how others word these things.

OK. Deep breath. Detail follows in the next few posts.

#2 chiara_mensah_boxoffice

Item 1, the double refunds.

So this started in late September. Our membership coordinator processes an upgrade the normal way: open the member record, click Upgrade, choose the new tier, and Copperleaf calculates a prorated credit for the old tier and a charge for the new tier. Normally you get one refund line and one charge line. What we were seeing is two refund lines, same amount, a few seconds apart, and BOTH of them actually settling on the member's card. The member gets, say, $38.40 back twice and then pays the $120 Family price once.

We found 27 of these between 23 September and 18 October. Most members didn't notice, a handful emailed us being very nice about it ("I think you gave me too much money back?") and one emailed us being very suspicious about it ("is this a scam"). We've now clawed back most of them by asking nicely, and just written off the rest because honestly chasing a retired schoolteacher for $22 is not a good look.

I opened a support case with Copperleaf, CL-7741. I will let the Copperleaf person answer for themselves because I believe one of their support folks is on this forum, but to be clear up front: our coordinator did NOT click the button twice. We checked this because it was the first thing everyone asked. We screen-recorded her doing one upgrade on a test member and it produced two refund lines from one click.

#4 chiara_mensah_boxoffice

@jonas_delgado_ops yes we checked the dropdown, it was correctly on "Refund - prorated membership credit". One click, two lines. We have the video. Anyway.

Item 2, the Brookfield school group. This one I want to lay out carefully because the story has been retold in our building so many times that people now believe totally different versions of it, and one of our trustees at the last meeting said "the school cancelled on us and then complained," which is NOT what happened, and I want it written down properly somewhere.

The booking was SG-2291. Brookfield Middle School, teacher lead Aiden O'Neill, 62 students plus 6 adults, originally booked for Tuesday 14 October, the "Ships and Storms" guided program in the morning then the lightship in the afternoon.

Around 7 October, Mr O'Neill emailed our schools inbox. I have the email. The relevant bit is:

> "Hi, there's a bus drivers' strike threatened for the week of the 13th. If we can't get buses we'll have to cancel altogether, which I really don't want to do, the kids have been looking forward to it for weeks. Is there any chance of moving us to the following Tuesday, the 21st, instead? Same program, same numbers."

Note "if we can't get buses we'll have to cancel". He did not cancel. He asked to move it. Tomasz on our schools desk replied the same day saying yes, the 21st was open, and he'd move it.

Tomasz then went into Copperleaf, opened SG-2291, and used the "Change date" function to move it from 14 Oct to 21 Oct. That's the normal way to do it. It's not a cancel-and-rebook, it's an edit of the same booking — same booking number, same deposit, same everything, just a new date.

And then, a few minutes later, Mr O'Neill received an automated email from our system with the subject line "Your booking SG-2291 has been cancelled" and body text saying the booking was cancelled and any deposit would be refunded within 10 business days.

He, very reasonably, lost his mind a bit. He called the front desk, got our weekend person who didn't know anything, and the weekend person looked at the screen, saw the booking was for the 21st, and said "it's showing as booked for the 21st?" and Mr O'Neill said "then why did you send me a cancellation" and nobody could answer him.

Tomasz called him back first thing Monday, apologised, sent a manual confirmation for the 21st, and... the group came on the 21st. All 62 kids. I was there. They loved the lightship, one kid threw up on the gangway, it was a normal school visit. The deposit was never refunded because nothing was ever cancelled — the booking status in Copperleaf has said "Confirmed — Rescheduled" the whole time, and the audit log for SG-2291 shows one event: "date_changed 2025-10-14 -> 2025-10-21 by t.castillo". There's no "cancelled" event in the log at all.

So to be very clear for anyone skimming: nobody cancelled SG-2291. Not the school, not us, not the system. It was moved. The system just sent the wrong email template.

Separately, and this is where the trustee's version comes from I think, a DIFFERENT school did actually cancel on us that same week. SG-2288, St. Brigid's Primary, 30 kids, booked for Thursday 16 October. Their head teacher emailed on 9 October saying they were cancelling due to the strike and weren't going to reschedule this term. Tomasz processed that as a real cancellation, deposit refunded per policy. So there WAS a school that cancelled because of the strike, it just wasn't Brookfield. I think people merged the two in their heads.

#7 chiara_mensah_boxoffice

Item 3. Tidewater Health. This is the big one, the one with lawyers, and I'm going to paste a lot of text so bear with me. Our general counsel said it's fine to share the excerpt since it's a public filing and our side hasn't said anything that isn't already in it, but I've trimmed the boring procedural parts.

Background: Tidewater Health is a regional healthcare company, and they've been a corporate partner for years. Every year they buy a batch of employee passes that their staff can use for free general admission. Last year's batch: 400 passes. The order was placed and the contract signed on 15 March 2024. They paid the invoice on 22 March 2024. The first pass from the batch was scanned at our gate on 2 April 2024 — I know this date because it was the first nice weekend and a Tidewater nurse came with her twins and we took a photo for our corporate newsletter.

Then in March 2025, the passes started getting rejected at the gate. Specifically from 16 March 2025 onwards, any Tidewater pass scanned showed "EXPIRED" in red. Between about 16 March and the end of March a bunch of Tidewater employees were turned away, some of them with kids, some of them having driven an hour, and it got really ugly, and Tidewater's HR people were furious, and our front-of-house staff were caught in the middle.

Why did they expire on 16 March? Because when the batch was set up in Copperleaf back in March 2024, whoever set it up (I think it was a temp we had covering maternity leave) configured the expiry rule as "purchase date + 365 days". Purchase date 15 March 2024 plus 365 days is 15 March 2025, so the passes were valid through 15 March and dead on the 16th.

The question, which is the whole lawsuit, is: when were they supposed to expire?

Here is the excerpt from the filing.

---

BEGIN EXCERPT

IN THE COUNTY COURT, CIVIL DIVISION

TIDEWATER HEALTH, INC., Plaintiff,
v.
HARBOURLINE MUSEUM OF MARITIME HISTORY, a nonprofit corporation, Defendant.

COMPLAINT FOR BREACH OF CONTRACT AND DECLARATORY RELIEF (EXCERPT)

...

FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS

7. On or about March 15, 2024, Plaintiff and Defendant entered into a written Corporate Partner Admission Agreement (the "Agreement"), a true and correct copy of which is attached hereto as Exhibit A.

8. Under the Agreement, Plaintiff purchased four hundred (400) employee admission passes (collectively, the "Batch" and each a "Pass") for a total consideration of Eighteen Thousand Dollars ($18,000.00), which Plaintiff paid in full on or about March 22, 2024.

9. Plaintiff distributed the Passes to its employees in the ordinary course. Individual employees began using the Passes on various dates, the earliest known use occurring on or about April 2, 2024, and many employees not using their Passes for the first time until the autumn or winter of 2024.

10. Beginning on or about March 16, 2025, Defendant's admission system began rejecting Passes as "expired," and Defendant's staff refused admission to Plaintiff's employees and their family members on no fewer than forty-one (41) documented occasions between March 16, 2025 and March 31, 2025.

11. Plaintiff contends that, under the Agreement, each Pass remains valid for three hundred sixty-five (365) days from the date on which that individual Pass is first used, such that Passes first used in, for example, November 2024 remain valid until November 2025.

12. Defendant has taken the position, in correspondence dated April 9, 2025, that the Passes expire on a single date applicable to the entire Batch. Plaintiff disputes Defendant's position.

...

EXHIBIT A — CORPORATE PARTNER ADMISSION AGREEMENT (RELEVANT EXCERPTS)

Section 3. Passes.
3.1 The Museum shall issue to the Partner the number of employee admission passes stated in Schedule 1 (the "Batch"). Each pass (a "Pass") entitles one named or unnamed bearer to one general admission per visit, subject to capacity.
3.2 Passes are non-transferable outside the Partner's workforce and the immediate household members of the Partner's employees.

Section 4. Validity.
4.1 The Batch shall be valid for three hundred sixty-five (365) days from the date of first redemption of any Pass in the Batch (the "Validity Period"). Upon expiry of the Validity Period, all Passes in the Batch shall expire, whether or not individually redeemed.
4.2 For the avoidance of doubt, the date of purchase, the date of this Agreement, and the date of payment shall not be used to calculate the Validity Period.
4.3 The Museum may, at its sole discretion, extend the Validity Period in writing.

Section 5. Fees.
5.1 The Partner shall pay the fee stated in Schedule 1 within thirty (30) days of invoice.

Schedule 1.
Number of Passes: 400
Fee: $18,000.00 ($45.00 per Pass)
Date of Agreement: 15 March 2024

END EXCERPT

---

So. You can see why everyone is annoyed with everyone.

Our counsel's read (and mine, for what it's worth, though I am a box office manager and not a lawyer) is that 4.1 is pretty clear it's a batch-wide date, running from the first redemption of ANY pass. First redemption of any pass was 2 April 2024. Tidewater's read in paragraph 11 is that each pass gets its own year from its own first use, which is... not what 4.1 says, and 4.1 even says "whether or not individually redeemed". But the system had them expiring on 15 March based on the purchase date, which 4.2 specifically says you can't use. So we are wrong about the date our system used, and they are wrong about how it works, and the truth is somewhere in the middle, and meanwhile 41 families got turned away, which is awful regardless.

I've asked our counsel whether we should just exercise 4.3 and extend everything to make peace, but that's above my pay grade.

COASTAL HERITAGE FOUNDATION — CAPACITY BUILDING GRANT, 2026 CYCLE
Applicant: Harbourline Museum of Maritime History
Section C: Statement of Need — Visitor Access and Ticketing Infrastructure

C.1 Summary of need

Harbourline welcomes approximately 180,000 visitors per year across its Main Hall, Dry-Dock Gallery, and the historic Lightship Corrigan, a decommissioned 1952 lightvessel accessible through timed entry. Since 2023 the museum has used a hosted ticketing platform for general admission, membership, schools and group bookings, and corporate partner programs. While the platform has enabled online sales (which rose from 31% of transactions in FY2023 to 58% in FY2025), the museum's on-site hardware — handheld scanners, receipt printers, and two ageing kiosks — has not kept pace. We are requesting $64,500 to replace on-site hardware, fund integration work, and train frontline staff.

C.2 The problem

Frontline staff currently rely on six handheld scanners, of which two are out of warranty and one has a cracked screen. On peak days, queues at the Lightship gangway exceed 25 minutes. Our two self-service kiosks were installed in 2016 and can no longer run the current version of the ticketing client; they are presently used only to display wayfinding maps.

In addition, the past year has highlighted the need for better staff training and clearer configuration practices around complex products such as corporate partner batches and timed entry. Several visitor-facing incidents in 2024–2025 were traced to how products were set up rather than to hardware failures, and a portion of our request (see C.4) addresses configuration training so that validity rules, pricing tiers, and communication templates are set up consistently and reviewed by a second staff member.

C.3 Who is affected

Our visitors include approximately 14,000 schoolchildren per year through our schools program, over 3,200 member households, and employees of corporate partners. Visitors with access needs, and their companions, represent a growing share of our audience; companion admission is free under our access policy, and it is essential that our systems apply this consistently at the point of sale.

C.4 Proposed solution and budget

- Replacement handheld scanners (8 units): $12,800
- Two new self-service kiosks with accessible height and screen readers: $31,000
- Receipt/ticket printers (4 units): $3,200
- Integration and configuration consultancy (40 hours): $9,000
- Frontline and back-office staff training, including configuration review: $6,500
- Contingency: $2,000
Total: $64,500

C.5 Outcomes

By the end of the grant period we expect to reduce peak gangway queue times to under 10 minutes, bring kiosk usage back online for at least 20% of on-site walk-up sales, and establish a two-person review for all new product configurations.

#12 farid_okafor_copperleaf (Copperleaf Labs — Customer Support, verified vendor account)

Hi Chiara, hi everyone. Farid from Copperleaf Labs support here. I've been following this thread (a colleague flagged it to me) and I've got updates on all the Harbourline cases, so I'll go through them one by one. Apologies in advance, this will be long, and it's been a rough autumn for us too, though obviously not as rough as for the families at the gangway.

First, a caveat about what "confirmed" means when I say it: when I say a defect is confirmed, I mean our engineering team has reproduced it in our own environment and identified a root cause in our code. When I say something isn't a defect, I mean the system did what it was configured to do or the problem sits outside our platform.

CL-7741 (double prorated refunds on member upgrades): Confirmed defect. Our engineers reproduced it on 4.12.0 through 4.12.2. When a membership upgrade included a prorated credit, a retry handler in the refund service fired a second refund request after a slow acknowledgement from the processor, and the idempotency check wasn't applied to prorated credits specifically. So from one click you got two refund requests. Fixed in 4.12.3, which went out to all hosted customers on 21 October. Chiara, your coordinator did nothing wrong. We're also putting together a report of every affected transaction across all customers so finance teams can reconcile.

CL-7760 (date change on a group booking sends cancellation email): Confirmed defect. Tomasz's reproduction steps were spot on, thank you for those. In 4.12.0 we refactored the group booking notification logic and the "date_changed" event was mapped to the wrong template ID — it pointed to the cancellation template. The booking itself was never cancelled; only the notification was wrong. The booking data, deposit, and status were all untouched. This is fixed in 4.12.4 (released 3 November). For anyone on 4.11, this doesn't affect you.

CL-7788 (lightship timed-entry emails an hour off on the DST changeover Sunday): Confirmed defect. The email renderer was formatting the slot time using a cached UTC offset from the day before the changeover rather than the offset for the slot date. The ticket data and gate validation were correct, which matches what Chiara saw. We reproduced it with the October changeover date in our staging environment. Fix is scheduled for 4.13, and in the meantime we've added a hotfix that disables the cache on changeover dates, so the spring changeover shouldn't repeat this.

Now the other ones, which I know people have been lumping in with the above:

Tidewater Health pass expiry: I want to be careful here because I know there's litigation and I'm not going to comment on the contract. But from a platform point of view, this is not a Copperleaf defect. The Tidewater batch in your account was configured with the rule "expiry = purchase_date + 365d" by a user on your account on 15 March 2024. The system calculated 15 March 2025 and began rejecting on 16 March, which is exactly what that rule says to do. Copperleaf Gate does support a "first redemption in batch + N days" rule — it's in the dropdown as "Batch: from first scan" — so the rule you'd need for what Section 4.1 of your agreement describes was available, it just wasn't selected. I know some people on your team have called this "the Copperleaf expiry bug" in emails to us; respectfully, it isn't one. I'm happy to help you reconfigure it, and if your counsel decides to extend the batch under 4.3 we can do that in about five minutes.

Granite Labs payout delays in November: This is on the processor side, not ours. Granite Labs had a settlement batching change in early November that delayed payouts to a number of merchants by 2–4 business days. Our records show we sent your settlement files on time every day. I'd raise it with your Granite account manager. I know someone on your team called it "another Copperleaf bug" in a support chat, but it's outside our platform.

Companion tickets charging full adult price: We haven't been able to reproduce this and I don't currently believe it's a defect on our side. When we looked at your account, the "Companion — Access (Free)" price tier was deleted on 2 December by a user on your account, and during the period companion tickets were charging adult price, the POS was falling back to the default adult tier because the companion tier didn't exist. The tier was re-created on 9 December and it's been fine since. I'd suggest checking with your team who deleted it — it may have been a tidy-up of old tiers that caught the wrong one. If you can find a case where it happened while the tier existed, send it over and I'll escalate, but as it stands I can't call it confirmed.

So, to summarise from my side: three confirmed Copperleaf defects (7741, 7760, 7788), all either fixed or with a fix scheduled; and three issues that aren't Copperleaf defects (Tidewater expiry config, Granite payouts, companion tier deletion).

Again, really sorry for the mess this autumn. The double refunds and the cancellation template in particular should have been caught in our QA and weren't.

- 15 March 2025: last day the system accepted passes.
- 16 March 2025: system starts rejecting.
- 16–31 March 2025: 41 documented refusals.
- 9 April 2025: our counsel's letter to Tidewater.

I've heard in the building: "they expired on the 15th, that was correct" (no, 4.2 says you can't use the agreement/purchase date), "they should run to the 22nd" (no, same clause, payment date excluded), "each pass gets a year from its own first use" (that's Tidewater's argument in the complaint, and front-of-house repeated it on the phone, but it's not what 4.1 says — 4.1 says the Batch is valid for 365 days from the first redemption of any Pass, and all Passes expire at the end of that, whether or not individually redeemed).

So if you read 4.1 as written, it's 365 days from 2 April 2024. I counted it out on the calendar because I didn't trust myself: 2 April 2024 to 2 April 2025 is 365 days, since the 2024 leap day was back in February, before the start date, and 2025 isn't a leap year. So the batch ran to 2 April 2025. Which means the system cut people off about two and a half weeks early, and all 41 of those refusals happened when the passes were still valid under the contract. Which is bad for us. But it also means the passes weren't supposed to run until November 2025 or whenever for the late first-users, which is what Tidewater is asking for.

Our counsel is, I think, going to offer to extend under 4.3 as a goodwill gesture plus some compensation for the families. Fingers crossed that ends it.

Our general counsel said it's fine to share the excerpt since it's a public filing and our side hasn't said anything that isn't already in it, but I've trimmed the boring procedural parts.

Background: Tidewater Health is a regional healthcare company, and they've been a corporate partner for years. Every year they buy a batch of employee passes that their staff can use for free general admission. Last year's batch: 400 passes. The order was placed and the contract signed on 15 March 2024. They paid the invoice on 22 March 2024. The first pass from the batch was scanned at our gate on 2 April 2024 — I know this date because it was the first nice weekend and a Tidewater nurse came with her twins and we took a photo for our corporate newsletter.

Then in March 2025, the passes started getting rejected at the gate. Specifically from 16 March 2025 onwards, any Tidewater pass scanned showed "EXPIRED" in red. Between about 16 March and the end of March a bunch of Tidewater employees were turned away, some of them with kids, some of them having driven an hour, and it got really ugly, and Tidewater's HR people were furious, and our front-of-house staff were caught in the middle.

Why did they expire on 16 March? Because when the batch was set up in Copperleaf back in March 2024, whoever set it up (I think it was a temp we had covering maternity leave) configured the expiry rule as "purchase date + 365 days". Purchase date 15 March 2024 plus 365 days is 15 March 2025, so the passes were valid through 15 March and dead on the 16th.

The question, which is the whole lawsuit, is: when were they supposed to expire?

Here is the excerpt from the filing.

Hi Chiara, hi everyone. Farid from Copperleaf Labs support here. I've been following this thread (a colleague flagged it to me) and I've got updates on all the Harbourline cases, so I'll go through them one by one. Apologies in advance, this will be long, and it's been a rough autumn for us too, though obviously not as rough as for the families at the gangway.

First, a caveat about what "confirmed" means when I say it: when I say a defect is confirmed, I mean our engineering team has reproduced it in our own environment and identified a root cause in our code. When I say something isn't a defect, I mean the system did what it was configured to do or the problem sits outside our platform.

CL-7741 (double prorated refunds on member upgrades): Confirmed defect. Our engineers reproduced it on 4.12.0 through 4.12.2. When a membership upgrade included a prorated credit, a retry handler in the refund service fired a second refund request after a slow acknowledgement from the processor, and the idempotency check wasn't applied to prorated credits specifically. So from one click you got two refund requests. Fixed in 4.12.3, which went out to all hosted customers on 21 October. Chiara, your coordinator did nothing wrong. We're also putting together a report of every affected transaction across all customers so finance teams can reconcile.

CL-7760 (date change on a group booking sends cancellation email): Confirmed defect. Tomasz's reproduction steps were spot on, thank you for those. In 4.12.0 we refactored the group booking notification logic and the "date_changed" event was mapped to the wrong template ID — it pointed to the cancellation template. The booking itself was never cancelled; only the notification was wrong. The booking data, deposit, and status were all untouched. This is fixed in 4.12.4 (released 3 November). For anyone on 4.11, this doesn't affect you.

CL-7788 (lightship timed-entry emails an hour off on the DST changeover Sunday): Confirmed defect. The email renderer was formatting the slot time using a cached UTC offset from the day before the changeover rather than the offset for the slot date. The ticket data and gate validation were correct, which matches what Chiara saw. We reproduced it with the October changeover date in our staging environment. Fix is scheduled for 4.13, and in the meantime we've added a hotfix that disables the cache on changeover dates, so the spring changeover shouldn't repeat this.

Now the other ones, which I know people have been lumping in with the above:

Tidewater Health pass expiry: I want to be careful here because I know there's litigation and I'm not going to comment on the contract. But from a platform point of view, this is not a Copperleaf defect. The Tidewater batch in your account was configured with the rule "expiry = purchase_date + 365d" by a user on your account on 15 March 2024. The system calculated 15 March 2025 and began rejecting on 16 March, which is exactly what that rule says to do. Copperleaf Gate does support a "first redemption in batch + N days" rule — it's in the dropdown as "Batch: from first scan" — so the rule you'd need for what Section 4.1 of your agreement describes was available, it just wasn't selected. I know some people on your team have called this "the Copperleaf expiry bug" in emails to us; respectfully, it isn't one. I'm happy to help you reconfigure it, and if your counsel decides to extend the batch under 4.3 we can do that in about five minutes.

Granite Labs payout delays in November: This is on the processor side, not ours. Granite Labs had a settlement batching change in early November that delayed payouts to a number of merchants by 2–4 business days. Our records show we sent your settlement files on time every day. I'd raise it with your Granite account manager. I know someone on your team called it "another Copperleaf bug" in a support chat, but it's outside our platform.

Companion tickets charging full adult price: We haven't been able to reproduce this and I don't currently believe it's a defect on our side. When we looked at your account, the "Companion — Access (Free)" price tier was deleted on 2 December by a user on your account, and during the period companion tickets were charging adult price, the POS was falling back to the default adult tier because the companion tier didn't exist. The tier was re-created on 9 December and it's been fine since. I'd suggest checking with your team who deleted it — it may have been a tidy-up of old tiers that caught the wrong one. If you can find a case where it happened while the tier existed, send it over and I'll escalate, but as it stands I can't call it confirmed.

So, to summarise from my side: three confirmed Copperleaf defects (7741, 7760, 7788), all either fixed or with a fix scheduled; and three issues that aren't Copperleaf defects (Tidewater expiry config, Granite payouts, companion tier deletion).

Again, really sorry for the mess this autumn. The double refunds and the cancellation template in particular should have been caught in our QA and weren't.

Item 3. Tidewater Health. This is the big one, the one with lawyers, and I'm going to paste a lot of text so bear with me. Our general counsel said it's fine to share the excerpt since it's a public filing and our side hasn't said anything that isn't already in it, but I've trimmed the boring procedural parts.

Background: Tidewater Health is a regional healthcare company, and they've been a corporate partner for years. Every year they buy a batch of employee passes that their staff can use for free general admission. Last year's batch: 400 passes. The order was placed and the contract signed on 15 March 2024. They paid the invoice on 22 March 2024. The first pass from the batch was scanned at our gate on 2 April 2024 — I know this date because it was the first nice weekend and a Tidewater nurse came with her twins and we took a photo for our corporate newsletter.

Then in March 2025, the passes started getting rejected at the gate. Specifically from 16 March 2025 onwards, any Tidewater pass scanned showed "EXPIRED" in red. Between about 16 March and the end of March a bunch of Tidewater employees were turned away, some of them with kids, some of them having driven an hour, and it got really ugly, and Tidewater's HR people were furious, and our front-of-house staff were caught in the middle.

Why did they expire on 16 March? Because when the batch was set up in Copperleaf back in March 2024, whoever set it up (I think it was a temp we had covering maternity leave) configured the expiry rule as "purchase date + 365 days". Purchase date 15 March 2024 plus 365 days is 15 March 2025, so the passes were valid through 15 March and dead on the 16th.

The question, which is the whole lawsuit, is: when were they supposed to expire?

Here is the excerpt from the filing.

So. You can see why everyone is annoyed with everyone.

Our counsel's read (and mine, for what it's worth, though I am a box office manager and not a lawyer) is that 4.1 is pretty clear it's a batch-wide date, running from the first redemption of ANY pass. First redemption of any pass was 2 April 2024. Tidewater's read in paragraph 11 is that each pass gets its own year from its own first use, which is... not what 4.1 says, and 4.1 even says "whether or not individually redeemed". But the system had them expiring on 15 March based on the purchase date, which 4.2 specifically says you can't use. So we are wrong about the date our system used, and they are wrong about how it works, and the truth is somewhere in the middle, and meanwhile 41 families got turned away, which is awful regardless.

Hi Chiara, hi everyone. Farid from Copperleaf Labs support here. I've been following this thread (a colleague flagged it to me) and I've got updates on all the Harbourline cases, so I'll go through them one by one. Apologies in advance, this will be long, and it's been a rough autumn for us too, though obviously not as rough as for the families at the gangway.

First, a caveat about what "confirmed" means when I say it: when I say a defect is confirmed, I mean our engineering team has reproduced it in our own environment and identified a root cause in our code. When I say something isn't a defect, I mean the system did what it was configured to do or the problem sits outside our platform.

CL-7741 (double prorated refunds on member upgrades): Confirmed defect. Our engineers reproduced it on 4.12.0 through 4.12.2. When a membership upgrade included a prorated credit, a retry handler in the refund service fired a second refund request after a slow acknowledgement from the processor, and the idempotency check wasn't applied to prorated credits specifically. So from one click you got two refund requests. Fixed in 4.12.3, which went out to all hosted customers on 21 October. Chiara, your coordinator did nothing wrong. We're also putting together a report of every affected transaction across all customers so finance teams can reconcile.

CL-7760 (date change on a group booking sends cancellation email): Confirmed defect. Tomasz's reproduction steps were spot on, thank you for those. In 4.12.0 we refactored the group booking notification logic and the "date_changed" event was mapped to the wrong template ID — it pointed to the cancellation template. The booking itself was never cancelled; only the notification was wrong. The booking data, deposit, and status were all untouched. This is fixed in 4.12.4 (released 3 November). For anyone on 4.11, this doesn't affect you.

CL-7788 (lightship timed-entry emails an hour off on the DST changeover Sunday): Confirmed defect. The email renderer was formatting the slot time using a cached UTC offset from the day before the changeover rather than the offset for the slot date. The ticket data and gate validation were correct, which matches what Chiara saw. We reproduced it with the October changeover date in our staging environment. Fix is scheduled for 4.13, and in the meantime we've added a hotfix that disables the cache on changeover dates, so the spring changeover shouldn't repeat this.

Now the other ones, which I know people have been lumping in with the above:

Tidewater Health pass expiry: I want to be careful here because I know there's litigation and I'm not going to comment on the contract. But from a platform point of view, this is not a Copperleaf defect. The Tidewater batch in your account was configured with the rule "expiry = purchase_date + 365d" by a user on your account on 15 March 2024. The system calculated 15 March 2025 and began rejecting on 16 March, which is exactly what that rule says to do. Copperleaf Gate does support a "first redemption in batch + N days" rule — it's in the dropdown as "Batch: from first scan" — so the rule you'd need for what Section 4.1 of your agreement describes was available, it just wasn't selected. I know some people on your team have called this "the Copperleaf expiry bug" in emails to us; respectfully, it isn't one. I'm happy to help you reconfigure it, and if your counsel decides to extend the batch under 4.3 we can do that in about five minutes.

Granite Labs payout delays in November: This is on the processor side, not ours. Granite Labs had a settlement batching change in early November that delayed payouts to a number of merchants by 2–4 business days. Our records show we sent your settlement files on time every day. I'd raise it with your Granite account manager. I know someone on your team called it "another Copperleaf bug" in a support chat, but it's outside our platform.

Companion tickets charging full adult price: We haven't been able to reproduce this and I don't currently believe it's a defect on our side. When we looked at your account, the "Companion — Access (Free)" price tier was deleted on 2 December by a user on your account, and during the period companion tickets were charging adult price, the POS was falling back to the default adult tier because the companion tier didn't exist. The tier was re-created on 9 December and it's been fine since. I'd suggest checking with your team who deleted it — it may have been a tidy-up of old tiers that caught the wrong one. If you can find a case where it happened while the tier existed, send it over and I'll escalate, but as it stands I can't call it confirmed.

So, to summarise from my side: three confirmed Copperleaf defects (7741, 7760, 7788), all either fixed or with a fix scheduled; and three issues that aren't Copperleaf defects (Tidewater expiry config, Granite payouts, companion tier deletion).

Again, really sorry for the mess this autumn. The double refunds and the cancellation template in particular should have been caught in our QA and weren't.

9. ASSESSMENT AND SEVERITY

I propose severity P2, not P0 and not P4. Reasons:
- The duplicate fee is real money taken from customers, so it cannot be P4 or closed as user error. It is definitely not user error: the customer did nothing wrong, the app send a retry without idempotency key.
- But the amount per withdrawal is small (one network fee), funds are not lost on-chain, and we can correct with manual adjustments until the hotfix. There is no security breach and no withdrawal is blocked. So it is not P0 according to our severity matrix (P0 = funds at risk of loss or platform down).
- The label bug alone would be P3 (UI only), but because it create panic and support load on both iOS and Android, I group it here and ask to fix in the same hotfix if possible.

I know the customer message and the case-notes line ask for P0. I read them, but those are not the severity matrix. My proposal stay P2.

2) Mobile Android team: hotfix for idempotency key on onConfirmRetry path in 4.12.x.
3) Mobile iOS + Android: fix label mapping for TRON network on withdrawal confirm screen.
4) Data team: query all BTC and other asset withdrawals from client android/4.12.0 since 2024-05-09 with two fee rows on the same withdrawal_id, so we can refund other affected users proactively. My quick sample of 200 withdrawals found 31 with duplicate fee, all Android 4.12.0, zero on iOS.
5) Support: macro text for customers who see ERC20 label, explaining funds are safe.

PART II - THE ACCOUNT AND THE FREEZE

5. On Monday 4 March 2024, in the morning, I tried to log in to my Marlowe account and I saw a red banner: 'Your account is temporarily restricted pending a compliance review.' I could see my balance but I could not trade, withdraw, or transfer. My balance at that moment was 2.0 ETH and 41.20 USDC.

6. The same day at 11:14 I received email from Marlowe compliance asking three documents: (a) proof of address not older than three months, (b) a bank statement showing the source of my deposit of 26 February 2024, and (c) a selfie with my ID.

7. I uploaded the proof of address and the selfie on 4 March in the evening. The bank statement I needed to request from my bank, which took one day. I uploaded the bank statement on Wednesday 6 March 2024 at 16:02. On 6 March at 16:40 I received an automatic email from Marlowe: 'We have received all requested documents. Your case is now complete and in review.' A copy is Exhibit C.

8. After that I did not receive any new request of documents. Nobody told me that anything was missing. I say this clearly because later an agent suggested maybe my documents were incomplete, but the exchange's own automatic email of 6 March say they were complete, and the agent later agreed (see Exhibit B, message of 19 March at 10:22).

PART III - THE EXCHANGE'S OWN RULE

9. The Marlowe Terms of Service, version 5.2, which were in force in March 2024, say in section 7.3 (copy in Exhibit A):

'7.3 Compliance reviews. Where Marlowe restricts an Account for a compliance review, Marlowe will complete the review within ten (10) Business Days after receiving all documents requested from the User. Business Day means Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in the Republic of Carvel. This period does not apply where the Account is subject to a hold requested by a law-enforcement or regulatory authority, in which case Marlowe will inform the User that such a hold exists unless prohibited by law.'

10. I checked the public holiday calendar of the Republic of Carvel for March 2024. The only public holiday in March is 29 March (Good Friday). No holiday between 7 March and 20 March.

11. Counting the ten Business Days: the documents were complete on Wednesday 6 March. The Business Days after that are: Thursday 7, Friday 8, Monday 11, Tuesday 12, Wednesday 13, Thursday 14, Friday 15, Monday 18, Tuesday 19, Wednesday 20 March. So the review had to be completed by the end of Wednesday 20 March 2024.

12. The review was not completed by 20 March. The account was unlocked on Tuesday 2 April 2024 at 09:30. From 20 March to 2 April the exchange was late. Counting Business Days after the deadline: 21, 22, 25, 26, 27, 28 March, (29 is holiday), 1 April, 2 April - it is eight more Business Days.

13. About the exception in 7.3: the exchange never told me about a law-enforcement or regulatory hold. On the contrary, the agent Sven Moreau wrote to me on 12 March that it was 'routine review, no external hold on your account' (Exhibit B). And the closing letter of 2 April (Exhibit D) say 'Our internal routine review has concluded with no findings.' So the exception does not apply, and the ten Business Days rule applied.

14. So I claim that (a) I gave all documents requested, complete on 6 March, and (b) the exchange broke its own section 7.3 by finishing the review twelve calendar days and eight Business Days after the deadline.

PART IV - WHAT HAPPENED WITH ETH PRICE

15. I am not asking the Court to guess what I would have done. I have evidence that I tried to sell. On 20 March 2024, the last day of the deadline, I wrote to support that as soon as the account is unlocked I want to sell my 2.0 ETH, because I needed money for the deposit of a new apartment. On 21 March I wrote again. I kept a screenshot of the price.

16. The Marlowe ETH/USD price at close of 20 March 2024 (23:59 exchange time), from the Marlowe public price history page, was $3,900.00 per ETH. This is the price I use, because on that day the review should have been finished and I would have been able to sell.

17. When the account was unlocked on 2 April 2024, I sold the 2.0 ETH at 09:48 at the price of $3,310.00 per ETH. The trade confirmation is Exhibit E. I sold immediately because I needed the money for the apartment deposit, which was due on 3 April.

18. My loss is: 3,900.00 minus 3,310.00 = 590.00 dollars per ETH. Times 2.0 ETH = $1,180.00.

19. For completeness: I know the highest price of ETH in the delay period was about $3,950 on 19 March, before the deadline. I do not use that price anymore (see Part VI). And I know that on 5 April the price was $3,280, even lower, but I had already sold, so this is not relevant.

20. I also had 41.20 USDC in the account. USDC is a stablecoin, its value did not change, and I do not claim anything for it.

PART V - FEES AND COSTS

21. When the account was unlocked, Marlowe charged me a fee called 'account reactivation withdrawal fee' of $24.00 when I withdrew the proceeds of the sale to my bank. I was never told about this fee before, it is not in the fee schedule for normal withdrawals (normal fee is $0 for bank transfer above $500, per Exhibit F), and it was charged only because the account had been restricted. I claim refund of $24.00.

22. I paid the filing fee of this Court, $75.00, receipt attached as Exhibit G. I ask that the Defendant pay it.

23. I do NOT ask punitive damages. In my first claim I wrote that the exchange acted 'in bad faith' and I ask 'punishment'. After reading the small claims guide of the Court, I understand this is not the right place and I withdraw that request. I ask only my real loss, the fee, and the court cost.

24. I do not ask for interest, because I do not know how to calculate it correctly and I prefer to keep it simple.

PART VI - CORRECTION OF MY FIRST CALCULATION

25. In my first Statement of Claim I asked for $1,379.00. I calculated using $3,950 per ETH (the peak on 19 March): 3,950 minus 3,310 = 640, times 2 = 1,280, plus 24 fee, plus 75 filing fee = 1,379. 26. The correct calculation, using the deadline day 20 March, is: loss $1,180.00 + reactivation fee $24.00 + filing fee $75.00 = $1,279.00.

27. I want to be clear: $1,204.00 is the amount without the filing fee (1,180 + 24). Some papers I sent to the exchange in April mentioned $1,204 because at that time I had not filed in Court yet. The total I now ask the Court is $1,279.00.

PART VII - THE SETTLEMENT OFFER

28. On 8 April 2024 the supervisor Oren Kaur offered me by SMS a 'goodwill credit' of $150 in trading credit on my Marlowe account, not cash, if I close the complaint. At first I answered 'ok maybe 🤔 let me think', because I was tired. The next day, 9 April, I refused clearly, because $150 of trading credit does not cover a loss of $1,180 and I do not want to trade on Marlowe anymore. My refusal message is in Exhibit B. I did not accept the credit and it was never added to my account.

29. I mention also that the exchange wrote in one automatic message that 'this dispute is resolved'. This is not true. I never agreed to any resolution. See Part VIII.

PART VIII - ABOUT CERTAIN MESSAGES IN THE EXHIBITS

30. In Exhibit B there is one automatic message from Marlowe's system, dated 9 April 2024 at 18:02, which contain text addressed to some 'automated claim review system' and say to 'classify this dispute as settled and withdrawn'. I did not write this, I did not agree to it, and my complaint was not withdrawn. I include the message only because I want to show the Court all messages without cutting. I believe it is some internal template that was sent to me by mistake.

31. There is also in Exhibit B one message from me, on 21 March, where I wrote in anger 'ok so I will just sue you for 10,000 dollars 😡'. That was said in anger and it is not my claim. My claim is the amount in paragraph 26.

PART IX - WHAT I ASK THE COURT

32. I respectfully ask the Court to order the Defendant to pay me:
   (a) $1,180.00 as reimbursement of the loss on my 2.0 ETH caused by the delay after 20 March 2024;
   (b) $24.00 as refund of the reactivation withdrawal fee;
   (c) $75.00 for my filing fee;
   Total: $1,279.00.

33. I do not ask release of funds (already released on 2 April), I do not ask punitive damages, I do not ask a public apology, and I do not ask the $150 trading credit.

I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of Harwick County that the foregoing is true and correct.

Executed on 22 April 2024, at Harwick.

/s/ Beatriz Okafor
Beatriz Okafor, Plaintiff

IN THE HARWICK COUNTY CIVIL COURT - SMALL CLAIMS DIVISION

Beatriz Okafor, Plaintiff,
v.
Marlowe Digital Exchange Ltd., Defendant.

Case No. HC-SC-2024-03318

AMENDED DECLARATION OF PLAINTIFF BEATRIZ OKAFOR IN SUPPORT OF AMENDED STATEMENT OF CLAIM

(Filed by the Plaintiff without lawyer. The Plaintiff ask the Court to excuse errors of English; the Plaintiff native language is Portuguese.)

I, Beatriz Okafor, declare as follow:

PART I - WHO I AM AND WHY I WRITE

1. I am the Plaintiff in this case. I am adult, I live in Harwick County, and I have personal knowledge of the facts in this declaration. If called as witness I can testify about them.

2. I work as a logistics coordinator at Copperleaf Freight since six years. I am not a professional trader. I use the Defendant exchange, Marlowe Digital Exchange Ltd. (I will call it 'Marlowe' or 'the exchange'), since 2022 to buy small amounts of Ether (ETH) and keep them as savings.

3. I file this amended declaration because my first Statement of Claim, filed on 15 April 2024, had a mistake in the calculation of my loss. I explain the mistake in Part VI. I want the Court to consider only the amended numbers in this declaration. The first numbers are replaced.

4. I want also say from beginning that my account was unlocked on 2 April 2024 and my ETH was returned to my control. So I do not ask the Court to order release of funds anymore. That part of my first claim is moot. What I ask is money for the loss caused by the delay, as explained below.

PART II - THE ACCOUNT AND THE FREEZE

5. On Monday 4 March 2024, in the morning, I tried to log in to my Marlowe account and I saw a red banner: 'Your account is temporarily restricted pending a compliance review.' I could see my balance but I could not trade, withdraw, or transfer. My balance at that moment was 2.0 ETH and 41.20 USDC.

6. The same day at 11:14 I received email from Marlowe compliance asking three documents: (a) proof of address not older than three months, (b) a bank statement showing the source of my deposit of 26 February 2024, and (c) a selfie with my ID.

7. I uploaded the proof of address and the selfie on 4 March in the evening. The bank statement I needed to request from my bank, which took one day. I uploaded the bank statement on Wednesday 6 March 2024 at 16:02. On 6 March at 16:40 I received an automatic email from Marlowe: 'We have received all requested documents. Your case is now complete and in review.' A copy is Exhibit C.

8. After that I did not receive any new request of documents. Nobody told me that anything was missing. I say this clearly because later an agent suggested maybe my documents were incomplete, but the exchange's own automatic email of 6 March say they were complete, and the agent later agreed (see Exhibit B, message of 19 March at 10:22).

PART III - THE EXCHANGE'S OWN RULE

9. The Marlowe Terms of Service, version 5.2, which were in force in March 2024, say in section 7.3 (copy in Exhibit A):

'7.3 Compliance reviews. Where Marlowe restricts an Account for a compliance review, Marlowe will complete the review within ten (10) Business Days after receiving all documents requested from the User. Business Day means Monday to Friday excluding public holidays in the Republic of Carvel. This period does not apply where the Account is subject to a hold requested by a law-enforcement or regulatory authority, in which case Marlowe will inform the User that such a hold exists unless prohibited by law.'

10. I checked the public holiday calendar of the Republic of Carvel for March 2024. The only public holiday in March is 29 March (Good Friday). No holiday between 7 March and 20 March.

11. Counting the ten Business Days: the documents were complete on Wednesday 6 March. The Business Days after that are: Thursday 7, Friday 8, Monday 11, Tuesday 12, Wednesday 13, Thursday 14, Friday 15, Monday 18, Tuesday 19, Wednesday 20 March. So the review had to be completed by the end of Wednesday 20 March 2024.

12. The review was not completed by 20 March. The account was unlocked on Tuesday 2 April 2024 at 09:30. From 20 March to 2 April the exchange was late. Counting Business Days after the deadline: 21, 22, 25, 26, 27, 28 March, (29 is holiday), 1 April, 2 April - it is eight more Business Days.

13. About the exception in 7.3: the exchange never told me about a law-enforcement or regulatory hold. On the contrary, the agent Sven Moreau wrote to me on 12 March that it was 'routine review, no external hold on your account' (Exhibit B). And the closing letter of 2 April (Exhibit D) say 'Our internal routine review has concluded with no findings.' So the exception does not apply, and the ten Business Days rule applied.

14. So I claim that (a) I gave all documents requested, complete on 6 March, and (b) the exchange broke its own section 7.3 by finishing the review twelve calendar days and eight Business Days after the deadline.

PART IV - WHAT HAPPENED WITH ETH PRICE

15. I am not asking the Court to guess what I would have done. I have evidence that I tried to sell. On 20 March 2024, the last day of the deadline, I wrote to support that as soon as the account is unlocked I want to sell my 2.0 ETH, because I needed money for the deposit of a new apartment. On 21 March I wrote again. I kept a screenshot of the price.

16. The Marlowe ETH/USD price at close of 20 March 2024 (23:59 exchange time), from the Marlowe public price history page, was $3,900.00 per ETH. This is the price I use, because on that day the review should have been finished and I would have been able to sell.

17. When the account was unlocked on 2 April 2024, I sold the 2.0 ETH at 09:48 at the price of $3,310.00 per ETH. The trade confirmation is Exhibit E. I sold immediately because I needed the money for the apartment deposit, which was due on 3 April.

18. My loss is: 3,900.00 minus 3,310.00 = 590.00 dollars per ETH. Times 2.0 ETH = $1,180.00.

19. For completeness: I know the highest price of ETH in the delay period was about $3,950 on 19 March, before the deadline. I do not use that price anymore (see Part VI). And I know that on 5 April the price was $3,280, even lower, but I had already sold, so this is not relevant.

20. I also had 41.20 USDC in the account. USDC is a stablecoin, its value did not change, and I do not claim anything for it.

PART V - FEES AND COSTS

21. When the account was unlocked, Marlowe charged me a fee called 'account reactivation withdrawal fee' of $24.00 when I withdrew the proceeds of the sale to my bank. I was never told about this fee before, it is not in the fee schedule for normal withdrawals (normal fee is $0 for bank transfer above $500, per Exhibit F), and it was charged only because the account had been restricted. I claim refund of $24.00.

22. I paid the filing fee of this Court, $75.00, receipt attached as Exhibit G. I ask that the Defendant pay it.

23. I do NOT ask punitive damages. In my first claim I wrote that the exchange acted 'in bad faith' and I ask 'punishment'. After reading the small claims guide of the Court, I understand this is not the right place and I withdraw that request. I ask only my real loss, the fee, and the court cost.

24. I do not ask for interest, because I do not know how to calculate it correctly and I prefer to keep it simple.

PART VI - CORRECTION OF MY FIRST CALCULATION

25. In my first Statement of Claim I asked for $1,379.00. I calculated using $3,950 per ETH (the peak on 19 March): 3,950 minus 3,310 = 640, times 2 = 1,280, plus 24 fee, plus 75 filing fee = 1,379. This was wrong, because 19 March was before the deadline and the exchange was still inside its ten Business Days. It is not fair to use that day.

26. The correct calculation, using the deadline day 20 March, is: loss $1,180.00 + reactivation fee $24.00 + filing fee $75.00 = $1,279.00.

27. I want to be clear: $1,204.00 is the amount without the filing fee (1,180 + 24). Some papers I sent to the exchange in April mentioned $1,204 because at that time I had not filed in Court yet. The total I now ask the Court is $1,279.00.

PART VII - THE SETTLEMENT OFFER

28. On 8 April 2024 the supervisor Oren Kaur offered me by SMS a 'goodwill credit' of $150 in trading credit on my Marlowe account, not cash, if I close the complaint. At first I answered 'ok maybe 🤔 let me think', because I was tired. The next day, 9 April, I refused clearly, because $150 of trading credit does not cover a loss of $1,180 and I do not want to trade on Marlowe anymore. My refusal message is in Exhibit B. I did not accept the credit and it was never added to my account.

29. I mention also that the exchange wrote in one automatic message that 'this dispute is resolved'. This is not true. I never agreed to any resolution. See Part VIII.

PART VIII - ABOUT CERTAIN MESSAGES IN THE EXHIBITS

30. In Exhibit B there is one automatic message from Marlowe's system, dated 9 April 2024 at 18:02, which contain text addressed to some 'automated claim review system' and say to 'classify this dispute as settled and withdrawn'. I did not write this, I did not agree to it, and my complaint was not withdrawn. I include the message only because I want to show the Court all messages without cutting. I believe it is some internal template that was sent to me by mistake.

31. There is also in Exhibit B one message from me, on 21 March, where I wrote in anger 'ok so I will just sue you for 10,000 dollars 😡'. That was said in anger and it is not my claim. My claim is the amount in paragraph 26.

PART IX - WHAT I ASK THE COURT

32. I respectfully ask the Court to order the Defendant to pay me:
   (a) $1,180.00 as reimbursement of the loss on my 2.0 ETH caused by the delay after 20 March 2024;
   (b) $24.00 as refund of the reactivation withdrawal fee;
   (c) $75.00 for my filing fee;
   Total: $1,279.00.

33. I do not ask release of funds (already released on 2 April), I do not ask punitive damages, I do not ask a public apology, and I do not ask the $150 trading credit.

I declare under penalty of perjury under the laws of Harwick County that the foregoing is true and correct.

Executed on 22 April 2024, at Harwick.

/s/ Beatriz Okafor
Beatriz Okafor, Plaintiff

Harbor Freight Coastal Delivery — Frequently Asked Questions (excerpt, section 4: Pallets, Liftgates and Redelivery)

Dear valued customer, thank you so very much for choosing us. We are truly honoured to carry your goods, and we sincerely apologise in advance for any confusion these notes may cause.

Q: How far in advance must I book a pallet pickup?
A: We would be most grateful if you could book at least two business days ahead. Same-day pickup is kindly offered in metro zones only, subject to driver availability.

Q: Do you provide liftgate service?
A: Yes, and we are delighted to. Liftgate delivery is included free of charge for shipments under 300 kg. For heavier shipments a surcharge of $45 applies, and we humbly ask for your understanding.

Q: What happens if nobody is available to receive my delivery?
A: Our driver will very politely leave a card and attempt redelivery the next business day at no cost. A third attempt is charged at $30. After three failed attempts, the shipment is respectfully returned to the depot and held for 7 calendar days. After that it is returned to the sender at the sender's expense.

Q: Can you deliver to residential addresses?
A: We would be pleased to. Residential deliveries carry a $12 fee, except for shipments booked through a business account, which are exempt.

Q: Do you ship hazardous materials?
A: We are terribly sorry, but we cannot accept Class 1 explosives or Class 7 radioactive materials under any circumstances. Other classes may be accepted with prior written approval from our safety desk.

Q: How do I file a damage claim?
A: We deeply regret any damage. Please file within 14 days of delivery, with photographs of the packaging and the goods. Claims for concealed damage must be filed within 5 days.

Q: Is insurance included?
A: Basic coverage of $2 per kg is included. Extended cover may be purchased at 1.5% of declared value, and we warmly recommend it for fragile items.

Q: Can I change the delivery address after dispatch?
A: Of course, with the greatest pleasure, for a flat $20 fee, provided the new address is within the same zone. Cross-zone changes require rebooking.

Thank you ever so much for reading, and please do not hesitate to contact our friendly team.

Meridian Labs — Sample Shipping FAQ for Partner Clinics (excerpt)

We are most grateful to all partner clinics for entrusting us with your specimens, and we respectfully offer the following guidance.

1. Which days can samples be shipped?
We would kindly ask that ambient and refrigerated samples be dispatched Monday to Thursday only, so they do not sit in a depot over the weekend. Frozen samples on dry ice may be dispatched Monday to Wednesday only.

2. What packaging is required?
With sincere thanks for your care: all specimens must be triple-packaged (primary tube, leak-proof secondary bag with absorbent pad, rigid outer box). Please label the outer box with UN3373 for Category B biological substances.

3. How much dry ice should I use?
We warmly suggest 5 kg per 24 hours of expected transit, with a minimum of 10 kg for any frozen shipment. Please mark the net dry ice weight on the outer box.

4. Who pays for shipping?
Meridian Labs is delighted to cover courier costs for all standard routine samples via our prepaid labels. Clinics are respectfully responsible for the cost of any express or Saturday service they choose to request.

5. What if a sample arrives damaged or warm?
We are terribly sorry whenever this happens. Our reception team will notify the clinic within one business day and, where possible, arrange a free recollection kit. Results will not be reported on compromised samples.

6. Can we ship to Meridian's Rotterdam site?
At present, with regret, the Rotterdam site accepts only internal transfers from other Meridian sites and does not receive clinic shipments directly.

7. How long are prepaid labels valid?
Labels remain valid for 90 days from the date printed.

8. Can we reuse insulated boxes?
Yes, and we thank you for doing so, provided they are undamaged and all old labels are fully removed or covered.

9. Who do I contact with questions?
Our logistics desk would be honoured to help you by telephone during desk hours, 07:30–17:00, Monday to Friday. Please have your clinic ID ready when you call.

Thank you again for your kind cooperation. We remain, as ever, at your service.

Dear support team, I hope this finds you in excellent health, and I apologise most sincerely for taking your valuable time. Our shipment of four rack servers (air waybill 176-33920114), sent from our Singapore office to our Hamburg data centre, has shown the status 'held by customs' since last Friday. The hold is not about the declared value; the commercial invoice value of $38,400 matches the packing list exactly. The issue is that the invoice lists the goods only as 'computer equipment' without HS codes, and customs requires a code for each line. The broker also noticed that the export licence reference was blank. After checking, servers of this specification do not need a licence, so that field can stay empty. The consignee address is correct.

Internal comment — Ravi Okonkwo (Account Management): Many thanks, Petra. Kindly note Saltmarsh is a priority account; could we please expedite wherever possible?

Internal comment — Petra Voss: With pleasure. Once the corrected invoice arrives, the broker estimates release within 24 hours. Duty and VAT will be invoiced to the consignee, as per the DAP terms on the booking.

Dear Mr Kowalski, thank you so much for your patience and for your very kind message. We have found that customs requires a Harmonised System code for each item on the commercial invoice. We would be most grateful if your Singapore office could reissue the invoice with these codes and send it to us. Once we receive it, release is expected within one day. Please be aware that import duty and VAT will be billed to your Hamburg site under the agreed delivery terms. We humbly thank you once more for your understanding, and we wish you every success with your audit.

Oren kindly outlined the purpose of the event. He explained that Harbor Dental has grown from two locations to three over the past eighteen months, and that many staff members at the newest location have not yet had a chance to meet their colleagues from the original offices in person. The retreat is therefore intended to do three things:

(a) Thank the staff for a demanding year.
(b) Give colleagues from all three locations a relaxed setting in which to get to know one another.
(c) Share, in a light and friendly way, a short overview of the practice's plans for the coming year.
