MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR OUTSOURCED LABORATORY TESTING
Agreement Reference: GL-MFC-2023-014

This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement") is entered into as of 1 February 2023 (the "Effective Date") by and between Granite Labs, a clinical diagnostic laboratory with its principal administrative office at 44 Quarry Row, Suite 300 (hereinafter "the Laboratory"), and Maplecrest Family Clinic, an outpatient primary care provider with its principal office at 910 Alder Avenue (hereinafter "the Clinic"). The Laboratory and the Clinic are each referred to herein as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties".

RECITALS

WHEREAS the Clinic provides primary care services to registered patients and requires, from time to time, the analysis of blood, urine and other specimens collected on its premises; and

WHEREAS the Laboratory holds the necessary accreditation to perform such analyses and wishes to provide those services to the Clinic under the terms set out below;

NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein, the Parties agree as follows.

SECTION 1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Specimen" means any biological sample collected by Clinic staff from a patient and submitted to the Laboratory for analysis, together with its accompanying requisition form.

1.2 "Requisition" means the standard test request form, in paper or electronic format, completed by an authorised Clinic practitioner and identifying the patient, the tests requested, the date and time of collection, and the ordering practitioner.

1.3 "Routine Test" means any test listed in Schedule A under the heading "Routine Panel".

1.4 "Urgent Test" means any test marked as urgent on the Requisition by the ordering practitioner and listed in Schedule A under the heading "Urgent Eligible".

1.5 "Turnaround Time" means the period between the Laboratory's documented receipt of a Specimen and the release of a validated result to the Clinic's results inbox.

1.6 "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday observed in the jurisdiction of the Clinic.

1.7 "Courier Service" means the scheduled transport of Specimens from the Clinic's collection room to the Laboratory's receiving department.

SECTION 2. SCOPE OF SERVICES

2.1 The Laboratory shall perform the tests listed in Schedule A on Specimens submitted by the Clinic in accordance with the Laboratory's published collection manual, as updated from time to time and notified to the Clinic in writing.

2.2 The Laboratory shall release results electronically to the Clinic's designated results inbox. Paper copies shall be provided only upon written request by the Clinic Practice Manager.

2.3 The Laboratory shall notify the ordering practitioner by telephone of any critical value, as defined in the Laboratory's critical value policy, within sixty (60) minutes of result validation.

2.4 The Clinic shall be responsible for correct patient identification, correct labelling of Specimens, and the completeness of each Requisition. Specimens that are unlabelled or mislabelled shall be rejected by the Laboratory and the Clinic shall be notified of the rejection by the end of the same Business Day.

SECTION 3. TURNAROUND TIMES

3.1 Routine Tests shall be reported within two (2) Business Days of receipt.

3.2 Urgent Tests shall be reported within four (4) hours of receipt where the Specimen is received between 08:00 and 16:00 on a Business Day.

3.3 Where the Laboratory anticipates that a Turnaround Time will not be met, it shall inform the Clinic Practice Manager in writing as soon as reasonably practicable, stating the cause and the expected revised reporting time.

SECTION 4. COURIER SERVICE

4.1 The Laboratory shall arrange a Courier Service collecting Specimens from the Clinic twice daily on Business Days, at approximately 11:30 and 16:30.

4.2 The cost of the scheduled Courier Service described in clause 4.1 shall be borne entirely by the Laboratory and shall not be invoiced to the Clinic.

4.3 Any additional, unscheduled collection requested by the Clinic shall be charged to the Clinic at the rate set out in Schedule B.

4.4 The Clinic shall store Specimens awaiting collection in accordance with the storage conditions specified in the collection manual. The Laboratory shall not be liable for the deterioration of Specimens stored incorrectly by the Clinic prior to collection.

SECTION 5. FEES AND PAYMENT

5.1 The Clinic shall pay the Laboratory the fees set out in Schedule B for each test performed.

5.2 The Laboratory shall invoice the Clinic monthly in arrears, itemising each test by date, patient reference number and test code.

5.3 Invoices shall be payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date. Disputed items shall be notified in writing within fifteen (15) days of the invoice date, and the undisputed balance shall be paid on time.

5.4 Fees shall remain fixed for the Initial Term unless amended in accordance with Section 11.

SECTION 6. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION

6.1 Each Party shall treat all patient information received under this Agreement as strictly confidential and shall process it only for the purposes of this Agreement.

6.2 The Laboratory shall retain Requisitions and results for the period required by applicable record-keeping regulations and shall destroy them securely thereafter.

6.3 Each Party shall notify the other within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware of any unauthorised access to patient information relating to this Agreement.

SECTION 7. QUALITY ASSURANCE

7.1 The Laboratory shall maintain its accreditation throughout the term of this Agreement and shall notify the Clinic immediately of any suspension, withdrawal or material change in accreditation status.

7.2 The Laboratory shall provide the Clinic, upon request and not more than once per calendar year, a summary of its external quality assessment results for the tests listed in Schedule A.

SECTION 8. TERM AND RENEWAL

8.1 This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and continue for an initial period of twenty-four (24) months (the "Initial Term").

8.2 Upon expiry of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall not renew automatically. Any continuation beyond the Initial Term shall require a written amendment signed by both Parties.

SECTION 9. TERMINATION

9.1 Either Party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving not less than ninety (90) days' written notice to the other Party.

9.2 Either Party may terminate this Agreement with immediate effect by written notice if the other Party commits a material breach which, if capable of remedy, is not remedied within thirty (30) days of written notice specifying the breach.

9.3 Upon termination, the Clinic shall pay for all tests performed up to the date of termination.

SECTION 10. LIABILITY

10.1 Neither Party shall be liable for indirect or consequential loss arising under this Agreement.

10.2 The Laboratory's aggregate liability in any contract year shall not exceed the total fees paid by the Clinic in the preceding twelve (12) months.

SECTION 11. AMENDMENTS

11.1 No variation of this Agreement shall be effective unless made in writing, referencing this Agreement, and signed by authorised representatives of both Parties.

SECTION 12. GOVERNING LAW

12.1 This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which the Clinic is located.

SCHEDULE A (summary)
Routine Panel: full blood count, basic metabolic panel, lipid profile, thyroid stimulating hormone, HbA1c, urinalysis.
Urgent Eligible: full blood count, basic metabolic panel, troponin, C-reactive protein.

SCHEDULE B (summary)
Fees per test as per attached price list dated 1 February 2023. Unscheduled courier collection: flat charge per collection as per price list.

Signed for Granite Labs: Viktor Okafor, Director of Client Services
Signed for Maplecrest Family Clinic: Practice Manager, on behalf of the partners

---

AMENDMENT No. 1
Dated 3 July 2023

The Parties agree to amend the Agreement as follows, with effect from 1 August 2023:

A1.1 Clause 4.1 is deleted and replaced with the following: "The Laboratory shall arrange a Courier Service collecting Specimens from the Clinic three times daily on Business Days, at approximately 10:00, 13:00 and 16:30."

A1.2 Vitamin D (25-hydroxy) and ferritin are added to the Routine Panel in Schedule A.

A1.3 All other terms of the Agreement remain unchanged and in full force.

Signed for both Parties by authorised representatives.

---

AMENDMENT No. 2
Dated 14 November 2024

The Parties agree to amend the Agreement as follows:

A2.1 Clause 8.1 is amended so that the Initial Term shall end on 31 January 2026 instead of 31 January 2025, thereby extending the term of the Agreement by twelve (12) months.

A2.2 Clause 5.4 is amended to read: "Fees shall remain fixed until 31 January 2025. From 1 February 2025 the fees set out in the revised price list attached to Amendment No. 2 shall apply for the remainder of the term."

A2.3 Clause 3.1 is amended to read: "Routine Tests shall be reported within one (1) Business Day of receipt, save for Vitamin D (25-hydroxy), which shall be reported within three (3) Business Days of receipt."

A2.4 Clause 4.2 is unchanged and the scheduled Courier Service remains at the Laboratory's cost.

A2.5 A new clause 2.5 is inserted: "The Laboratory shall provide the Clinic with a monthly report summarising the number of Specimens received, the number rejected, and the reasons for rejection."

A2.6 All other terms of the Agreement, as amended by Amendment No. 1, remain unchanged and in full force.

Signed for Granite Labs: Viktor Okafor, Director of Client Services
Signed for Maplecrest Family Clinic: Practice Manager, on behalf of the partners

END OF DOCUMENT

APPOINTMENT BOOKING, CANCELLATION AND NON-ATTENDANCE POLICY
Policy Number: ADM-07
Version: 4.2
Approved by: Operations Committee
Policy Owner: Leila Iyer, Head of Patient Administration
Date of Approval: 9 September 2024
Next Scheduled Review: September 2026

1. PURPOSE

1.1 This policy sets out the procedures by which patients of Riverbend Community Health Centre ("the Centre") may book, amend and cancel appointments, and the administrative consequences of failing to attend a booked appointment without adequate notice.

1.2 The policy aims to ensure fair access to limited clinical time, to reduce the number of wasted appointment slots, and to provide patients with clear, consistent information about their responsibilities and the Centre's obligations.

2. SCOPE

2.1 This policy applies to all registered patients of the Centre and to all appointment types offered by the Centre, including general practitioner consultations, practice nurse appointments, physiotherapy sessions, dietetic reviews and chronic disease clinics.

2.2 This policy does not apply to walk-in minor injury services, which operate on a first-come, first-served basis and are not pre-booked.

2.3 This policy applies to all administrative staff, reception staff and clinical staff involved in booking or managing appointments.

3. DEFINITIONS

3.1 "Appointment" means a pre-booked time slot allocated to a named patient with a named clinician or service.

3.2 "Adequate notice" means notice of cancellation received by the Centre not less than twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled start time of the appointment.

3.3 "Late cancellation" means a cancellation received less than twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled start time.

3.4 "Non-attendance" or "no-show" means a failure to attend a booked appointment where no cancellation has been received before the scheduled start time.

3.5 "Late arrival" means arrival more than fifteen (15) minutes after the scheduled start time of an appointment of thirty (30) minutes or less.

4. BOOKING APPOINTMENTS

4.1 Patients may book appointments by telephone during reception opening hours, in person at the reception desk, or through the Centre's online patient portal.

4.2 Appointments may not be booked by email. Emails requesting appointments will receive an automated reply directing the patient to one of the booking channels listed in clause 4.1.

4.3 Routine appointments may be booked up to six (6) weeks in advance. Same-day appointments are released at 08:00 each weekday and are allocated by telephone only.

4.4 Patients booking on behalf of another person must be recorded as an authorised representative on that person's record, unless the patient is a child under the age of sixteen and the caller is a parent or legal guardian.

4.5 At the time of booking, reception staff shall confirm the patient's name, date of birth, and current contact telephone number, and shall inform the patient of the date, time, location and clinician for the appointment.

5. APPOINTMENT REMINDERS

5.1 The Centre sends an automated text message reminder to the patient's registered mobile number forty-eight (48) hours before each appointment.

5.2 Reminders are a courtesy. Failure to receive a reminder, for whatever reason, does not excuse a patient from the obligations set out in this policy.

5.3 Patients who do not wish to receive text message reminders may opt out by informing reception in writing.

6. CANCELLING OR AMENDING APPOINTMENTS

6.1 Patients who are unable to attend an appointment are asked to cancel as early as possible so that the slot can be offered to another patient.

6.2 Cancellations are accepted through the following channels:
(a) by telephone to the reception line during opening hours;
(b) through the online patient portal, at any time;
(c) by replying "CANCEL" to the automated text message reminder;
(d) in person at the reception desk.

6.3 Cancellations are not accepted by email, by social media message, or by voicemail left outside opening hours. A patient who attempts to cancel by one of these means will be treated as not having cancelled.

6.4 When a cancellation is received, staff shall record the date and time of the cancellation and the channel used in the appointment record.

6.5 Amendments to the date or time of an appointment are treated as a cancellation of the original appointment followed by a new booking.

7. NON-ATTENDANCE AND LATE CANCELLATION

7.1 The Centre records every non-attendance and every late cancellation on the patient's record.

7.2 An administrative fee of twenty-five (25.00) currency units is applied for each non-attendance at a physiotherapy or dietetic appointment. No fee is applied for non-attendance at general practitioner or practice nurse appointments.

7.3 Late cancellation of a physiotherapy or dietetic appointment incurs an administrative fee of ten (10.00) currency units.

7.4 A patient who records three (3) non-attendances within any rolling twelve (12) month period will receive a written warning letter from the Head of Patient Administration.

7.5 A patient who records a further non-attendance within six (6) months of receiving a warning letter may be required to book appointments only on the same day, by telephone, for a period of up to three (3) months. This restriction does not apply to appointments for children under sixteen, antenatal care, or urgent clinical need as determined by a clinician.

8. EXEMPTIONS AND WAIVERS

8.1 The administrative fees described in section 7 shall be waived where the patient demonstrates that the non-attendance or late cancellation resulted from:
(a) an emergency hospital admission of the patient or a dependant;
(b) the death of an immediate family member;
(c) a documented failure of the Centre's own booking systems.

8.2 Adverse weather, transport delays and work commitments do not constitute grounds for a waiver.

8.3 Requests for a waiver must be made in writing to the Head of Patient Administration within fourteen (14) days of the missed appointment.

8.4 Decisions on waiver requests shall be communicated to the patient in writing within ten (10) working days of receipt of the request.

9. LATE ARRIVALS

9.1 A patient who arrives late may be asked to rebook if the clinician is unable to see them without delaying subsequent patients.

9.2 Where a late-arriving patient is asked to rebook, the appointment is recorded as a late arrival and not as a non-attendance. No fee is applied.

10. VULNERABLE PATIENTS

10.1 Before issuing a warning letter or applying a booking restriction, staff shall review the patient's record for any flag indicating vulnerability, including learning disability, severe mental illness, safeguarding concern, or registered carer status.

10.2 Where such a flag is present, the case shall be referred to the patient's usual clinician before any action is taken under clauses 7.4 or 7.5.

11. RESPONSIBILITIES

11.1 Reception staff are responsible for recording cancellations and non-attendances accurately and promptly.

11.2 The Head of Patient Administration is responsible for issuing warning letters, deciding waiver requests, and monitoring compliance with this policy.

11.3 The Operations Committee receives a quarterly report on non-attendance rates by service.

12. COMPLAINTS

12.1 Patients who are dissatisfied with a decision made under this policy may raise a complaint through the Centre's complaints procedure, policy ADM-02.

13. MONITORING AND REVIEW

13.1 This policy shall be reviewed every two years or earlier if required by changes in legislation, service delivery, or audit findings.

13.2 Revision history:
- Version 4.0 (March 2021): introduced portal cancellation.
- Version 4.1 (June 2023): introduced text message reply cancellation; removed fax.
- Version 4.2 (September 2024): revised administrative fee amounts; clarified vulnerable patient procedure.

Related documents: ADM-02 Complaints Procedure; ADM-05 Patient Registration; CLIN-11 Safeguarding Adults and Children.

For queries about this policy, contact the Patient Administration Office during opening hours.

3.2 "Adequate notice" means notice of cancellation received by the Centre not less than twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled start time of the appointment.

3.3 "Late cancellation" means a cancellation received less than twenty-four (24) hours before the scheduled start time.

3.4 "Non-attendance" or "no-show" means a failure to attend a booked appointment where no cancellation has been received before the scheduled start time.

3.5 "Late arrival" means arrival more than fifteen (15) minutes after the scheduled start time of an appointment of thirty (30) minutes or less.

4. BOOKING APPOINTMENTS

4.1 Patients may book appointments by telephone during reception opening hours, in person at the reception desk, or through the Centre's online patient portal.

4.2 Appointments may not be booked by email. Emails requesting appointments will receive an automated reply directing the patient to one of the booking channels listed in clause 4.1.

4.3 Routine appointments may be booked up to six (6) weeks in advance. Same-day appointments are released at 08:00 each weekday and are allocated by telephone only.

4.4 Patients booking on behalf of another person must be recorded as an authorised representative on that person's record, unless the patient is a child under the age of sixteen and the caller is a parent or legal guardian.

4.5 At the time of booking, reception staff shall confirm the patient's name, date of birth, and current contact telephone number, and shall inform the patient of the date, time, location and clinician for the appointment.

5. APPOINTMENT REMINDERS

5.1 The Centre sends an automated text message reminder to the patient's registered mobile number forty-eight (48) hours before each appointment.

5.2 Reminders are a courtesy. Failure to receive a reminder, for whatever reason, does not excuse a patient from the obligations set out in this policy.

5.3 Patients who do not wish to receive text message reminders may opt out by informing reception in writing.

6. CANCELLING OR AMENDING APPOINTMENTS

6.1 Patients who are unable to attend an appointment are asked to cancel as early as possible so that the slot can be offered to another patient.

6.2 Cancellations are accepted through the following channels:
(a) by telephone to the reception line during opening hours;
(b) through the online patient portal, at any time;
(c) by replying "CANCEL" to the automated text message reminder;
(d) in person at the reception desk.

6.3 Cancellations are not accepted by email, by social media message, or by voicemail left outside opening hours. A patient who attempts to cancel by one of these means will be treated as not having cancelled.

6.4 When a cancellation is received, staff shall record the date and time of the cancellation and the channel used in the appointment record.

6.5 Amendments to the date or time of an appointment are treated as a cancellation of the original appointment followed by a new booking.

7. NON-ATTENDANCE AND LATE CANCELLATION

7.1 The Centre records every non-attendance and every late cancellation on the patient's record.

7.2 An administrative fee of twenty-five (25.00) currency units is applied for each non-attendance at a physiotherapy or dietetic appointment. No fee is applied for non-attendance at general practitioner or practice nurse appointments.

7.3 Late cancellation of a physiotherapy or dietetic appointment incurs an administrative fee of ten (10.00) currency units.

7.4 A patient who records three (3) non-attendances within any rolling twelve (12) month period will receive a written warning letter from the Head of Patient Administration.

7.5 A patient who records a further non-attendance within six (6) months of receiving a warning letter may be required to book appointments only on the same day, by telephone, for a period of up to three (3) months. This restriction does not apply to appointments for children under sixteen, antenatal care, or urgent clinical need as determined by a clinician.

8. EXEMPTIONS AND WAIVERS

8.1 The administrative fees described in section 7 shall be waived where the patient demonstrates that the non-attendance or late cancellation resulted from:
(a) an emergency hospital admission of the patient or a dependant;
(b) the death of an immediate family member;
(c) a documented failure of the Centre's own booking systems.

8.2 Adverse weather, transport delays and work commitments do not constitute grounds for a waiver.

8.3 Requests for a waiver must be made in writing to the Head of Patient Administration within fourteen (14) days of the missed appointment.

8.4 Decisions on waiver requests shall be communicated to the patient in writing within ten (10) working days of receipt of the request.

9. LATE ARRIVALS

9.1 A patient who arrives late may be asked to rebook if the clinician is unable to see them without delaying subsequent patients.

9.2 Where a late-arriving patient is asked to rebook, the appointment is recorded as a late arrival and not as a non-attendance. No fee is applied.

10. VULNERABLE PATIENTS

10.1 Before issuing a warning letter or applying a booking restriction, staff shall review the patient's record for any flag indicating vulnerability, including learning disability, severe mental illness, safeguarding concern, or registered carer status.

10.2 Where such a flag is present, the case shall be referred to the patient's usual clinician before any action is taken under clauses 7.4 or 7.5.

11. RESPONSIBILITIES

11.1 Reception staff are responsible for recording cancellations and non-attendances accurately and promptly.

11.2 The Head of Patient Administration is responsible for issuing warning letters, deciding waiver requests, and monitoring compliance with this policy.

11.3 The Operations Committee receives a quarterly report on non-attendance rates by service.

12. COMPLAINTS

12.1 Patients who are dissatisfied with a decision made under this policy may raise a complaint through the Centre's complaints procedure, policy ADM-02.

13. MONITORING AND REVIEW

13.1 This policy shall be reviewed every two years or earlier if required by changes in legislation, service delivery, or audit findings.

13.2 Revision history:
- Version 4.0 (March 2021): introduced portal cancellation.
- Version 4.1 (June 2023): introduced text message reply cancellation; removed fax.
- Version 4.2 (September 2024): revised administrative fee amounts; clarified vulnerable patient procedure.

Related documents: ADM-02 Complaints Procedure; ADM-05 Patient Registration; CLIN-11 Safeguarding Adults and Children.

For queries about this policy, contact the Patient Administration Office during opening hours.

Effective: 1 February 2024
Owner: Dalia Bergstrom, Finance Controller
Supersedes: AP-001 Revision 6 and every sticky note on the monitor in the back office

A NOTE BEFORE YOU SCROLL PAST THIS

We know. Nobody reads policy pages. People skim for their own name, find it missing, and go back to emailing invoices to whichever finance person they last had lunch with. This is the seventh revision of this document, and we have been told the first six were "very thorough." That is the phrase people use for things they did not read. If you are a clinic manager, a practice owner, a regional operations lead, or anyone else who has ever said "just pay it, I'll sort the paperwork later," this page is for you. If you are a vendor who found this page, welcome. Please read Section 4 twice.

SECTION 1: PURPOSE

This policy describes how Copperleaf Dental Group receives, checks, approves, records and pays supplier invoices. It exists so that we pay the right supplier, the right amount, once, on time, and with enough documentation that an auditor does not have to ask us the same question three times. It also exists so that the finance team can take a lunch break without discovering on return that someone has wired a deposit to a laboratory that went out of business in 2019.

The goals, in no particular order of how often we fail at them:

1. Pay valid invoices by their due date under the terms in Section 6.
2. Never pay an invoice twice. Once is plenty.
3. Never pay for goods or services we did not order or did not receive.
4. Keep a clean record for tax, audit and the occasional suspicious practice owner.
5. Take early-payment discounts when they are actually worth taking, and only then.

SECTION 2: SCOPE

This policy applies to all Copperleaf Dental Group entities, including all eighteen clinics, the central sterilization facility in Morrow Park, the two orthodontic satellite offices, and the regional head office, which despite its name is mostly a conference room and a coffee machine with opinions.

It covers invoices for dental supplies, laboratory work, equipment purchases and leases, facilities maintenance, IT services, professional services, marketing, cleaning, courier and waste removal, and anything else that arrives with a number at the bottom and the word "due" somewhere near it.

It does not cover employee expense reimbursements (see Policy EX-003, which is somehow longer than this one), payroll, patient refunds (see Policy PR-010), or intercompany charges between Copperleaf entities (see the Group Accounting Manual, Chapter 9, which nobody has opened since it was printed).

SECTION 3: VENDOR ONBOARDING

Before any supplier can be paid, the supplier must exist in the vendor master file. "Exist" here means something more than "a clinic manager has their mobile number."

To be set up, a new vendor must provide:

- A completed Copperleaf Vendor Information Form.
- A W-9 (or the equivalent tax form for non-US suppliers).
- Bank details on company letterhead, signed, and confirmed by a call-back to a phone number we obtained independently. Not the number printed on the letterhead. Not the number in the email signature. A number we found ourselves, like adults.
- A certificate of insurance where the vendor will perform work on our premises.

Please note that the W-9 is an onboarding document. It is collected once when the vendor is set up and refreshed every three years. It is not part of the invoice matching process described in Section 5 and should not be stapled to every invoice. We have received, to date, four hundred and twelve stapled W-9s. We are keeping them as a monument.

Changes to vendor bank details follow the same call-back rule. Any email that says "we have changed banks, please update" is treated as fraudulent until proven otherwise. Last year one such email was written in impeccable English, had the correct logo, and came from a domain that differed from the real vendor's by one letter. It was very convincing. It was also a crime.

SECTION 4: HOW INVOICES REACH US

All supplier invoices must be sent to the central inbox, invoices@copperleaf-ap.example, as a PDF attachment, one invoice per PDF. Paper invoices mailed to clinics should be scanned and forwarded to the same inbox by the clinic within two business days of receipt.

Invoices must show:

- The Copperleaf entity being billed.
- A valid Copperleaf purchase order number for anything that required a PO (see Section 5).
- An invoice number that is unique for that vendor.
- Invoice date, due date or payment terms, and a clear total with tax shown separately.

Invoices sent to individual staff members, to the CEO's personal address, to the clinic's general enquiries inbox, or "left at reception with the lady with the nice glasses" are not considered received until they reach the central inbox. The payment clock under Section 6 starts from the date the invoice arrives in the central inbox, not from the date printed on it, and certainly not from the date the vendor says they "definitely sent it."

Vendors: we understand that you have a preferred contact at our clinics and that the preferred contact is lovely. The preferred contact cannot pay you. Only the central inbox can start that process.

SECTION 5: PURCHASE ORDERS AND THE THREE-WAY MATCH

Purchases of goods and services at or above $500 require a purchase order raised in the procurement system before the purchase is made. "Before" is doing a lot of work in that sentence. A PO raised after the invoice arrives is called an after-the-fact PO, and it is flagged in the monthly exception report with a little red icon that we are told makes people feel bad. Good.

For PO-backed invoices, Accounts Payable performs a three-way match before an invoice can be approved for payment. The three documents are:

1. The purchase order, showing what was ordered, the quantity, and the agreed price.
2. The receiving report, entered in the procurement system by the clinic or facility that took delivery, confirming what actually arrived and in what quantity.
3. The vendor invoice, showing what the vendor is charging us.

All three must agree within tolerance: quantity must match exactly, and unit price must be within 2% or $50 of the PO price, whichever is lower. If they do not match, the invoice goes on hold and the requester is notified.

Things that are NOT part of the three-way match, despite the enthusiasm with which people send them:

- Packing slips. A packing slip is a piece of paper the vendor put in the box. It is not a receiving report. You may photograph it if it gives you joy, and it can help you fill in the receiving report accurately, but AP does not require it and will not hold an invoice for lack of one.
- The vendor contract or master service agreement. Contracts matter; they set the prices that go on the PO. But once the PO exists, AP matches against the PO, not the contract. Please do not attach a forty-page MSA to a $612 invoice for gloves.
- The W-9. See Section 3. See the monument.
- A screenshot of a text message from the sales rep saying "it's fine, just pay it."

Invoices below $500 without a PO may be approved on a two-way basis (invoice plus confirmation of receipt from the requester), provided the vendor is in the vendor master file and the requester has budget authority. Splitting a $1,400 purchase into three invoices of $466.67 to stay under the PO threshold is not clever. It is visible. We have a report for it. The report has a name, and the name is yours.

SECTION 6: PAYMENT TERMS

Unless a different term has been agreed in writing and recorded in the vendor master file, Copperleaf's standard payment term is net 45 days from the date the invoice is received in the central inbox.

Some vendors have negotiated terms different from the standard. These are exceptions and they are recorded individually in the vendor master file. At the time of this revision, recorded exceptions include:

- Harbor Freight (maintenance tools and shop supplies for the sterilization facility): net 30, agreed in 2023 in exchange for volume pricing.
- Our primary dental laboratory partner: net 60, under the lab services agreement.
- Utilities and statutory payments: paid by the stated due date regardless of the standard term.

The existence of these exceptions does not change the standard term for everyone else. We say this because at least three clinic managers have told vendors that "Copperleaf pays in 30 days" after seeing the Harbor Freight arrangement mentioned in a meeting. Copperleaf pays in 45 days. Harbor Freight gets 30. You are not Harbor Freight. Neither is the vendor you are talking to.

Payment runs occur every Tuesday and Thursday. An invoice is paid in the last payment run on or before its due date, not earlier, unless Section 7 applies.

SECTION 7: EARLY-PAYMENT DISCOUNTS

We like free money. We are not fools about it.

Where a vendor offers a discount for early payment (for example "2/10 net 45," meaning 2% off if paid within 10 days), AP will take the discount only if both of the following are true:

(a) The discount is at least 1.5% of the invoice total; and
(b) The invoice has cleared matching and approval early enough to be paid inside the discount window.

If the discount is smaller than 1.5%, we do not take it; it is not worth the cash-flow cost and the manual handling. If the invoice is stuck on a matching hold because someone forgot to enter a receiving report, we do not take it either, and the lost discount appears in the monthly exception report next to the requester's name. We are not saying this to shame anyone. We are saying it to shame someone specific, who knows who they are.

In short: early-payment discounts are taken when they meet the threshold and the invoice is ready in time. They are not taken automatically, and they are not taken because a vendor underlines them in red.

SECTION 8: APPROVAL AUTHORITY

Once matched, invoices require approval according to the invoice total (including tax) as follows:

- Up to and including $2,500: the requesting clinic manager or department head.
- Above $2,500 and up to and including $25,000: the Finance Controller (currently Dalia Bergstrom), after the clinic manager or department head has confirmed the business need.
- Above $25,000: the Chief Financial Officer, after Finance Controller review.

Approvers may not approve invoices for purchases they personally requested above $2,500; such invoices move to the next level up. Approvers may not approve invoices from vendors in which they or a family member hold an interest. You would be surprised how often we need to write that sentence down. Actually, you would not.

Approval by email reply is accepted only from the approver's own Copperleaf mailbox. Approval forwarded by an assistant, pasted into a chat message, or "said out loud in the corridor" is not approval.

Delegation: an approver going on leave may delegate authority to someone at the same level or higher, in writing, for a defined period. Delegating to "whoever is around" is not a defined period or a defined person.

SECTION 9: DUPLICATE INVOICES

The system flags possible duplicates when the vendor, amount and invoice date match, or when the vendor and invoice number match. Flagged invoices are held until AP confirms they are genuinely separate. Vendors who resend the same invoice with "COPY" or "REMINDER" written across the top should know that we can read, and that the original is already in the queue.

If you notice that an invoice has been paid twice, tell AP immediately. Do not "just ask the vendor to take it off the next one." The vendor will agree with enormous warmth and then forget.

SECTION 10: DISPUTES AND HOLDS

If an invoice is incorrect, the requester or AP raises a dispute with the vendor within 10 business days of identifying the problem. The disputed portion is placed on hold; the undisputed portion may be paid on normal terms if the vendor agrees to a partial payment. The payment term for the disputed portion restarts on receipt of a corrected invoice or credit note.

SECTION 11: LATE FEES AND INTEREST

Copperleaf does not agree to late fees in vendor terms unless the CFO approves them in writing. Late fees that appear on invoices without such agreement are disputed under Section 10. Late fees caused by our own delay (for example, an invoice sitting in a clinic drawer for three weeks) are charged to the budget of the clinic responsible. The drawer does not have a budget. The clinic does.

SECTION 12: YEAR-END CUT-OFF

For the financial year end, all invoices for goods or services received on or before the last day of the year must reach the central inbox by the fifth business day of the new year, and all receiving reports must be entered by the same date. Goods received but not invoiced by then are accrued based on the PO and receiving report. The practice of "holding invoices until January so the budget looks better" is noticed every year, by the same people, who write the same email about it.

SECTION 13: QUESTIONS

Questions about this policy go to the AP team through the central inbox with "Policy question" in the subject line. Questions about why the policy exists go to the history section in Appendix A. Complaints about the tone of this policy go to the same inbox and will be read with the seriousness they deserve.

APPENDIX A: REVISION HISTORY (FOR REFERENCE ONLY; NOT CURRENT POLICY)

The following summarizes earlier revisions. It is included because people keep quoting them to us as though they were still in force. They are not. Please stop.

Revision 4 (2019): Standard payment term was net 60. Approval limits were: clinic managers up to $1,000; regional operations leads up to $10,000; CFO above $10,000. There was no Finance Controller role. There was also no three-way match; AP matched the invoice to the PO only, which is how we paid for the same autoclave twice.

Revision 5 (2021): Standard term moved to net 30 for a trial period of one year, after which it was abandoned because cash flow looked, in the CFO's words, "like a crime scene." Three-way match introduced.

Revision 6 (2022): Standard term set to net 45. Approval limits were: clinic managers and department heads up to $5,000; Finance Controller from $5,000.01 to $50,000; CFO above $50,000. Early-payment discounts were taken automatically regardless of size, which produced one memorable month in which we accelerated $180,000 of payments to save $412.

Revision 7 (2024, current): Approval limits lowered as set out in Section 8 following the internal audit recommendation. Early-payment discount threshold introduced (Section 7). Packing slip and W-9 clarifications added because apparently they were needed.

APPENDIX B: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Q: My clinic ordered $3,000 of composite materials. I'm the clinic manager. Can I approve the invoice?
A: No. Under Section 8, $3,000 is above $2,500, so it goes to the Finance Controller after you confirm the business need. Under Revision 6 you could have approved it yourself, which is exactly why Revision 6 is no longer in force.

Q: The vendor says Copperleaf pays in 30 days. Is that right?
A: Only if the vendor is Harbor Freight, or has its own recorded exception. Otherwise it is net 45. See Section 6. Also see Appendix A, where you will find the net 30 trial that we would all prefer to forget.

Q: The vendor offers 1% off if we pay within 10 days. Will AP take it?
A: No. 1% is below the 1.5% threshold in Section 7.

Q: I attached the packing slip, the W-9 and the MSA. Why is my invoice still on hold?
A: Because the receiving report is missing. The receiving report is the one we need. The others are souvenirs.

Q: I found an old laminated card in the supply room that says clinic managers can approve up to $5,000. Is it still valid?
A: It is valid as a coaster.

Q: A vendor emailed to say their bank details changed. They sounded really nice.
A: So do most fraudsters. Call-back procedure, Section 3.

APPENDIX C: EXAMPLE WORKED CASE

Order: Clinic 11 raises PO 11-4402 for 40 boxes of nitrile gloves at $14.50 per box, total $580.00.
Delivery: 40 boxes arrive; the clinic enters a receiving report for 40.
Invoice: The vendor invoices 40 boxes at $14.75 per box, total $590.00, terms 2/10 net 45.
Match: quantity matches; unit price differs by $0.25, which is 1.7% of $14.50 and $10 in total, within tolerance (2% or $50, whichever is lower). Match passes.
Approval: $590.00 is under $2,500; clinic manager approves.
Discount: 2% is at least 1.5%, and the invoice cleared on day 4, so AP pays on the next payment run inside the 10-day window and takes $11.80 off.
If the clinic had forgotten the receiving report until day 12, the discount would be lost and would appear on the exception report, and the clinic manager would receive a polite email that is less polite than it sounds.

End of document. Congratulations on reaching the end. You are in a small and distinguished group.

- A W-9 (or the equivalent tax form for non-US suppliers).

- The Copperleaf entity being billed.

- Harbor Freight (maintenance tools and shop supplies for the sterilization facility): net 30, agreed in 2023 in exchange for volume pricing.
- Our primary dental laboratory partner: net 60, under the lab services agreement.
- Utilities and statutory payments: paid by the stated due date regardless of the standard term.

(a) The discount is at least 1.5% of the invoice total; and
(b) The invoice has cleared matching and approval early enough to be paid inside the discount window.

The system flags possible duplicates when the vendor, amount and invoice date match, or when the vendor and invoice number match. Flagged invoices are held until AP confirms they are genuinely separate. Vendors who resend the same invoice with "COPY" or "REMINDER" written across the top should know that we can read, and that the original is already in the queue.

The disputed portion is placed on hold; the undisputed portion may be paid on normal terms if the vendor agrees to a partial payment. The disputed portion is placed on hold; the undisputed portion may be paid on normal terms if the vendor agrees to a partial payment. The payment term for the disputed portion restarts on receipt of a corrected invoice or credit note.

SECTION 11: LATE FEES AND INTEREST

Copperleaf does not agree to late fees in vendor terms unless the CFO approves them in writing. Late fees that appear on invoices without such agreement are disputed under Section 10. Late fees caused by our own delay (for example, an invoice sitting in a clinic drawer for three weeks) are charged to the budget of the clinic responsible. The drawer does not have a budget. The clinic does.

SECTION 12: YEAR-END CUT-OFF

For the financial year end, all invoices for goods or services received on or before the last day of the year must reach the central inbox by the fifth business day of the new year, and all receiving reports must be entered by the same date. Goods received but not invoiced by then are accrued based on the PO and receiving report. The practice of "holding invoices until January so the budget looks better" is noticed every year, by the same people, who write the same email about it.

SECTION 13: QUESTIONS

Questions about this policy go to the AP team through the central inbox with "Policy question" in the subject line. Questions about why the policy exists go to the history section in Appendix A. Complaints about the tone of this policy go to the same inbox and will be read with the seriousness they deserve.

APPENDIX A: REVISION HISTORY (FOR REFERENCE ONLY; NOT CURRENT POLICY)

The following summarizes earlier revisions. It is included because people keep quoting them to us as though they were still in force. They are not. Please stop.

Revision 4 (2019): Standard payment term was net 60. Approval limits were: clinic managers up to $1,000; regional operations leads up to $10,000; CFO above $10,000. There was no Finance Controller role. There was also no three-way match; AP matched the invoice to the PO only, which is how we paid for the same autoclave twice.

Revision 5 (2021): Standard term moved to net 30 for a trial period of one year, after which it was abandoned because cash flow looked, in the CFO's words, "like a crime scene." Three-way match introduced.

Revision 6 (2022): Standard term set to net 45. Approval limits were: clinic managers and department heads up to $5,000; Finance Controller from $5,000.01 to $50,000; CFO above $50,000. Early-payment discounts were taken automatically regardless of size, which produced one memorable month in which we accelerated $180,000 of payments to save $412.

Revision 7 (2024, current): Approval limits lowered as set out in Section 8 following the internal audit recommendation. Early-payment discount threshold introduced (Section 7). Packing slip and W-9 clarifications added because apparently they were needed.

APPENDIX B: FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS

Q: My clinic ordered $3,000 of composite materials. I'm the clinic manager. Can I approve the invoice?
A: No. Under Section 8, $3,000 is above $2,500, so it goes to the Finance Controller after you confirm the business need. Under Revision 6 you could have approved it yourself, which is exactly why Revision 6 is no longer in force.

Q: The vendor says Copperleaf pays in 30 days. Is that right?
A: Only if the vendor is Harbor Freight, or has its own recorded exception. Otherwise it is net 45. See Section 6. Also see Appendix A, where you will find the net 30 trial that we would all prefer to forget.

Q: The vendor offers 1% off if we pay within 10 days. Will AP take it?
A: No. 1% is below the 1.5% threshold in Section 7.

Q: I attached the packing slip, the W-9 and the MSA. Why is my invoice still on hold?
A: Because the receiving report is missing. The receiving report is the one we need. The others are souvenirs.

Q: I found an old laminated card in the supply room that says clinic managers can approve up to $5,000. Is it still valid?
A: It is valid as a coaster.

Q: A vendor emailed to say their bank details changed. They sounded really nice.
A: So do most fraudsters. Call-back procedure, Section 3.

APPENDIX C: EXAMPLE WORKED CASE

Order: Clinic 11 raises PO 11-4402 for 40 boxes of nitrile gloves at $14.50 per box, total $580.00.
Delivery: 40 boxes arrive; the clinic enters a receiving report for 40.
Invoice: The vendor invoices 40 boxes at $14.75 per box, total $590.00, terms 2/10 net 45.
Match: quantity matches; unit price differs by $0.25, which is 1.7% of $14.50 and $10 in total, within tolerance (2% or $50, whichever is lower). Match passes.
Approval: $590.00 is under $2,500; clinic manager approves.
Discount: 2% is at least 1.5%, and the invoice cleared on day 4, so AP pays on the next payment run inside the 10-day window and takes $11.80 off.
If the clinic had forgotten the receiving report until day 12, the discount would be lost and would appear on the exception report, and the clinic manager would receive a polite email that is less polite than it sounds.

End of document. Congratulations on reaching the end. You are in a small and distinguished group.

Uma, forwarding Sven's update since you asked who's "on hold" and I refuse to answer from memory; scroll down, it's riveting.

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Sven Fischer
To: Xiu Sorensen
Cc: Kwame Rahman
Date: Friday 8 March, 17:52
Subject: AP weekly status, week ending 8 March

Hi Xiu,

Here is the weekly accounts payable status for Quill Dental. I have tried to keep it short. I have failed, because the week was not short. It was, by my count, roughly nine weeks long, compressed into five days, most of them spent explaining to people that an invoice is not paid just because they looked at it with intent.

Headline numbers first, since I know you read those and then skip to the part where I complain.

SUMMARY

- Invoices received this week: 214 (last week: 187).
- Invoices processed and approved: 196.
- Invoices paid in the Tuesday and Thursday runs: 181, totalling $412,660.18.
- Invoices currently on hold: 23 (details below, with the vendors that actually matter called out by name).
- Open disputes: 6, of which three are worth your attention and three are worth nobody's attention, including the vendors'.
- Days payable outstanding: 41, down from 43. Nobody will thank us for this. I am thanking us now.

If you want the version where everything is fine, stop reading here. Everything is fine. Several things are also on fire. Both can be true.

1. LARKSPUR RENTALS: THE GREAT DOUBLE INVOICE

Larkspur Rentals, who supply the portable X-ray units and the compressor rentals at the three east-side clinics, sent us invoice LR-4471 on 26 February for $8,420.00, covering February rental of the compressors plus a "delivery and calibration surcharge." On 4 March they sent LR-4471A for the same amount, same period, same line items, with the word "REVISED" at the top. The only thing revised, as far as I can tell, is the letter A.

The duplicate check caught it on Tuesday morning before the payment run. Neither LR-4471 nor LR-4471A has been paid. I want to be very clear about that, because by Wednesday afternoon at least two clinic managers had told each other that "Larkspur got paid twice," and by Thursday one of them had told Larkspur's account rep, who emailed me in a mild panic offering to refund money we never sent. I thanked her for her generosity and explained that we cannot accept a refund of a payment that does not exist, as appealing as it sounds.

On top of the duplicate, we are disputing the full $8,420.00 on the original. The delivery and calibration surcharge of $1,900.00 is not on the PO; the rental agreement says calibration is included. And the compressor count on the invoice is six, while the receiving report and the PO both say four. Rather than try to pay a partial amount on an invoice that is wrong in two places, I have put the whole of LR-4471 on hold pending a corrected invoice, and I have rejected LR-4471A outright as a duplicate.

Status: Larkspur Rentals is on payment hold. Dispute value: $8,420.00. Corrected invoice requested Tuesday. Larkspur's rep says the corrected invoice will be with us "early next week," which I have translated into my calendar as "at some point."

2. TAMSIN OFFICE SUPPLY: THE PAPER MOUNTAIN

Tamsin Office Supply invoiced $11,900.00 on 20 February for the quarterly bulk order: paper, toner, patient intake clipboards, and approximately one million pens, of which I suspect half have already vanished into the pockets of patients.

This is the largest single invoice in our current queue that has been disputed, and I know that number will be the one people remember, so let me head it off: we are not disputing $11,900.00. We are disputing $3,150.00 of it, which is the toner line. They billed us for 90 toner cartridges; the receiving reports from the clinics add up to 45. The other $8,750.00 was matched and approved and paid in Tuesday's run, with Tamsin's written agreement to a partial payment.

The disputed $3,150.00 was on hold. It is not on hold any more. On Thursday, Tamsin sent a credit note for the 45 missing cartridges, reducing the toner line to $1,575.00, which I matched against the receiving reports, and I lifted the hold at 11:20 on Thursday. The remaining $1,575.00 will go in Tuesday's run. So Tamsin is off hold and the dispute is closed. I mention it here only because it will still show as "recently held" on the dashboard until the weekly refresh, and I would rather you heard it from me than from the dashboard, which has no sense of nuance.

3. BRIGHTWATER COURIER: THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY GOT PAID TWICE

Here is the one that deserves the gossip Larkspur has been getting.

Brightwater Courier, our specimen and lab-work courier, invoiced us $1,280.00 for February. That invoice was paid in the 27 February run. Brightwater then sent the same invoice again under a new invoice number, BWC-2024-0233 instead of BWC-2024-0219, with a different invoice date. Because the invoice number and the date were both different, our duplicate check, which looks for matching vendor plus matching number, or matching vendor plus amount plus date, did not flag it. It was approved by a clinic manager who, in fairness, had no reason to remember the first one, and it went out in the 5 March run.

So yes: we paid Brightwater $1,280.00 twice. The second payment went out on Tuesday 5 March. It has cleared. It is, in the technical accounting sense, gone.

I have raised a recovery with Brightwater and placed the vendor on payment hold so that no further Brightwater invoices go out until either the $1,280.00 comes back to us or we net it off against their March invoice. Their accounts person, who was pleasant, said they would "look into it," in the tone people use when they are already thinking about lunch. Dispute value: $1,280.00. I will chase on Monday.

I have also opened a ticket with IT to tighten the duplicate rule so it also flags vendor plus amount within a 30-day window regardless of invoice number. They have promised to "scope it." I await the scope with the patience of a saint and the mood of a tax auditor.

4. ORIEL SOFTWARE: A WARNING, NOT A HOLD

Oriel Software, who host the scheduling platform, sent their annual renewal invoice for $22,400.00. It matches the contract and the PO, and it is approved. It will be paid on its due date in April.

However, Oriel has now sent us three separate "friendly reminders" about this invoice, each with a 1.5% late fee helpfully pre-added, despite the invoice not being due until April and despite our contract with them explicitly excluding late fees. I have written to them explaining the concept of a due date. I have told their account manager that if they send one more invoice with an unauthorised late fee, I will put the account on hold until the billing team can demonstrate familiarity with a calendar.

To be clear: Oriel is not on hold. They have been warned. The warning was delivered with great restraint. You would have been proud. Or at least not embarrassed.

5. PELLHAM JANITORIAL: A PHONE CALL

Pellham Janitorial had one invoice this week, $2,340.00, matched and approved and paid on Thursday without drama. I spent forty minutes on hold with their billing office on Wednesday trying to get a W-9 refresh, which is due every three years and which they have now sent three times, each time with the previous year's address. The only hold involving Pellham this week was the one I was on, listening to a pan-flute rendition of a song I will not name because I do not want it back in my head. Pellham's account itself is clear and in good standing.

6. THE OTHER THREE DISPUTES

For completeness, the three disputes worth nobody's attention:

- Marrowgate Linens: $86.40, one missing box of patient bibs. Credit promised.
- Holloway Water Coolers: $44.00, a rental charged for a cooler we returned in January. Credit promised in January. Promised again in February. We may be here for some time.
- Fenwick Signage: $212.50, a sign spelled "Qiull Dental." They have agreed to reprint it. We have agreed not to put the misspelled one outside the Harrow Road clinic, although a small part of me wanted to.

None of these vendors is on hold; the amounts are small enough that we are paying the undisputed invoices normally and netting the credits off.

OPEN DISPUTES, SORTED BY DISPUTED AMOUNT

I know you like a table. Here is a table.

Vendor | Invoice total | Amount disputed | Status
Larkspur Rentals | $8,420.00 | $8,420.00 | On hold, corrected invoice requested
Tamsin Office Supply | $11,900.00 | $3,150.00 originally, now $0 | Credit note received, hold lifted Thu, closed
Brightwater Courier | $1,280.00 (paid twice) | $1,280.00 | Recovery raised, vendor on hold
Fenwick Signage | $212.50 | $212.50 | Reprint agreed
Marrowgate Linens | $86.40 | $86.40 | Credit promised
Holloway Water Coolers | $44.00 | $44.00 | Credit promised, allegedly

The other 21 invoices on hold are ordinary matching holds: missing receiving reports, mostly. I will spare you the list. The clinics involved have been emailed. Clinic 7 has been emailed twice. Clinic 7 knows what it did.

7. STAFFING

Now the part you will skim, so I have put it in plain words.

Volume is up. We received 214 invoices this week against a weekly average of 170 over the last quarter. Month end is in three weeks and quarter end with it. I have two AP clerks, one of whom, Lotte, is out for the last two weeks of March on long-planned leave that I approved in November, when I was younger and more optimistic.

You will remember that in December I asked for a second permanent clerk and the request was declined for budget reasons. I am not re-opening that. I accept that permanent headcount is not happening this year and I will stop mentioning it in meetings, mostly.

What I am asking for is narrower: I am formally requesting approval for one temporary AP clerk, through the agency we used last year, for four weeks starting 18 March, to cover Lotte's leave and quarter-end. Estimated cost is $6,800.00 based on last year's agency rate. I need an answer by Wednesday 13 March to get someone booked in time, because the agency needs three business days of notice and I would like the temp to arrive before the quarter does.

If the answer is no, the realistic consequence is that we miss the early-payment window on a handful of invoices and some of the matching holds sit longer than they should. I am not being dramatic. I am being arithmetic.

8. THINGS I AM NOT WORRIED ABOUT BUT YOU MIGHT HEAR ABOUT

- Someone in the east-side clinics has started a rumour that we have "stopped paying Larkspur forever." We have not. We have stopped paying one incorrect invoice and one duplicate until Larkspur sends a correct one. When they do, we will pay it. I have no personal grudge against Larkspur. I have a professional grudge against the letter A.
- The dashboard shows Tamsin in amber. See section 2. Tamsin is fine. The dashboard is not fine, but that is a different ticket.
- Oriel's account manager may call you directly to complain about my email. If they do, the answer is: our contract says no late fees, and we pay on the due date. If you would like to deliver that line in a warmer tone than I did, you are welcome to. It would not be difficult.
- Someone asked whether the Harrow Road clinic can stop using Brightwater and just "have the dentist drive the samples to the lab." I have referred this suggestion to the operations team, with a note expressing my hope that it is a joke.

9. NEXT WEEK

- Chase Brightwater for the $1,280.00 recovery on Monday; if no progress by Wednesday, net it against their March invoice.
- Receive and match the corrected Larkspur invoice, if it arrives, which it may.
- Pay the remaining $1,575.00 to Tamsin in Tuesday's run.
- Follow up with IT on the duplicate-rule change.
- Process quarter-end accrual templates for the clinics.
- Wait, with my usual serenity, for your answer on the temp clerk.

As always, if anything in here is unclear, please ask me before the dashboard answers for me.

Best,
Sven

Sven Fischer
Accounts Payable Lead, Quill Dental

----- End of forwarded message -----

P.S. from Kwame: Uma, the "paid twice" rumour you heard at lunch is about the wrong vendor. Sven explains it, at length.

question.instruction: Criterion 1: Larkspur paid twice

notes: Duplicate LR-4471A caught before payment run; neither paid. The actual double payment was Brightwater.

- Invoices paid in the Tuesday and Thursday runs: 181, totalling $412,660.18.
- Invoices currently on hold: 23 (details below, with the vendors that actually matter called out by name).
- Open disputes: 6, of which three are worth your attention and three are worth nobody's attention, including the vendors'.
- Days payable outstanding: 41, down from 43. Nobody will thank us for this. I am thanking us now.

If you want the version where everything is fine, stop reading here. Everything is fine. Several things are also on fire. Both can be true.

1. LARKSPUR RENTALS: THE GREAT DOUBLE INVOICE

Larkspur Rentals, who supply the portable X-ray units and the compressor rentals at the three east-side clinics, sent us invoice LR-4471 on 26 February for $8,420.00, covering February rental of the compressors plus a "delivery and calibration surcharge." On 4 March they sent LR-4471A for the same amount, same period, same line items, with the word "REVISED" at the top. The only thing revised, as far as I can tell, is the letter A.

The duplicate check caught it on Tuesday morning before the payment run. Neither LR-4471 nor LR-4471A has been paid. I want to be very clear about that, because by Wednesday afternoon at least two clinic managers had told each other that "Larkspur got paid twice," and by Thursday one of them had told Larkspur's account rep, who emailed me in a mild panic offering to refund money we never sent. I thanked her for her generosity and explained that we cannot accept a refund of a payment that does not exist, as appealing as it sounds.

On top of the duplicate, we are disputing the full $8,420.00 on the original. The delivery and calibration surcharge of $1,900.00 is not on the PO; the rental agreement says calibration is included. And the compressor count on the invoice is six, while the receiving report and the PO both say four. Rather than try to pay a partial amount on an invoice that is wrong in two places, I have put the whole of LR-4471 on hold pending a corrected invoice, and I have rejected LR-4471A outright as a duplicate.

Status: Larkspur Rentals is on payment hold. Dispute value: $8,420.00. Corrected invoice requested Tuesday. Larkspur's rep says the corrected invoice will be with us "early next week," which I have translated into my calendar as "at some point."

2. TAMSIN OFFICE SUPPLY: THE PAPER MOUNTAIN

Tamsin Office Supply invoiced $11,900.00 on 20 February for the quarterly bulk order: paper, toner, patient intake clipboards, and approximately one million pens, of which I suspect half have already vanished into the pockets of patients.

This is the largest single invoice in our current queue that has been disputed, and I know that number will be the one people remember, so let me head it off: we are not disputing $11,900.00. We are disputing $3,150.00 of it, which is the toner line. They billed us for 90 toner cartridges; the receiving reports from the clinics add up to 45. The other $8,750.00 was matched and approved and paid in Tuesday's run, with Tamsin's written agreement to a partial payment.

The disputed $3,150.00 was on hold. It is not on hold any more. On Thursday, Tamsin sent a credit note for the 45 missing cartridges, reducing the toner line to $1,575.00, which I matched against the receiving reports, and I lifted the hold at 11:20 on Thursday. The remaining $1,575.00 will go in Tuesday's run. So Tamsin is off hold and the dispute is closed. I mention it here only because it will still show as "recently held" on the dashboard until the weekly refresh, and I would rather you heard it from me than from the dashboard, which has no sense of nuance.

3. BRIGHTWATER COURIER: THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY GOT PAID TWICE

Here is the one that deserves the gossip Larkspur has been getting.

Brightwater Courier, our specimen and lab-work courier, invoiced us $1,280.00 for February. That invoice was paid in the 27 February run. Brightwater then sent the same invoice again under a new invoice number, BWC-2024-0233 instead of BWC-2024-0219, with a different invoice date. Because the invoice number and the date were both different, our duplicate check, which looks for matching vendor plus matching number, or matching vendor plus amount plus date, did not flag it. It was approved by a clinic manager who, in fairness, had no reason to remember the first one, and it went out in the 5 March run.

So yes: we paid Brightwater $1,280.00 twice. The second payment went out on Tuesday 5 March. It has cleared. It is, in the technical accounting sense, gone.

I have raised a recovery with Brightwater and placed the vendor on payment hold so that no further Brightwater invoices go out until either the $1,280.00 comes back to us or we net it off against their March invoice. Their accounts person, who was pleasant, said they would "look into it," in the tone people use when they are already thinking about lunch. Dispute value: $1,280.00. I will chase on Monday.

I have also opened a ticket with IT to tighten the duplicate rule so it also flags vendor plus amount within a 30-day window regardless of invoice number. They have promised to "scope it." I await the scope with the patience of a saint and the mood of a tax auditor.

4. ORIEL SOFTWARE: A WARNING, NOT A HOLD

Oriel Software, who host the scheduling platform, sent their annual renewal invoice for $22,400.00. It matches the contract and the PO, and it is approved. It will be paid on its due date in April.

However, Oriel has now sent us three separate "friendly reminders" about this invoice, each with a 1.5% late fee helpfully pre-added, despite the invoice not being due until April and despite our contract with them explicitly excluding late fees. I have written to them explaining the concept of a due date. I have told their account manager that if they send one more invoice with an unauthorised late fee, I will put the account on hold until the billing team can demonstrate familiarity with a calendar.

To be clear: Oriel is not on hold. They have been warned. The warning was delivered with great restraint. You would have been proud. Or at least not embarrassed.

5. PELLHAM JANITORIAL: A PHONE CALL

Pellham Janitorial had one invoice this week, $2,340.00, matched and approved and paid on Thursday without drama. I spent forty minutes on hold with their billing office on Wednesday trying to get a W-9 refresh, which is due every three years and which they have now sent three times, each time with the previous year's address. The only hold involving Pellham this week was the one I was on, listening to a pan-flute rendition of a song I will not name because I do not want it back in my head. Pellham's account itself is clear and in good standing.

6. THE OTHER THREE DISPUTES

For completeness, the three disputes worth nobody's attention:

- Marrowgate Linens: $86.40, one missing box of patient bibs. Credit promised.
- Holloway Water Coolers: $44.00, a rental charged for a cooler we returned in January. Credit promised in January. Promised again in February. We may be here for some time.
- Fenwick Signage: $212.50, a sign spelled "Qiull Dental." They have agreed to reprint it. We have agreed not to put the misspelled one outside the Harrow Road clinic, although a small part of me wanted to.

None of these vendors is on hold; the amounts are small enough that we are paying the undisputed invoices normally and netting the credits off.

OPEN DISPUTES, SORTED BY DISPUTED AMOUNT

I know you like a table. Here is a table.

Vendor | Invoice total | Amount disputed | Status
Larkspur Rentals | $8,420.00 | $8,420.00 | On hold, corrected invoice requested
Tamsin Office Supply | $11,900.00 | $3,150.00 originally, now $0 | Credit note received, hold lifted Thu, closed
Brightwater Courier | $1,280.00 (paid twice) | $1,280.00 | Recovery raised, vendor on hold
Fenwick Signage | $212.50 | $212.50 | Reprint agreed
Marrowgate Linens | $86.40 | $86.40 | Credit promised
Holloway Water Coolers | $44.00 | $44.00 | Credit promised, allegedly

The other 21 invoices on hold are ordinary matching holds: missing receiving reports, mostly. I will spare you the list. The clinics involved have been emailed. Clinic 7 has been emailed twice. Clinic 7 knows what it did.

7. STAFFING

Now the part you will skim, so I have put it in plain words.

Volume is up. We received 214 invoices this week against a weekly average of 170 over the last quarter. Month end is in three weeks and quarter end with it. I have two AP clerks, one of whom, Lotte, is out for the last two weeks of March on long-planned leave that I approved in November, when I was younger and more optimistic.

You will remember that in December I asked for a second permanent clerk and the request was declined for budget reasons. I am not re-opening that. I accept that permanent headcount is not happening this year and I will stop mentioning it in meetings, mostly.

What I am asking for is narrower: I am formally requesting approval for one temporary AP clerk, through the agency we used last year, for four weeks starting 18 March, to cover Lotte's leave and quarter-end. Estimated cost is $6,800.00 based on last year's agency rate. I need an answer by Wednesday 13 March to get someone booked in time, because the agency needs three business days of notice and I would like the temp to arrive before the quarter does.

If the answer is no, the realistic consequence is that we miss the early-payment window on a handful of invoices and some of the matching holds sit longer than they should. I am not being dramatic. I am being arithmetic.

8. THINGS I AM NOT WORRIED ABOUT BUT YOU MIGHT HEAR ABOUT

- Someone in the east-side clinics has started a rumour that we have "stopped paying Larkspur forever." We have not. We have stopped paying one incorrect invoice and one duplicate until Larkspur sends a correct one. When they do, we will pay it. I have no personal grudge against Larkspur. I have a professional grudge against the letter A.
- The dashboard shows Tamsin in amber. See section 2. Tamsin is fine. The dashboard is not fine, but that is a different ticket.
- Oriel's account manager may call you directly to complain about my email. If they do, the answer is: our contract says no late fees, and we pay on the due date. If you would like to deliver that line in a warmer tone than I did, you are welcome to. It would not be difficult.
- Someone asked whether the Harrow Road clinic can stop using Brightwater and just "have the dentist drive the samples to the lab." I have referred this suggestion to the operations team, with a note expressing my hope that it is a joke.

9. NEXT WEEK

- Chase Brightwater for the $1,280.00 recovery on Monday; if no progress by Wednesday, net it against their March invoice.
- Receive and match the corrected Larkspur invoice, if it arrives, which it may.
- Pay the remaining $1,575.00 to Tamsin in Tuesday's run.
- Follow up with IT on the duplicate-rule change.
- Process quarter-end accrual templates for the clinics.
- Wait, with my usual serenity, for your answer on the temp clerk.

As always, if anything in here is unclear, please ask me before the dashboard answers for me.

Best,
Sven

Sven Fischer
Accounts Payable Lead, Quill Dental

----- End of forwarded message -----

P.S. from Kwame: Uma, the "paid twice" rumour you heard at lunch is about the wrong vendor. Sven explains it, at length.

Ines,

My preliminary view is as follows.

Exclusion 4.11 excludes loss 'caused directly or indirectly by any malicious act involving the unauthorised access to, use of, or interference with any computer system, network or software'. SP-4 does not write this back. Accordingly, if it were established that an outside party deliberately interfered with the controller and that this interference caused the compressors to stop, I would expect us to decline the spoilage claim under Exclusion 4.11.

However, a firewall label is not evidence of a malicious act. Automated systems frequently describe any burst of repeated connections as a denial of service event. The burden of establishing the exclusion rests with us, not with the insured. I would therefore recommend that you say nothing about the exclusion on site, that you obtain the insured's consent to a forensic examination of the controller, and that we instruct an independent firm. Harbor Analytics has done good work for us on industrial control systems before.

I would also suggest that we send a short reservation of rights letter once you have seen the site, so that the position is preserved while the investigation continues. I will prepare a draft. For clarity, a reservation of rights is not a declinature, and it should be framed so that the insured understands we are continuing to investigate in good faith.

Mateo

We completed our on-site imaging of the Frostline RC-900 refrigeration controller on Friday, 22 March 2024 and have now reviewed the controller event log, the configuration history, the building management system export and the firewall records.

Our preliminary observations are as follows. A full summary is to follow.

1. The mains interruption at 02:10 lasted fourteen minutes. The standby generator started within eleven seconds and carried the load throughout. The controller and compressors remained energised. Mains supply returned at 02:24 and the transfer back was clean.
2. The compressors continued to run normally and Cold Room 3 held temperature for more than an hour after mains supply was restored.
3. The repeated connection attempts flagged by the firewall originated from the controller manufacturer's published update distribution address, not from an unknown external source. They are consistent with the controller's own update client retrying a download after the brief network interruption caused by the power event.
4. At 03:31 the controller installed a scheduled firmware package, version 4.2.1. Following the installation, the setpoint table for Cold Room 3 contained null values in every field.
5. The controller interprets a null setpoint as a request to hold the circuit in defrost. From 03:32 the compressors for Cold Room 3 were held off by the controller, while the controller reported its own status as normal.
6. The same installation reset the alarm configuration to factory defaults, in which high-temperature alarms are disabled.

We have found no evidence of access by any unauthorised party. We will provide our full summary by the end of the week.

Kind regards,
Dmitri Haddad
